December 31, 1935. Morning Translation.

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:

THE RENT REDUCTION MOVEMENT

Sometime ago, the Executive Yuan called a
meeting at which officials of the Ministry of Finance,
the Ministry of Industry, the Shanghai City Government
and the Nanking City Government drew up a set of
regulations governing the solution of disputes over
house rent. The Shanghai City Government then asked
the local Tangpu and the City Government Council to
state their views on these regulations.
On December 18, the City Government Council
held a meeting to examine the regulations, at which
Wong Shiao Lai (汪曉籟), Doo Yuet Sun (杜月笙) and
others were present.
The request made by the Shanghai Citizens
Federation to the effect that the standard house rent
be fixed at 5 per cent of the combined value of the land
on which the house stands and the cost of the construction
of the house was approved. It was also decided that all
other charges are to be prohibited.

1935年12月31日。晨间译文。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

减租运动

前此，行政院召开了一次会议，财政部、实业部、上海市政府及南京市政府的官员在会上起草了一套关于解决房屋租金纠纷的规章。随后，上海市政府要求地方党部和市参议会就这些规章发表意见。
12月18日，市参议会召开会议审查该规章，汪曉籟（Wong Shiao Lai）、杜月笙（Doo Yuet Sun）等人出席了会议。
上海市民联合会提出的将标准房租定为房屋所占土地价值与房屋建筑成本总和的百分之五的请求获得批准。会议还决定禁止收取其他任何费用。

August 29, 1940
TAIRIKU SHIMPO

"SIX RUSSIANS OF VOLUNTEER CORPS OF FRENCH POLICE
DISAPPEAR WITH TWO MACHINE-GUNS."

Six White Russians attached to the
Volunteer Corps of the French Municipal Council disappeared
a few days ago.
On August 28, it was found that two of the
machine-guns owned by the Volunteer Corps were missing.
The Police, however, are keeping this matter secret, but
are making every effort to locate the men.

1940年8月29日
《大陆新报》

“法国警察志愿队六名俄国人携两挺机枪失踪。”

隶属于法国公董局志愿队的六名白俄人员于数日前失踪。
8月28日，发现志愿队拥有的两挺机枪不见踪影。
警方对此事保密，但正全力搜寻这些人。

(印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE File No. R.L.G. S.B.D. 7782 Special Branch 45 Date Nov. 4, 1935)

REPORT

Subject Meeting of the Federation of Rent Reduction Movement
Committees of Various Districts in Shanghai.

Made by D.P.S. Mackay Forwarded by (签名)

Between 3.15 p.m. and 4 p.m. on November 2,
fifty-four Chinese claiming to represent various sections
of the Federation of Rent Reduction Movement Committees of
Various Districts in Shanghai, 13 Station Road, Chapei,
held a meeting in the Ming Sung Middle School, 14 Nan Ling
Li (南林里), Singkiang Road, Chapei, Zung Chien-pu (鄭劍波)
presiding.

The primary discussion affected a rival
organization, the Rent Reduction Federation of All Tenants
in Shanghai, 173 Chun Ka Zah Road, Chapei, and the meeting
resolved to approach the local Kuomintang and the Bureau
of Social Affairs in regard to its activities. Apparently
this organization has attempted to compel local residents
to join their movement on payment of an entrance fee, and
has also distributed propaganda opposing the Federation
of Rent Reduction Movement Committees of Various Districts
in Shanghai.

Discussions were then held in regard to the
rent reduction movement, and it was decided that :-
1. In the event of landlords failing to grant reductions
in rent, all payments due to them be withheld and the money
banked deposited in a bank.
2. That the case of the sub-tenants of Shou Ping Li (寿品里),
Ward Road, be referred to the Eastern District Rent
Reduction Movement Committee of the Federation, 44 Feng
Yuan Li, Tongshan Road. These sub-tenants have
appealed to the Federation for assistance in opposing
their first tenants, who are attempting to eject them
as they have not paid their rents.

报告

主题 上海各区减租运动委员会联合会会议。

由 D.P.S. Mackay 撰写 由 (签名) 转呈

11月2日下午3时15分至4时之间，五十四名自称代表上海各区减租运动委员会联合会各分会的华人在闸北车站路13号开会，会议地点位于闸北辛江路南林里14号的明松中学，由鄭劍波（Zung Chien-pu）主持。

主要讨论涉及一个对立组织，即位于闸北春卡扎路173号的“上海全体租户减租联合会”，会议决定就其活动向当地国民党及社会局进行交涉。显然，该组织试图通过收取入门费强迫当地居民加入其运动，并且还散发了反对上海各区减租运动委员会联合会的宣传品。

随后就减租运动进行了讨论，并决定：
1. 如果房东拒绝减租，则扣留应付给他们的所有款项，并将钱存入银行。
2. 将华德路寿品里次承租人的案件提交给位于同山路丰元里44号的联合会东区减租运动委员会。这些次承租人已向联合会求助，以对抗试图将他们驱逐的一手承租人，原因是他们未缴纳租金。

Subject Rent Reduction movement (French Concession)

Made by D.P.S. Mackay Forwarded by [签名]

The Yung Yu Li (永裕里) (Rue Porte de l'Ouest) Rent
Reduction Section held a meeting at 2 p.m. November 3 at house
No.13 in the alleyway and passed the following resolutions :-
1) That the tenants of the alleyway be instructed to deposit
rents in the branch office of the Shanghai Commercial and
Savings Bank, 123 boulevard de montigny, pending a settlement
of the dispute with the landlord.
2) That a lawyer be engaged to deal with possible legal
proceedings by the landlord against the tenants.
3) That any tenant who pays rents to the landlord be regarded
as an enemy of the Section.
4) That the tenants be instructed to report to the Section any
coercive action taken by the landlord against them.
5) That the office of the Section be removed from No.13 Yung
Yu Li to No.65 in the same alleyway.
6) That a letter be addressed to the landlord requesting a
reduction in rents with effect from October, 1935.

The Heng Mow Li (恒茂里) Rent Reduction Section of
the 3rd District Branch of the 2nd Special District Rent
Reduction Movement Committee was removed on November 3 from 91
Heng Mow Li, boulevard de montigny to 81 Rue Marco Polo.

Date October 30, 1935.
Subject Rent Reduction movement (Chapei) - Activities of the "Federation
of Rent Reduction movement Committees of various Districts in Shanghai."
Made by D.P.S. Mackay Forwarded by [签名]

Twelve committee members of the "Federation of Rent
Reduction movement Committees of Various Districts in Shanghai"
held a meeting in their office, 13 Station Road, Chapei, between
4 p.m. and 5.30 p.m. October 29. Zung Chien-pu (鄭劍波 )
presided. The following resolutions were discussed and
passed :-
1) That the petition to be presented to the 6th Plenary Session
of the Kuomintang requesting the issue of a decree for a
general reduction in rents, which is being circulated among
local residents for signatures, be ready for despatch not
later than November 5.
2) That a meeting of representatives of various rent reduction
sections be convened at 2 p.m. November 3 in the Ming Sung
Middle School, Nan Ling Li, Sinkiang Road, Chapei, to discuss
measures to accelerate the movement.
3) That the monthly expenditure of the federation be limited to
$20.
4) That the request for assistance to obtain a reduction in
rents, made by the residents of Foh Ying Fang (福蔭坊 ),
Liaoyang Road, be referred to the Eastern District Rent
Reduction Movement Committee, 44 Vong Yuen Li, Tongshan Road.
5) That legal action be taken against Hu Chien-pah (胡健伯), a
committee member of the Paoshing Li (Paoshan Road, Chapei)
Rent Reduction Section and the "Rent Reduction Federation of
All Tenants in Shanghai," 173 Chun Kai Shek Road, Chapei,
who are alleged to have libelled the committee members of
of the Northern District Rent Reduction Branch of the
"Federation of Rent Reduction movement Committees of Various
Districts in Shanghai," 13 Station Road, Chapei.

（印：OFFICE OF COMMISSIONER OF POLICE 31 OCT. 1935）
（批：File 1 NOV 1935）

Subject The rent reduction movement and the tenants of
S. A. Hardoon & Co.
Made by D.P.S. Mackay. Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the attached cutting from the
"China Press" of October 15, I have to report that for some
time past the tenants of Hardoon & Co. along Nanking Road have
been agitating for a reduction in their rents. As no such
reduction was forthcoming, the tenants decided to suspend
payment of rent, and coercion by employees of the Company
failed to have any effect.

The Hardoon Company then selected the San Yih Silk
Store, 463 Nanking Road, as an example, and on September 20
applied to the Special District Court for attachment of the
property of the store. The following day the proprietor of
the store, to avert attachment of his property, appeared in
Court and deposited $2250, representing three months' rent on
his premises, with the Court. It is understood that the Court
paid over this sum to the landlords. Hardoon & Co. then
notified their tenants that all rents more than four months
in arrears should be paid by October 13, failing which legal
proceedings would be instituted.

None of the tenants, most of whom are three to six
months in arrears, have paid; no legal action has yet been
taken by Hardoon & Co., although it is understood that they
intend to do so within the course of the next few days.

事由：减租运动及哈同洋行（S. A. Hardoon & Co.）的租户
制作人：副巡官麦凯（D.P.S. Mackay）。转呈人 [签名]

关于附上的10月15日《字林西报》（China Press）剪报，兹报告如下：过去一段时间以来，南京路沿线哈同洋行的租户一直在鼓动降低租金。由于未能实现减租，租户决定停付租金，且洋行雇员采取的胁迫手段未产生任何效果。

随后，哈同洋行选取南京路463号的三益丝绸店（San Yih Silk Store）作为典型，于9月20日向特区地方法院申请查封该店财产。次日，该店店主为避免财产被查封，出庭并向法院存入2250美元，相当于其铺位三个月的租金。据悉，法院已将此款项支付给房东。哈同洋行随即通知其租户，所有拖欠超过四个月的租金须于10月13日前付清，否则将提起诉讼。

大多数租户已拖欠租金三至六个月，但均未付款；尽管据悉哈同洋行打算在未来几天内采取法律行动，但目前尚未对任何租户提起诉讼。

警探潘雷伯（Pan Lein-pih）和华籍侦探社第156号探员（C.D.S. 156）协助获取了构成本报告基础的信息。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 15, 1935
SPECIAL INQUIRY
Tenants Of
Hardoon Fail
To Pay Up
Renters On Nanking Rd.
Still Determined As
Deadline Passes
NO EFFORTS MADE
TO COMPROMISE
Boycott By Chinese
Shop-Keepers Is
Hinted
With yesterday set as the dead-
line by the S. A. Hardoon Com-
pany for the payment of rents in
arrears by tenants of Hardoon
shops and store spaces on Nan-
king Road, legal action of an
almost unprecedented nature in
Shanghai is expected to ensue dur-
ing the next few days. The tenants,
according to information obtained
by a CHINA PRESS reporter yester-
day, didn't pay up.
Officials of the Hardoon Company
could not be reached last night,
hence nothing definite could be
learned of their plans. When they
last discussed the matter, however,
they were emphatic in statements
that they would sue provided the
rents were not paid on the schedul-
ed time.
A committee member of the First
Special District Rent Reduction
Association, however, declared that
the attitude of the tenants on Nan-
king Road toward the Hardoon
concern remained just what it was
three and four weeks ago. No efforts
at compromise have been made, he
declared, adding that none will be
made until the landlord concern
decides to follow the lead of other
Shanghai landlords by reducing
rents.
He pointed out that in other
sections of the city, in the French
Concession, the Settlement and in
Chinese-controlled territory, land-
lords have reduced rents rather
than to see their properties un-
occupied. He expressed the belief
that the threat made by the Har-
doon Company to sue the proprietors
of firms refusing to pay their rents
on Nanking Road would hardly
work to an advantage for the
Hardoons.
He continued that in his opinion,
the local depression has made
such heavy inroads on business
that the average tenant cannot
afford to pay the old rates and
would be forced to close down if
 compelled to do so.
$1
For inquiry
and report please
M/S
15 OCT. 1935

《字林西报》，1935年10月15日，星期二
特别调查
哈同租户
未能缴清
南京路租客
在最后期限过后
仍态度坚决
未作妥协努力
暗示中国
店主进行抵制

随着哈同公司（S. A. Hardoon Company）将昨日定为南京路哈同商铺及店面租户支付拖欠租金的最后期限，预计未来几天内上海将出现几乎前所未有的法律诉讼。据《字林西报》记者昨日获得的消息，租户并未缴款。

昨晚未能联系到哈同公司的官员，因此无法确切了解其计划。然而，他们上次讨论此事时，曾 emphatically 声明，若租金未按预定时间支付，他们将提起诉讼。

不过，第一特区减租协会的一名委员宣称，南京路租户对哈同商号的态度与三四周前完全一样。他宣称，双方未作出任何妥协努力，并补充说，在房东商号决定效仿其他上海房东降低租金之前，不会作出任何努力。

他指出，在本市其他地区，包括法租界、公共租界以及华人管辖区域，房东们宁愿降低租金，也不愿看到房产空置。他认为，哈同公司威胁起诉南京路拒绝支付租金的公司业主，此举很难为哈同方带来有利结果。

他继续表示，在他看来，当地的经济萧条对商业造成了如此沉重的打击，以至于普通租户无力支付旧有的租金费率，如果被迫支付，将被迫停业。

THE NEW WORLD, WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER, 23, 1935.
11400

Hardoon & Co. Opens
Hostilities Against Tenants

The uncompromising attitude
the Hardoon & Co. took in the
protracted dispute with its ten-
ants in regard to rent reduction
came to a climax last Saturday
when three suits have been
filed with the. First Special Dis-
trict court to the amount of
Dol. 15,772 claimed to be rent
in arrears due from the Foo
Loo Zoo Confectioners, the Tuck
Lee Watch Company and the
San Yik Silk Store, all of Nan-
king Road. One of this concerns
is said to owe eight months
rent and the other two to three
months'. The hearing is sched-
uled to take place shortly.

All negotiations with the Har-
doon & Co. have failed as the
firm refused to lower the rents.
It is reported that this is a
trial baloon the firm not inten-
ding to take legal action against
other tenants preferring to wait
the judgment in these three
suits.
page_data.zh:
《新世界报》（THE NEW WORLD），1935年10月23日，星期三。
11400

哈同洋行对租户
开启敌对行动

哈同洋行在与租户就减租问题进行的长期争端中采取的不妥协态度，于上周六达到高潮，当时向第一特区地方法院提起了三起诉讼，索赔金额共计15,772美元，声称是福露祖糖果店（Foo Loo Zoo Confectioners）、德利钟表公司（Tuck Lee Watch Company）和三益丝绸店（San Yik Silk Store，均位于南京路）拖欠的租金。据说其中一家欠租八个月，另外两家欠租三个月。听证会定于近期举行。

与哈同洋行的所有谈判均已失败，因为该公司拒绝降低租金。据报道，这只是该公司的试探气球（trial baloon），其并不打算对其他租户采取法律行动，而是倾向于等待这三起诉讼的判决结果。

Subject Rent Reduction movement - the mei yuan (梅園) Restaurant and
the Zung Chow (神州) hotel.
Made by D.P.S. Mackay Forwarded by [Signature]

In September 1935, the Zung Chow (神州) hotel,
159 Chekiang Road, landlords, sued their tenant, the mei yuan
(梅園) Restaurant, 621 - 623, roochow Road, in the Special
District Court for five months' arrears of rent. On October
26 the Court ordered the landlords to reduce the rent by 20%,
retroactive from April 1, 1935, and the tenant was instructed
to pay off the arrears.

Some years ago this restaurant rented five shop
premises from the hotel at $928.00 per mensem. In October 1932,
the rent was increased by 20% and a contract was signed by
both parties that this rental of $1,113.60 per mensem should
remain in force for a period of ten years. In March this year
the tenant requested the landlord to reduce this sum by 50%
giving as his reasons the existing business depression. As
no reply was given by the landlords, the tenant withheld
payment of rent for the months of April, May, June, July and
August.

The above information was obtained by C.D.S. 94.

Subject.........The Rent Reduction Federation of All Tenants in
Shanghai.

Made by....C.A....Tizon................Forwarded by. B. B. Somerset. 89

About 300 persons claiming to be promoters of the
Rent Reduction Federation of All Tenants in Shanghai whose
office is in the Chungshan Guild, No.173 Chun Ka Zah Road,
off Jukong Road, Chepei, held their first general meeting at the
above address between 2 p.m. and 3.30 p.m. October 21.
The meeting had originally been scheduled to take place
at the Kwangtung Theatre, North Szechuen Road.
Wu Tae Wan (吳子垣), a member of the Chungshan
Guild, who presided, in the course of a speech stated that
the rent reduction associations in Shanghai already in
existence had failed in their duty with the result that
the rent reduction movement has had no result. He declared
that the principal aim of the promoters in organizing the
Federation was to enable the people to secure relief from
their financial burdens.
The following resolutions were then passed :-
1. That the regulations of the Federation (37 in number)
be passed.
2. That the work of canvassing members for the Federation
be expanded.
3. That the Authorities and various circles be requested to
render assistance to the rent reduction movement.
Subsequently the following 21 persons were elected to serve
on a temporary Executive Committee of the Federation :-
Zia Fee (謝非), a graduate of the Shanghai
Law College, Wu Tae Wan (吳子垣), a member of the Chungshan
Guild, Tseng Seu Ngo (張守我), a lawyer, Wong Dung Kung
(王鈍根), a novel writer, Bang Zuen Loong (彭瑞龍),
Au Sz Ching (夏時清), Zee Chiu Zung (徐秋澄), Zung Tien (陳天),

Subject Activities of the Rent Reduction Committee of the
2nd Special District Citizens' Federation.

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Grubb

In the afternoon of September 18, Mr. A.H. Hetherly,
Land and Estate Agent, 50 Kiukiang Road, called at Police
Headquarters and reported that on September 17 a man named
Chang Dao-doong (常道同) had visited his office and
presented a letter from the 2nd Special District Rent
Reduction Movement Committee of the 2nd Special District
Citizens' Federation, the contents of which referred to
the question of reduction of rents for the Estate Agency's
houses in the French Concession. Chang, who was represented
in the letter as a secretary of the Rent Reduction Committee,
proposed to Mr. Hetherly that if he would agree to the payment
of $2 to the Committee for each house the agency represented
in the Concession, he would undertake the task of persuading
recalcitrant tenants to pay their rents without delay.

This proposition was rejected by Mr. Hatherly who
feels indignant regarding the methods of the Rent Reduction
Committee, and looks upon the matter as a form of black-

由 C.D.I. Grubb 撰写并转呈

9月18日下午，九江路50号房地产代理人 A.H. Hetherly 先生前往警察总局报案称，9月17日，一名名为 Chang Dao-doong（常道同）的男子造访其办公室，并提交了一封来自第二特区市民联合会第二特区减租运动委员会的信件，信中提及该房地产代理行在法租界所管房屋的减租问题。Chang 在信中被指称为减租委员会秘书，他向 Hetherly 先生提议，若后者同意就其在法租界代理的每一栋房屋向委员会支付2美元，他将负责劝说那些顽固的租户立即缴纳租金。

Hatherly 先生拒绝了这一提议，他对减租委员会的手段感到愤慨，并将此事视为一种勒索。他前往警察总局仅是为了将此事件通报给租界警方，因为他正向法国巡捕房交涉此案。

A meeting of representatives of various branches and
sections of the Northern District Rent Reduction Movement
Committee was held at 3 p.m. October 16 at 13, Station Road.
During the meeting it was decided to notify each branch and
section to draft a petition to be dispatched to the Govern-
ment requesting that a notification ordering a reduction in
rents be issued.

Under the auspices of the Nantao District Rent Reduction
Movement Committee, No.1 Tsə An Li, Loo Hsiang Yuan Road,
Nantao, representatives of various branches of the committee
held a meeting at 3 p.m. October 16 in the Young Men's
Lecturing Group Building, Small West Gate, Nantao, when the
following resolutions were discussed and passed :-

1) That the tenants of houses on Min Kuo Road, Chung Hwa
Road, Zao Ka Road, and Fang Pang Road, Nantao, be instructed
to withhold payment of rents from October 17.

2) That representatives be appointed to the appealing group
organized by the Federation of Rent Reduction Movement
Committees of Various Districts of Shanghai, 13 Station
Road, Chapei, for the purpose of submitting a petition
to the 6th Plenary Session of the C.E.C.of the Kuomintang,
requesting the issue of a decree ordering a reduction in
rents.

3) That the tenants in Chung Hwa Road, Min Kuo Road, Fang
Pang Road, and Zao Ka Road, Nantao, be instructed to form
rent reduction branches of the committee.

4) That any tenant who violates the resolutions of the meeting
be held responsible for any loss that may be sustained by
the committee.

Date August 24, 1935.

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Everest

On August 22, information was received that in
connection with the Rent Reduction Propaganda Week to be
conducted by the Rent Reduction Committee of the 1st Special
District between August 25 and 31, theatrical performances
were to be staged during the inauguration meeting to be
held in the hall of the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's
Association, 480, Thibet Road, on August 25, and that
handbills containing propaganda relating to the rent
reduction movement were to be thrown from aeroplanes flying
over the Settlement and handbills and posters distributed
and posted in various districts of the Settlement.

At 4.30 p.m. August 23, Mr. Li Ngan-kuei (酈鰲釡),
a member of the Standing Committee of the Rent Reduction
Movement Committee of the 1st Special District, was
interviewed by D.I. Everest and D.I. Sih Tse-liang in the
office of the Committee in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce,
North Soochow Road. It was explained to Mr. Li that it
would be advisable if his committee obtained the permission
of the Municipal Council before holding the theatrical
entertainment in the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association
on August 25, and that the proposal of the Committee to
distribute handbills and posters on the streets, did not
meet with the approval of the Municipal Police. Mr. Li
was also informed that although the Municipal Police had
no cause for complaint against the rent reduction movement,
the distribution of handbills either from aeroplanes or
by individuals was a movement which smacked of agitation
and was therefore deemed unadvisable. In reply Mr. Li
Ngan-kuei stated that he agreed with these views and promised

由 D.I. Everest 撰写并转呈

8月22日收到情报称，第一特区减租委员会将于8月25日至31日举行“减租宣传周”，为此，定于8月25日在西藏路480号宁波同乡会大厅举行的开幕会议上上演戏剧表演，并计划由飞越租界上空的飞机抛撒包含减租运动宣传内容的传单，同时在租界各区分发和张贴传单及海报。

8月23日下午4时30分，第一特区减租运动委员会常务委员 Li Ngan-kuei（酈鰲釡）先生在苏州河北路中国商会内的委员会办公室接受了 D.I. Everest 和 D.I. Sih Tse-liang（音译）的问询。向 Li 先生解释称，如果其委员会在8月25日于宁波同乡会举行戏剧娱乐活动前能获得工部局的许可，将是明智之举；此外，委员会在街道上分发传单和海报的计划未获工部局警务处批准。还告知 Li 先生，虽然工部局警务处对减租运动本身并无不满，但无论是通过飞机还是由个人分发传单，此类举动带有煽动性质，因此被认为是不妥的。作为回应，Li Ngan-kuei 先生表示同意这些观点，并承诺

REPORT

Subject Rent Reduction Movement - meeting of the Nantao District
Rent Reduction Movement Association.

Made by D.S. McKeown Forwarded by H. Grubb capt

Under the auspices of the Nantao District Rent Reduction
Movement Association, some forty representatives of tenants of
various alleyways held a meeting at 4.30 p.m. April 12, in the
office of the Association at No.3 Yung Ching Li, Ming Kuo Road,
Nantao. Sung Sing-fu (沈心撫) presided over the meeting.

The following resolutions were discussed and passed :-

1) That the tenants of the Ih An Li, Zung An Li, and Chi An Li,
Chiu Mow Dien, City, be notified that the Association will
not render any assistance should they refuse to accept the
10% reduction in rent proposed by the landlord.

2) That a letter of thanks be sent to Tu Yoeh-sung for having
accepted an invitation to become a director of the
Association.

3) That an Industry and Commerce Relief Committee be appointed
by the Association to co-operate with the China Industry and
Commerce Relief Co-operative Association in connection with
the division of the fund to be raised by the Ministry of
Finance to provide loans for factory owners and merchants.

4) That Sung Sing-fu and 14 others be elected to form the
above committee.

5) That factory owners and merchants in Nantao be notified to
register with the Association if they desire to obtain loans.
(The registration office of the Committee will be located
at Houses Nos.2 and 3 Yung Ching Li, Ming Kuo Road.)

6) That no fee be charged for the registration. The Committee
will commence registration at 1 p.m. April 13.

D. S.
D. C. (Special Branch).

Thirty-two committee members of the Shanghai
Municipality Rent Reduction Committee held a meeting in their
office, Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Soochow Road,
between 3.45 p.m. and 4.45 p.m. December 14 and passed the
following resolutions :-

instructed to cease publication of the "Special Periodical

RENT REDUCTION
MEASURES

Representatives Sent to
Nanking Conference

Three resolutions were passed at a
meeting of the Shanghai Rent Re-
duction Committee, held at 2 p.m. on
Friday. Some twenty persons were
present. The following were the
resolutions:—
1.—That representatives be detail-
ed to proceed to Nanking immediate-
ly to submit a petition to the Fifth
Plenary Conference of the Kuomin-
tang.
2.—That actors be engaged to prop-
agate the rent reduction movement
through radio broadcasting stations.
3.—That measures to accelerate the
movement be devised by Mr. Chang
Hsien-fang and others, such proposed
measures to be submitted for dis-
cussion at the next conference.
The representatives selected left
for Nanking by the 11 p.m. train on
Friday.

Special Issue) (上海減租特刊) (For the month of November
1934) contained articles with the following headings:-
1) Principles for a reduction in rent.
2) General Chiang Kai Shek's reply to the Rent Reduction
Movement Committee.
3) Notice of the Nantao District Rent Reduction Movement
Committee.
4) Warning.
5) Petition sent by the Rent Reduction Movement Committee
to the Administrative Yuan in Nanking and the Shanghai
City Government for drawing up immediately standard
measures for a reduction in rent.
6) Petition of the Nantao District Rent Reduction Movement
Committee to the Administrative Yuan in Nanking.
7) Suggestions made by Chiang Wu Tsung (姜和椿) of the
Chinese Bar Association to urge the Nanking Government
to stipulate standard measures for a reduction in rent.
8) Complaint sent by the Nantao District Rent Reduction
Movement Committee in connection with the lawsuit
between the landlord and tenants of Zoong Tuh Faung
Alleyway (常佳坊).
9) Letter to the Footung Branch Public Safety Bureau.
10) Reply from the Footung Branch Public Safety Bureau to
the Nantao District Rent Reduction Movement Committee.
11) Meeting of the Rent Reduction Movement Committee.
12) Letter of the Nantao District Rent Reduction Movement
Committee to a 'chief' tenant asking the latter not to
compel a sub-tenant to remove.
13) The errors of the Chinese people.
14) Unemployment and rent reduction.

1) 减租原则。
2) 蒋介石将军对减租运动委员会的答复。
3) 南市减租运动委员会通告。

The following slogans appeared on the same paper:-
1) To develop the native goods as far as possible, a
reduction in house rent must first materialize!
2) Shanghai will have no hope of prosperity unless house
rent is reduced!
3) A reduction in house rent will equalize the burden of
a chief tenant and a sub-tenant!
4) House rent must be reduced in order to revive the market
and stop lawsuits regarding rent in arrears!
5) To carry out the "principle of people's livelihood"
(one of the Three Principles of the People), house rent
must be reduced!
6) To reduce house rent means to observe the New Life
Movement!

GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK'S REPLY TO THE RENT REDUCTION
MOVEMENT COMMITTEE

The other day, the Rent Reduction Movement Committee
sent a petition to General Chiang Kai Shek, Chief of the
Military Affairs Commission of the National Government,
requesting him to instruct the Shanghai City Government
to promulgate measures governing a reduction in house rent
immediately.

The Committee received a reply from General Chiang
Kai Shek at Nanchang yesterday, stating that the Shanghai
City Government has already been instructed to act according
to the request of the Committee.

WARNING

Landlords are firmly refusing to reduce the rents
in an endeavour to bend the tenants to their will. Under
page_data.zh:
2.
同一刊物上出现了以下标语：-
1) 为尽可能发展国货，必须首先实现房租减免！
2) 除非减免房租，上海繁荣无望！
3) 减免房租将平衡二房东与转租户的负担！
4) 必须减免房租以振兴市场并停止关于欠租的诉讼！
5) 为实行“民生主义”（三民主义之一），必须减免房租！
6) 减免房租即是践行新生活运动！

蒋介石将军对减租运动委员会的答复

日前，减租运动委员会向国民政府军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军递交请愿书，请求他指令上海市政府立即颁布管理房租减免的措施。

委员会昨日收到蒋介石将军从南昌发来的复信，称已指令上海市政府按照委员会的请求行事。

警告

房东们坚决拒绝减租，试图迫使租户顺从其意愿。在

such conditions, they do not think of co-operating with
the tenants for better mutual existence. As a result,
it is now almost too late for the landlords to change
their minds, which if they do not do, will lead to
mutual ruin of both landlord and tenant.

REPORT

Subject (in full)...Report in connection with the Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by......D.S. MacLennan......Forwarded by...D. I. Wardrop

Sir,
At 2.40 p.m. 10-11-34 C.D.S. 80 attached to Kashing Road Station brought to this station two male Chinese named Wong Zau Dong (王位棠) and Zung Nyoh Zau (仲文善) both residing at No.1 An Ping Lee, Nanzing Road. These two men were in possession of a number of special supplements and receipt books in connection with the Rent Reduction Movement, also two badges and a certificate of identification in regard to same.

Enquiries showed that these supplements which are under the heading "Shanghai Gai Tso Da Kai" are printed in Nantao, and are authorized by the Municipality of Greater Shanghai, Shanghai Education Bureau and Public Safety Bureau, the head office being in Nantao whilst sub-offices are at North Honan Road Temple and at Foochow Road.

On communicating with the association Headquarters office in Nantao it was learned that these two men and others are employed by the said association in selling these supplements in Chinese Territory and the Settlement for 10 cents each copy, the purpose being to circulate the idea of the Rent Reduction Movement. The money collected is handed in to the association head office in Nantao and is used in connection with expenses incurred by same.

These two men, whilst selling the papers in the Settlement, called at the home of C.D.S. 80 and asked if he wished to purchase one, he accordingly brought them to the station, where, after enquiries were conducted, they were released and allowed to take their papers and receipt books with them.

Copy of supplement attached.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
D.M. MacLennan

事由（全称）……关于减租运动的报告。

呈报人……D.S. MacLennan……转呈人……D. I. Wardrop

先生，
1934年11月10日下午2时40分，配属嘉兴路捕房的华籍巡捕第80号将两名华籍男子带至本捕房，二人名为王位棠（Wong Zau Dong）和仲文善（Zung Nyoh Zau），均居住于南京路安平里1号。这两人持有若干与减租运动有关的特刊和收据簿，以及与此相关的两枚徽章和一张身份证明书。

经查，这些题为“上海各界大开”的特刊印刷于南市，由大上海市政府、上海市教育局和公安局授权，总办事处设在南市，分办事处设在河南北路庙宇及福州路。

经与南市该协会总部联系获悉，这两人及其他人员受雇于该协会，在华界和租界以每份一角的价格出售这些特刊，目的是宣传减租运动的理念。所收款项上交南市协会总部，用于支付该协会产生的费用。

这两人在租界售卖报纸时，曾到华籍巡捕第80号的住所，询问他是否愿意购买一份，他随即将他们带到捕房，经查询后，予以释放，并允许他们带走报纸和收据簿。

Date November 3, 1934. 11/3"

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction movement.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by H Grubb

Some 90 Chinese who claimed to be representatives
of various local rent reduction sections held a meeting
in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Soochow Road,
at 3 p.m. November 2, and passed the following resolutions:
1. That the Shanghai municipality Rent Reduction Committee
be asked to devise measures for an extensive demonstration
in connection with the rent reduction movement.
2. That the same Committee be entrusted with the task
of organizing appealing groups.
3. That representatives be assigned to call at the
Estate Owners' Association with a view to requesting
its members to voluntarily reduce the rent of houses
owned by them.

At the conclusion of the meeting at 4.30 p.m.
forty of the attendance led by Tsang Yien Faung (张连芳)
and Zung Chiu Feng (宗九峰) proceeded to the Estate
Owners' Association, 270 Peking Road, with a view to
carrying out the mission detailed in Resolution 3 above.
They, however, dispersed from the above address on finding
that no responsible persons were there.

The tenants of Ching Woo Faung, Canton Road,
have organized a rent reduction section. There are some
30 houses in this alleyway.

The tenants of houses on Lan Nyi Doo Road,
Pootung, have organized a rent reduction section with
an office at No.54 Zung Chi Road, Pootung.

Copy sent DC (Div)
R. W. Mac Adie.
D. S.
(Special Branch)

约90名自称是各地减租分会代表的华人于11月2日下午3时在苏州河北路的上海总商会举行会议，并通过以下决议：
1. 请上海市减租委员会制定措施，开展与减租运动有关的大规模示威活动。
2. 委托该委员会负责组织请愿团体。
3. 指派代表拜访业主联合会，要求其成员自愿降低其所拥有房屋的租金。

Date October 30, 1934.

REPORT

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D.S. Mac Adie Forwarded by H. Grubb A.S.

The rent reduction movement which started
in January, 1934, by local public bodies continues
throughout Shanghai under the rent reduction organiza-
tions in various districts. Although in many
cases reductions in rent have been made by the landlords
as a result of agitation carried out by the tenants,
the majority of the disputes are up to the present
still in abeyance. Attached is a list of alleyways
the tenants of which have been granted a reduction in
rent, as well as the scale of reduction in each case.
The local Kuomintang Headquarters has address-
ed a letter to the Shanghai City Government suggesting
the following measures in settling local rent disputes:-
1. That should the tenants and landlords concerned in
a dispute fail to reach a compromise among themselves,
the case is to be referred to the City Government
which will conduct mediation and decide the amount
of rent it deems proper. The rent decided by the
City Government, however, should not exceed the rentals
at present in force.
2. That a dispute may be re-discussed on appeal made
by the tenants or landlords concerned who are dis-
satisfied with the decision of the City Government,
but the final ruling cannot be appealed against and
must be complied with by both sides concerned.

R. W. Mac Adie
D. S.

D. C. (Special Branch)

报告

事由（全称）减租运动。

呈报人 D.S. Mac Adie 转呈人 H. Grubb A.S.

始于1934年1月由地方公共团体发起的减租运动，在各区的减租组织领导下继续在上海全境进行。虽然在许多情况下，由于租户进行的抗争，房东已降低租金，但迄今为止，大多数纠纷仍处于搁置状态。附件是一份弄堂列表，列出了其中租户已获得减租的情况，以及每种情况下的减租幅度。当地国民党党部致函上海市政府，建议采取以下措施解决本地租金纠纷：
1. 如果纠纷涉及的租户和房东无法自行达成妥协，案件应提交市政府，由市政府进行调解并决定其认为适当的租金数额。然而，市政府决定的租金不应超过目前现行的租金。
2. 如果租户或房东对市政府的决定不满意，可以提出上诉重新讨论纠纷，但最终裁决不得上诉，相关双方必须遵守。

R. W. Mac Adie
D. S.

D. C. （特务科）

Made by D.S.I. Moore Forwarded by

With reference to the attached communication
from Algar & Co. Ltd., regarding one Ging Yung Faung,
enquiries by C.D.S. 156 Zah Pao Ying have elicited that
this individual is a native of Ningpo, and claims to be
a member of the 4th District Kuomintang, and an acquaintance
of Chu Tseng (居正), Vice President of the Judicial Yuan.
Following his eviction on September 5, for
arrears in rent to the amount of $130.00, from No.164 Loong
Nee Li, Fenchow Road, where he resided and carried on a
business styled the Yung Shing (永興) Clothes Washing
and Dyeing Shop, Ging called a meeting of the tenants of the
Loong Nee Li (隆義里), Fenchow Road, the Loong Zung Li
(隆盛里), and Loong Shing Li (隆興里), Yulin Road, the
property of Algar & Co.. The meeting was held on Sept. 6,
in the Poo Shing Dong (普興堂), Yulin Road, some 25 persons
attending, when it was decided to demand a reduction in
rent as well as to render assistance to the evicted tenant
Ging Yung Faung. During the proceedings, the attendance
contributed $1.00 each to a fund for the establishment of
a Rent Reduction Section.
A further meeting was held in the morning of
September 13, in the Poo Shing Dong, Yulin Road, with
some 80 tenants of the alleyways in question attending,
when Ging and 16 others were elected the Committee of the
Rent Reduction Section.
Ging has solicited the Ningpo Guild, Thibet Road, for
assistance in the matter, but the result of his appeal is
not known.
He is in possession of two photographs of the

9月5日，岑因拖欠租金130.00美元，被从其所居住并经营名为“永兴”洗衣染坊的汾州路隆义里164号驱逐。随后，岑召集了阿尔加公司所属物业，即汾州路隆义里、玉林路隆盛里和隆兴里的租户开会。会议于9月6日在玉林路普兴堂举行，约有25人出席，会上决定要求减租，并向被驱逐的租户岑永芳提供援助。会议期间，出席者每人捐款1.00美元，作为成立减租分会的基金。
9月13日上午，在玉林路普兴堂举行了另一次会议，相关弄堂的约80名租户出席，会上选举岑及其他16人为减租分会委员会成员。

制作人 特别分部督察长 穆尔 转呈人 A. Grubb o/i

9月10日下午3时，当司法警察代表在嘉兴路警署市政警察的协助下，试图对狄思威路807弄（常乐里）27号房屋执行因拖欠租金而发出的扣押令时，遭到弄堂居民的干扰，居民向部分行动人员投掷粪便。
随后逮捕了六名女性和一名男性，女性后经警告释放。该名男性罪犯被控公然侮辱罪，将于9月11日出庭上海特区地方法院。
常乐里的物业由Brandt & Rodgers管理，该公司已就该弄堂某些租户拖欠8个月租金一事提起诉讼。

September 11, 1934. Morning Translation.

China Times, Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers

POLICE AND RESIDENTS IN ZANG LO LI ALLEYWAY (窄路里)

Members of the Zang Lo Li (Dixwell Rd) Unit of the Rent Reduction Movement Committee are protesting against the oppression of tenants of houses Nos. 40 and 27 by the landlord who has requested the Court to seal up the two houses and to order the occupants to remove.
House No. 40, which is occupied by Waung Ngoh Zien (汪鶴全), a native of Ningpo, was sealed up on September 6. On August 21, the Court ordered Chow Tieh Noon (周鐵農), occupant of house No. 27, to pay up the four of the eight months rent in arrears before August 30. Chow paid the rent for four months on August 29 in compliance with the Court's order and saved his house from being sealed up.
The Zang Lo Li Unit later called an urgent meeting and resolved to ask the Rent Reduction Movement Committee for assistance. The Committee sent a representative named Chang Yien Feung (張賢芳) to Brandt & Rodgers Ltd. (泰利公司), the representative of the landlord of the houses in Zang Lo Li, to mediate.
The management of Brandt & Rodgers, relying on the fact that it is a foreign firm, not only rejected the mediation, but filed an action in Court charging the tenants of Zang Lo Li with being criminals.
At 4 p.m. yesterday, over ten Chinese and foreign detectives and policemen of Kashing Road Police Station,- in three vans, proceeded to Zang Lo Li with workers and a large quantity of lumber to seal up the houses in the alleyway. The tenants obstructed the sealing up process. Somebody threw ordure at a Chinese policeman and trouble took place. Detectives and policemen assaulted the tenants with batons and drove them off. The following persons received injuries:-
An old woman named Waung (汪), native of Kwangtung, living in house No. 20 Zang Lo Li. (She was more seriously injured than the others.)
Waung Ngoh Zien living in house No. 40.
Wife of Hu Yung Shing (胡永興), a tailor, living in house No. 42.
Wife and sister-in-law of Ma Hu Kwei (馬胡貴) living in house No. 29.
Wong Yoeh Ying (王育英) and her mother, native of Ningpo, living in house No. 20.
Hu Lai Sung (胡來生), his brother Hu Chai Sung (胡再生), the wife and daughter of Ma Hu Kwei and Wong Yoeh Ying and her mother were taken to the Police Station where they were detained. Action will be taken when the Chinese policeman has been cleared of the ordure.
It is learned that in view of the arbitrary arrest and assault of innocent residents by the Police, which is contrary to law, the tenants of Zang Lo Li and the Rent Reduction Movement Committee held an urgent meeting at 7 p.m. yesterday at the Dah Sie Yang Restaurant (大西洋), Foochow Road, to discuss measures to deal with the situation.

《字林西报》、《新闻报》及其他本地报纸

窄路里（Zang Lo Li）的警察与居民

减租运动委员会窄路里（狄思威路）分部的成员正在抗议房东对40号和27号房屋租户的压迫，该房东已请求法院查封这两处房屋并命令居住者搬离。
由宁波人汪鶴全（Waung Ngoh Zien）居住的40号房屋已于9月6日被查封。8月21日，法院命令27号房屋的居住者周鐵農（Chow Tieh Noon）在8月30日前付清八个月欠租中的四个月租金。周于8月29日遵照法院命令支付了四个月租金，使其房屋免于被查封。
随后，窄路里分部召开紧急会议，决议请求减租运动委员会提供援助。委员会派遣一名名为張賢芳（Chang Yien Feung）的代表前往泰利公司（Brandt & Rodgers Ltd.），即窄路里房屋房东的代理方，进行调解。
泰利公司管理层倚仗其为外商洋行，不仅拒绝调解，还向法院提起诉讼，指控窄路里的租户为罪犯。
昨日下午4时，卡辛路（Kashing Road，音译）巡捕房的十余名中外探员和警员，分乘三辆卡车，携带工人和大量木材前往窄路里，意图查封巷内房屋。租户阻碍了查封过程。有人向一名华籍警员投掷粪便，引发骚乱。探员和警员用警棍殴打租户并将其驱散。以下人员受伤：
住在窄路里20号的广东籍老妇人汪氏（Waung）。（她的伤势比其他人更重。）
住在窄路里40号的汪鶴全（Waung Ngoh Zien）。
住在窄路里42号的裁缝胡永興（Hu Yung Shing）的妻子。
住在窄路里29号的馬胡貴（Ma Hu Kwei）的妻子和嫂嫂（或弟媳）。
住在窄路里20号的宁波籍人士王育英（Wong Yoeh Ying）及其母亲。
胡來生（Hu Lai Sung）、其弟胡再生（Hu Chai Sung）、馬胡貴（Ma Hu Kwei）的妻子和女儿、以及王育英（Wong Yoeh Ying）及其母亲被带往巡捕房拘留。待那名华籍警员身上的粪便被清除后，将采取进一步行动。
据悉，鉴于警方非法任意逮捕和袭击无辜居民，窄路里租户和减租运动委员会于昨晚7时在福州路的大西洋菜馆（Dah Sie Yang Restaurant）举行紧急会议，商讨应对局势的措施。

At 10.30 a.m. September 3, some 200 persons who
claimed to be representatives of various sub-offices
and sections of the Nantao District Rent Reduction Association,
2 Yung Ching Li, Min Kuo Road, Nantao, proceeded in four
motor trucks from Nantao to the New Civic Centre with a
view to appealing to the City Government for definite
measures in settling the rent dispute in Shanghai. They
were, however, stopped on Gi Mei Road, Chapei, by Police
of the Bureau of Public Safety who instructed them to
appoint delegates to call at the City Government instead
of proceeding there in a body. The order was complied
with, and 14 delegates, who subsequently called at the above
organ, were promised consideration of their request by the
Mayor. These petitioners returned to Nantao at 5.30 p.m.
and dispersed.

At 2 p.m. the same day, some 10 representatives of the
1st Special District (Settlement), 2nd Special District
(French Concession), Chapei District and Nantao District
Rent Reduction Associations called at the local Kuomintang
Headquarters and asked for permission to sell copies of a
periodical published by them bearing on the rent reduction
movement to residents as a means of raising funds for the
maintenance of these bodies. They were promised by a
staff employee of the organ that their request would be
referred to the Standing Committee of the Tangpu.

D. S.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

9月3日上午10时30分，约200名自称是南市减租协会各分部及分支代表的人士，从南市民国路永庆里2号出发，乘坐四辆卡车前往新市中心，旨在向市政府呼吁采取明确措施解决上海的租金纠纷。然而，他们在闸北吉美路（Gi Mei Road，音译）被公安局警员拦下，警员指示他们指派代表前往市政府，而不是集体前往。该命令得到遵守，随后有14名代表前往上述机构，市长承诺会考虑他们的请求。这些请愿者于下午5时30分返回南市并解散。

July 30, 34

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by H. Grubb. A. J.

Some 120 persons who claimed to be members of the
20th Sub-Office of the Settlement Rent Reduction Association,
Lane 614 No.11 Foochow Road to which tenants on Foochow Road
are affiliated, held a meeting in the Joong Shing Lur Restaurant,
435 Foochow Road, between 2 and 5 p.m. July 28. The following
decisions were passed:-
1. That commencing from July rentals be deposited in the
Shanghai Commercial and Savings Bank as a measure to
compel the landlords to come to an agreement for a
reduction in rent.
2. That the landlords be requested to exempt houses in the
thoroughfare from rent for two months as compensation
for losses sustained by residents as a result of the
local Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1932.
3. That the Shanghai Municipality Rent Reduction Committee
be requested to make arrangements for a general suspension
of business by shops as a step to extend the movement.
4. That the same Committee be asked to convene a mass meeting
of local residents to discuss the course of action to
be undertaken in connection with the movement.
During the proceedings copies of two pamphlets purporting to
emanate from the Sub-Office, one urging the landlords to
voluntarily reduce the rent and the other asking residents
to carry out the movement energetically, were distributed among
the attendance.
The landlords of the Yi An Faung (怡安坊), Rue Bourgeat
have agreed to reduce the rent of the houses in the alleyway by
10% with effect from June, 1934.

R. W. Mac Adie

Four of the 63 houses of the Republic Land Investment
Company situated in the Lee Zung Faung (隆诚坊), Broadway East,
on which distress warrants were served on June 5 and 6 for
non-payment of rent (Vide report dated June 7 on this subject)

carried out by representatives of the tenants, the landlord

when the following decisions were passed :-

the measures relating to rent reduction devised by the

(Chamber of Commerce building).

public its measures in connection with rent reduction.

2. “若要本地商业繁荣，必须减租”。

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D.S. Mac Adie Forwarded by A. Grubb D.I.

Soong Faung (宋芳), resident of house No.11
Kong Nying Li, Macao Road, recently received a letter from
a so-called "Investigation Group of the Rent Reduction
Association". The correspondence, apart from accusing him
of conducting secret negotiations with the landlords there-
by obtaining a special privilege of being exempt from pay-
ing the increase of $1 in water charges, threatens drastic
measures against him should he pay rent to the landlords while
other tenants of the alleyway are agitating for reduction in
rentals.

From enquiries made it was ascertained that the
person in question was one among other tenants of the alley
who led in an agitation against a decision of the landlords to
increase the water charges by $1 in November, 1933. Later he
went to visit his native place but on his return to Shanghai,
the above decision had been put into effect. Owing to dis-
agreement with other tenants he has refrained from taking part
in the rent reduction movement in the alley.

R. W. Mac Adie.
D. S.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

Date June 7, 1934.

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by A. Grubb A.J

On June 1, Wong Ching Sung (王金城), residing at
No.266/7 Macao Road, received a letter purporting to emanate
from the "Investigation Group of the City Rent Reduction
Committee" threatening that a bomb would be thrown into his
house on June 3 should he fail to have a rent reduction section
organized by that date. No action, however, was taken to
effect the above measure.

From enquiries made it was ascertained that the
person, Wong, was formerly a committee member of the Preparatory
Committee of the Joint Rent Reduction Section of Ng Foh Li
(五福里) (Lane 921), Tonquin Road, Ying Sih Li (印雪里) (Lane
929), Tonquin Road, Kong Wing Li (康寧里) (Lane 272), Macao
Road, and Tai Lai Faung (泰來坊) (Lane 335), Gordon Road,
with an office at No.4 Ying Sih Li, but had recently withdrawn
from membership of the body owing to discordance with other
committee members. The same person was also in receipt of
a letter of a similar strain on May 28 and the door of his
house was smeared with excrement on the night of May 30.

On June 5 and 6 distress warrants were served on the
tenants of 63 houses of the Lee Zung Faung (聯成坊) (Lane 1004)
Broadway East, by the Judicial Police at the instance of
the landlords for non-payment of rent for the last 5 months.

Three tenants were taken into custody by the
Municipal Police on June 5 for interfering with the Judicial
Police while executing the warrants and another 3 on June 6
for the same offence. They were, however, subsequently
released after having been cautioned against such an action.
These tenants have been agitating for a reduction of 20%
in rent.

6月1日，居住于澳门路266/7号的王金城（Wong Ching Sung，王金城）收到一封信，声称发自“全市减租委员会调查组”，威胁称若他未能在该日期前组织成立减租分会，将于6月3日向其住所投掷炸弹。然而，并未采取任何行动来实施上述威胁。

经查询查明，王某曾任通金路五福里（Ng Foh Li，五福里）（921弄）、通金路印雪里（Ying Sih Li，印雪里）（929弄）、澳门路康宁里（Kong Wing Li，康宁里）（272弄）以及戈登路泰来坊（Tai Lai Faung，泰來坊）（335弄）联合减租分会筹备委员会委员，办公地点位于印雪里4号，但近期因与其他委员不和而退出该组织。此人还于5月28日收到了一封类似内容的信件，且其家门在5月30日晚被人涂抹粪便。

6月5日和6日，应房东以过去5个月未付租金为由提出的请求，司法警察向东百老汇路联成坊（Lee Zung Faung，聯成坊）（1004弄）63户房屋的租户送达了扣押令。

6月5日，三名租户因在司法警察执行扣押令时进行干扰，被公共租界警务处逮捕；另有3人于6月6日因同一罪行被捕。然而，他们在受到不得此类行为的警告后随即获释。这些租户一直在煽动要求减租20%。

Rent Reduction Readjustment Committee called on Mo Zu Kung

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by H. Grubb A.S.

Some 90 persons who claimed to be representatives
of various rent reduction associations, branches and sections
held a meeting in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, north
Soochow Road on May 31. The following resolutions were
discussed and passed:-
1. That in demanding reduction in rent, tenants should
personally sign their names on the letter addressed to
the landlords to that effect.
2. That letters of the above nature be sent to the landlords
by chit-books.
3. That should the landlords ignore these letters, the
tenants should deposit their rent in the banks at the
present rate in the name of the landlords or the rent
collecting agents.

REPORT

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction movement.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by Whounean ASS

Twenty members of the Shanghai municipality
Rent Reduction movement Committee held a meeting in the
Chinese Chamber of Commerce, north Soochow Road, at 4 p.m.
May 26 and passed the following resolutions:

1. That a petition be sent to the Shanghai City
Government Provisional Council to repudiate the
excuse made by the local real estate owners in
opposing the rent reduction movement.

2. That a letter be sent to a newspaper in Tientsin
asking the editor to explain his publishing an
article alleging that the rent reduction movement
in Shanghai was collapsing.

3. That a general meeting of representatives of various
branches be held at 4 p.m. may 31.

The tenants of the houses of the Wai San
Li (山里) facing Broadway East have been notified by
the landlords that commencing from may 1, 1934, the
rent will be reduced from $139.86 to $120.00 per house
per mensem provided that rent in arrears prior to that date
is paid up. The tenants of the houses in the alley who
are not entitled to the reduction, however, are endeavouring
to induce the landlords to grant the same privilege to them.

In connection with the suit filed by the land-
lords against their failing to sign a new lease, some 25
tenants of the Si Zung Li (西成里), Rue Chapsal, held a meet-
ing in the office of their rent reduction section, no.189
Rue Chapsal, between 9 p.m. and 10 p.m. may 27 when they
were each drilled in a statement to be made before Court
on the hearing of the case.

上海市减租运动委员会的二十名成员于5月26日下午4时在北苏州路中国商会举行会议，并通过以下决议：

1. 向上海市政府临时理事会提交请愿书，驳斥本地房地产业主为反对减租运动所提出的借口。

2. 致函天津一家报纸，要求编辑解释其刊登声称上海减租运动正在瓦解的文章一事。

3. 于5月31日下午4时召开各分会代表全体会议。

面向东百老汇路的山里（Wai San Li，山里）房屋租户已接到房东通知，自1934年5月1日起，若付清该日期之前的欠租，每栋房屋每月租金将从139.86美元降至120.00美元。然而，该弄堂中无权享受减租优惠的租户正试图促使房东给予他们同样的待遇。

就房东因租户拒绝签署新租约而提起的诉讼而言，霞飞路（Rue Chapsal）西成里（Si Zung Li，西成里）的约25名租户于5月27日晚9时至10时在其减租分会办公室（霞飞路189号）举行会议，会上对每位租户进行了训练，以便在案件审理时在法庭上发表声明。

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement - meeting under the auspices
of the City Government Provisional Council.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by Whouncan DSS

Under the auspices of the City Government Council
some 20 persons who claimed to be representatives of the 1st
and 2nd Special District Citizens' Federations, Rent Reduction
Associations and other public bodies held a meeting in the
office of the above Council, 87 Kiaochow Road. Wong Yien
Soong (王逸松), a member of the Council, who presided,
addressed the attendance stating that the meeting was to be
confined to discussion of the following two points:-
a) Real motive of the movement.
b) Causes necessitating a reduction in rentals.
Speeches were then made by representatives attending
all advocating that unless house rents were reduced,
there was no hope of relieving the people from their
present distressing state and consequently no way of
restoring Shanghai to its former prosperous condition.
Eventually the chairman instructed each of the attendance
to compile a detailed report setting out the state of the
movement following the inauguration of the Rent Reduction
Associations. These reports should apart from explaining
the value of the existence of the latter organs, stipulate
measures to deal with the foreign estate owners.
The tenants of Chung Woo Li, (中和里) Ward Road
have formed a rent reduction section with an office at
1103-5 Ward Road.

R. W. Mac adie.

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D.S. Mac Adie Forwarded by W Ounean DSS

At 7 p.m. May 18, a number of tenants of the
Zang Kong Li, Kaifeng Road, proceeded to the Joint Rent
Reduction Section of the Zang Kong Li, Yue An Faung, Tuh
Shing Faung (Kaifeng Road), and Yah Shing Li (Alabaster Road)
at House No.341 of the 1st mentioned alleyway, where one
of their number smashed a frame containing a picture of the
late Dr. Sun Yat-sen. They alleged that the section was
inefficient and that its inauguration had caused the issue
of a notice by the landlords ordering the tenants of the
Zang Kong Li to vacate their premises in order that they
might be pulled down and rebuilt.

In connection with the above disturbance, 10
members of the 32nd Branch of the 1st Special District
Citizens' Federation held a meeting in their office, 245 Yah Shing
Li, Alabaster Road, and decided to instruct Wong Ah Pong (王阿胖),
the ringleader, to tender an apology to the section for
conducting illegal activities against the body. It was also
resolved to request the landlords of the Zang Kong Li to
postpone the demolition of the block fora further three years.

The Shanghai City Government Provisional Council,
87 Kiaochow Road, will convene a meeting of representatives
of local public bodies for May 25 in its office to discuss
the rent reduction movement in Shanghai.

It is reported that a compromise has been reached
between the tenants and the landlords of Sing Nyi Faung, Rue
Bourgeat, both agreeing the rentals of houses facing the
street be increased by 10% and those in the alley by 5%.
The landlords at first intended to increase the rent which

Subject (in full) Bei Teh Li Alleyway - Rent Reduction and Water Rate Dispute.

Made by D.S. Mac Adie Forwarded by W. Rounean D.S.I.

At 9.30 a.m. May 16 two representatives of the tenants
of the Bei Teh Li Alleyway, Tatung Road, together with their
legal advisor, called at the Sicawei Cathedral with a view
to obtaining a reply from the Father therein in regard to
the water dispute in the alley. There they were told that
the Church had decided to reduce the rent by $1 per house
per mensem which was the former charge for water rate and
that thereafter the tenants to pay their water charged to
the Shanghai Water Works Company direct.

alley held a meeting in house no.33 and decided to make further
appeal to the Shanghai Water Works Company on May 17 for
restoration of water supply pending a settlement of the
dispute.

Date May 14, 1934

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by Whaneau DSS

Nineteen members of the Shanghai Municipality
Rent Reduction Committee held a meeting in their office,
Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building, North Soochow Road,
between 2 p.m. and 3.45 p.m. May 13 and passed the follow-
ing resolutions:-

1. That the Dah Kung Pao in Tientsin be asked to reveal
the name of the writer of the article "The Collapse of
Rent Reduction Movement". (This article appeared on
the Sin Wan Pao Evening Edition of May 6. Subsequently
a letter asking for the name of the writer was addressed
by the Committee to the Newspaper (Vide previous report
on subject) which in a reply stated that the article
first appeared in the Dah Kung Pao in Tientsin and was
copied therefrom.)

2. That in rent disputes, residents be instructed to
deposit their rent in banks in the joint name of the
tenants and the sub-offices to which they are affiliated.

3. That the deposits be checked monthly by the Sub-offices.

4. That no money be collected from residents by the sections
or sub-offices unless with the approval of the Committee.

On May 13, some 20 boyscouts distributed on behalf
of the Nantao District Rent Reduction Association, 3 Yung
Ching Li, Min Kuo Road, Nantao, copies of a leaflet to
pedestrians on Chung Hwa Road, Nantao. The document
purporting to emanate from the Association apart from
announcing that the body is offering its service free
of charge to strive for a reduction in rent as a measure
to restore Shanghai to its former prosperous condition,
urges tenants in Nantao to register with the Association.

R. W. Mac Adie
D. S.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

5月13日下午2时至3时45分之间，上海市减租委员会的十九名成员在其位于北苏州路中国商会大楼的办公室举行会议，并通过以下决议：-

1. 要求天津《大公报》披露题为《减租运动之崩溃》一文的作者姓名。（该文刊登于5月6日的《新闻报》晚刊。随后，委员会致函该报询问作者姓名（参见此前关于此事的报告），该报回复称该文首发于天津《大公报》，系由此转载。）

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction movement.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by W. Lounean D.S.

In consequence of the tenants of Lanes 308
and 358, Chaoufoong Road, refusing to comply with the
agreement concluded between them and the landlords in
1933 that rentals be increased from $5.00 to $10.00
per mensem with effect from January, 1934, the latter
issued on May 5 a notice instructing the tenants to
vacate their premises before June 6, 1934. The
tenants announced that they would not pay the increased
rent at such a time when a general reduction in rent
was being urged by residents throughout Shanghai.
Since the election of the Executive and
Supervisory Committees of the Chapei District Rent
Reduction Association on April 29, opposition has
been raised by several rent reduction sub-offices
who consider that the election was not carried out
in a legal manner. Consequently the Association
instructed the 7th and 8th Sub-offices, the two ring-
leaders in the dispute, to suspend functioning alleging
that they had collected excessive membership fees from
the residents (Vide previous reports on subject).
The high handed measure only led to further opposition
from the majority of the sub-offices in Chapei, and
their threat to withdraw from membership obliged the
Association to close down on May 12 pending re-organization.
The dispute has been referred to the Shanghai municipality
Rent Reduction Committee.

R. W. Mac Adie
D. S.

自4月29日闸北区减租协会执行委员会和监察委员会选举以来，一些减租分办事处提出了反对意见，认为该选举未依法进行。因此，协会指令作为纠纷主要煽动者的第7和第8分办事处停止运作，理由是他们向居民收取了过高的会员费（参见此前关于此事的报告）。这种强硬措施仅导致闸北大多数分办事处的进一步反对，他们威胁要退出会员资格，迫使协会于5月12日关闭以待重组。该纠纷已提交至上海市减租委员会。

Made by D.S. Mac Adie Forwarded by W Ounean DS

Fourteen members of the Shanghai Rent Reduction
Movement Committee at a meeting held in their office, Chinese
Chamber of Commerce Building, North Soochow Road, between
3 p.m. and 5 p.m. May 9, passed the following resolutions :-
1. That local journalists be warned not to make untrue
reports on the rent reduction movement as well as to
refrain from altering reports supplied to them by the
Committee on pain of being dealt with by law.
2. That the Sin Wan Pao Evening Edition be requested to
reveal the name of the writer of the article "The Collapse
of the Rent Reduction Movement" which appeared in the
edition of May 6.
3. That a reward of $500.00 be given to any one who can
point out facts which certify that the Committee is
disheartened in its activities.
4. That a Scheme Planning Committee of 15 persons be organized.
In connection with resolution 2, the Committee
considers that the article in question had a great affect
on the progress of the rent reduction movement and is
endeavouring to trace the writer of the essay with a view to
compelling him to have a correction of the assertions contained
in the article inserted in the local press.
Some 100 tenants of the Pao Hwa Li, Singkeepang
Road, held a meeting in House 1269 and passed the following
decisions :-

consenting to postpone the demolition of the premises to
the end of June, 1934.

Made by...... D.S. Mac Adie ............Forwarded by... W. Kouman D.S.

On May 8 the Shanghai Water Works Company notified
the tenants of the Bei Tuh Li Alleyway, Tatung Road, to sign
contracts with the concern before May 10 for the installation
of water meters in their respective houses. Their ignoring
this notice, however, led to the disconnection of the water
supply to the alley at 11 a.m. this morning, May 10.
It will be recalled that the water supply to this
alley was cut off on April 24 and re-connected on May 5
(Vide previous reports on subject).
The tenants are of the opinion that their water
charges are included in the house rent, thus they are not
prepared to sign contracts for the installation of water
meters unless the landlords agree to reduce the rent by the
amount charged for water supply.
They will hold an urgent meeting this evening
either in House No.106 Bei Tuh Li or in the Ming Zee (民族)
Primary School, 106 North Chengtu Road, to discuss the dispute.

The Commissioner of Police
S.M.C. Shanghai

Sir,

I have to call your attention to trespass on
the property of the Mission at No 35. Tatung Road by Chinese
tenants in the vicinity. The water supply of these people
has been cut by the Shanghai waterworks Co. and for the
past three days they have been entering the Church ground
and building and helping themselves to a supply of water.
While we did not object to their doing so for
the first two days, it must be realised that unless some
remedy is found these people will carry on indefinitely.
I have therefore to request the good offices
of the Police in preventing further trespassing on the
Mission property both on the Church compound and on the
girls school compound, right to the east of the Church.

Yours sincerely.
Freudenberg

Subject (in full)......... Bei Tuh Li Alleyway - Rent Reduction and Water
Rate Dispute.

Made by...... D. S. Mac Adie ........Forwarded by W Duncan ASP

In compliance with the demand of the tenants
of the Bei Tuh Li Alleyway, Tatung Road, the Catholic
Church on the same thoroughfare supplied the former
water from two hoses for three hours from 7 a.m.
April 30 and will continue to do so this morning, May 1.
Between 8.30 p.m. and 10.30 p.m. April 30,
some 60 tenants held a meeting in house No.106 and
passed the following resolutions:-
1. That the Church be instructed to supply water without
interruption to the tenants.
2. That in view of straitened condition of the rent
reduction section of the alley, tenants be urged to contribute
voluntarily funds to the funds of the organ.
3. That posters bearing on the dispute be prepared for
exhibition on walls in the alley.
At the conclusion of the meeting, a total of $51.00
was raised from amongst the attendance.
On the morning of April 30, 7 delegates of the
tenants called at the Shanghai Water Works Co., Kiangse
Road, and requested that the water supply to the alley
in question be re-connected at the same time giving
an assurance that they would share the charges until
the dispute was settled. They were told to conduct
negotiations with the landlords instead of approaching
the Company.

R. W. Mac Adie.
D. S.

4月29日晚8时30分，该弄堂约60名租户在16号房屋再次举行会议，并通过以下决议：-
1. 组织六个请愿小组。
2. 第一组由女租户组成，向大同路的天主教堂要求供水，

Translation of a letter from 9th Branch Association of the

April 28th, 1934.

To Sinza Police Station,

We beg to inform you that we have
received verbal reports from the residents of Bei Tuh Li
off Tatung Road, that the residents of more than one hundred
houses in that alleyway suffered deep distress owing to the
water being illegally cut off by the landlord, with the result
that they have had no water supply for four days. Therefore
they requested us for assistance.

In consequence of the above we know
that the public life depends on water, which is necessary for
drinking. The landlord paid no attention to the public life
and stopped the water supply, in case of fire occurring, not
only the life of more than one thousand people in that alleyway
will be endangered but also the public in general, so that we
consider this a very important matter. For the purpose of
procuring public safety we inform you of the above circumstance
and request you to take the responsibility for protecting the
citizens in your district, then you will immediately notify the
Water Works to turn on the water supply for the public safety
and prevent the landlord from doing any unlawful action, pending
settlement. It is in the interests of public life and safety,
we write this letter to you and hope you will deal with this
matter with pleasure.

the 1st Special Area Dis-
trict Citizens' Federation
of the Municipality of
Greater Shanghai.

1934年4月28日。

致新闸捕房，

谨此告知，我方收到大同路培德里居民的口头报告，称该弄堂内一百多户居民因房东非法切断供水而遭受极大困苦，导致已断水四天。因此，他们请求我方提供援助。

鉴于上述情况，我方深知公众生活依赖饮水。房东无视公众生活需求而停止供水，一旦发生火灾，不仅该弄堂一千余人的生命将面临危险，广大公众亦将受累，故我方认为此事至关重要。为保障公共安全，特将上述情况通报贵方，并请贵方承担保护辖区内市民之责，随即通知自来水公司恢复供水以保公共安全，并在问题解决前阻止房东采取任何非法行动。出于公众生活与安全之利益，特致函贵方，望贵方乐意处理此事。

It is reported that the landlords of the Pao
Wha Li, Singkeepang Road, have agreed to postpone the
demolition of the block to the end of June. The
premises were to be pulled down at the end of March
(Vide previous report on subject), but owing to
opposition on the part of the tenants, the scheme
failed to materialize.

Some 40 persons who claimed to be representatives
of various alleyways in Kaifeng and Alabaster Roads held
a meeting in the office of the 32nd Sub-office of the
Settlement District Rent Reduction Association, 341
Kaifeng Road, between 7.30 p.m. and 9 p.m. April 26
and passed the following resolutions:-

1. That various alleyways in the area be instructed
to organize rent reduction sections without further
delay.

2. That tenants be requested to subscribe contributions
voluntarily for the maintenance of the Sub-Office.

3. That another meeting of representatives of tenants
be held on May 2.

The Jui Tuh Girls School, 33 Bei Tuh Li,
Tatung Road, which suspended studies on April 26 to avoid
possible disturbances which might be staged by the tenants
of the alleyway, resumed functioning this morning, April 27.

The 1st Sub-Office of the Chapei District Rent
Reduction Association was formally inaugurated on April 26 at
No.11 Zeu Woo Faung (瑞和坊), Paoshan Road, Chapei.

R. W. Mac Adie.

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement.

Made by D. S. Mac Adie Forwarded by Whounean DSJ

At 4 p.m. April 25, some 150 tenants of the
Bei Tuh Li Alleyway (培德里) with entrances on Tatung
and Sinza Roads gathered before the Jui Tuh Girls School
(求德女校), No.33 established by the Catholic Mission
in the same alley with a view to obtaining water from the
institution, the water supply to which, they alleged, had
been restored. Seeing the hostile attitude adopted by
the tenants who threatened to assault the principal and
teachers should they emerge from the school, the latter
kept the pupils, some 1,000 in number, on the premises
until about 5 p.m. when a party of police arrived on the
scene and succeeded in dispersing the crowd, the school
usually finishing at 4 p.m.

At 7 o'clock in the evening, some 30 tenants
held a meeting in the office of the rent reduction section
formed by them, House No.51 and passed the following resolutions:
1. That assistance be solicited from local public bodies
in connection with the dispute.
2. That two lawyers be engaged to carry out negotiations
with the landlords.

It is reported that the tenants are arranging to
re-connect the water supply to the alleyway themselves.

The Jui Tuh School suspended studies this morning,
April 26.

At 9.30 a.m. April 25, some 350 persons who claimed
to be representatives of various sub-offices and sections
of the Chapei District Rent Reduction Association proceeded
on seven motor trucks to the Shanghai City Government at

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Report re water supply being cut off from Pai Tuh Li Alleyway. (白德利里)

At 9.20p.m. 24-4-74, two residents representatives of Pai Tuh Li Alleyway, Tatung Road, came to the Station and reported that the water supply had been cut off from the aforementioned alleyway. The Water Works were informed by telephone and they stated that the instructions to that effect had been received from the Revenue Office owing to the residents of the said alleyway were in default of revenue due. A hydrant was opened so that water could be obtained.

At 4p.m. 25-4-74, the residents of this alleyway approached Mere Marie de St. Benvit (沈本篤姆) of the Jeu Tuh Primary School, situated at No. 78 of the same alleyway for the purpose of getting water supply from inside the school, to which she refused and ordered that the school gates be closed. Owing to a large number of residents who had adopted an aggressive attitude at the entrance of the premises, as a result the students were unable to leave in fear of being subjected to rough treatment at the hands of the residents.

On arrival of Police the crowd dispersed and the students left the school premises under Police protection.

Further enquiries ascertained that three days ago, the landlord of the alleyway in question notified all the chief tenants that a water meter be put up at every house

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE File No. B-REGI. S. No. D 3080/1 Date 26. 1. 34）

REPORT
Date 26. 1. 34

Subject (in full) Letter from Kaifeng Road landlords protesting against
meeting of tenants to further the rent reduction movement.

Made by D.S. Mac Adie Forwarded by Thomson DSS

Attached letter from landlords of alleyways on
Kaifeng Road appears to be somewhat exaggerated. The
meeting which is reported in detail below was of a similar
nature to those held by tenants of alleyways in various
districts throughout Shanghai in furthering the rent
reduction movement.

Between 2.30 p.m. and 4.30 p.m. April 22,
some 30 persons who claimed to be representatives
of the tenants of the Mah Shing Li (法興里), and Zang
Kong Li (長康里), Alabaster Road, and Yu Shing Faung
(餘興坊) and Tuh Shing Faung (德興坊), Kaifeng Road, held
a meeting in the Nanyang Girls School, No.1 Kaifeng Road.
Tsang Kai Shou (張介壽), who presided, reported that
arrangements had been made to form a rent reduction section
and application for membership had been submitted to the
Shanghai Municipality Rent Reduction Committee. The
following decisions were discussed and passed:-
1. That a Preparatory Committee be established at No.341
Kaifeng Road.
2. That local residents be urged to demand that the landlords
voluntarily reduce rentals.
3. That tenants who conspire with the landlords in an endeavour
to break the movement be warned in the first instance
and that should they again offend, they be proceeded
against in Court on a charge of breaking the regulations
of public organizations.

（批：file 2/3）

R. W. Mac Adie.
D. S.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

报告
日期 34.1.26

主题（全称） 开封路房东来信抗议租户集会以推动减租运动。

由特别区巡官 (D.S.) Mac Adie 撰写 由副高级巡官 (DSS) Thomson 转呈

所附开封路弄堂房东的来信似乎有些夸大。下文详细报告的这次集会，其性质与上海各区租户为推动减租运动而举行的类似集会相同。

4月22日下午2时30分至4时30分之间，约30名自称是阿拉巴斯特路（Alabaster Road）马兴里（Mah Shing Li，法興里）和长康里（Zang Kong Li，長康里），以及开封路余兴坊（Yu Shing Faung，餘興坊）和德兴坊（Tuh Shing Faung，德興坊）租户代表的人士，在开封路1号南洋女中举行了一次会议。主持会议的张介寿（Tsang Kai Shou）报告称，已安排成立减租分会，并向上海市减租委员会提交了入会申请。讨论并通过了以下决议：-
1. 在开封路341号设立筹备委员会。
2. 敦促当地居民要求房东自愿降低租金。
3. 对企图与房东勾结以破坏运动的租户首先提出警告，若再犯，则以违反公共团体规章之罪名起诉至法院。

（批注：归档 2/3）

R. W. Mac Adie.
特别区巡官 (D. S.)
特务科主管警官。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
G & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D
Date ...... / ...... / ......
Kaifeng Road Landlords,
Shanghai, April 22, 1934.

The Secretary,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
209 Kiangse Road, Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

We have to report to you that in the house No. Id 341
Kaifeng Road in the Northern District, an association of
tenants for the reducing of house rent has been established,
and that at about 2 o'clock this afternoon, more than 5 hun-
dred tenants, west of North Chekiang Road, north of North
Soochow Road, east of North Thibet Road, south of Haining Road,
attended the meeting held in the Nanyang Primary School in
Kaifeng Road at the end of Winchester Road, Cad. Lot §1 in
the Northern District.

"Knock down landlords. Not to pay the house rent,
until we have attained our object." was heard at this afternoon
meeting. We hear that they collect the membership fee, which
ranges from 20 cents to $1.50. Those who attended the meeting
are members of this association. Of course, the terants are
glad to be the members.

We wonder why the Municipal Council does not interfere
with, or prohibit the establishment of such associations in
the foreign Settlement, as such associations as these are
detrimental to the good order of the Settlement. Can you see
your way to drive such associations out of the Settlement? If
not, the Settlement will be ruined soon. We shall be glad to
see your notification regarding this affair.

Yours very truly,

Sze Kung Kwei & 7
Other Kaifeng Road Landlords.

上海，1934年4月22日。

秘书先生，
上海公共租界工部局，
上海江西路209号。

尊敬的先生：

我们要向贵局报告，在北区开封路341号（门牌Id 341）成立了一个旨在降低房租的租户协会，今天下午2时许，浙江北路以西、苏州河以北、西藏北路以东、海宁路以南地区的五百多名租户，参加了在北区 Winchester Road 尽头、地段 §1 的开封路南阳小学举行的会议。

在这次下午的会议上，有人听到喊出“打倒房东。不达目的，不付房租。”的口号。我们听说他们收取会员费，金额从2角到1.5元不等。参加会议的人都是该协会的会员。当然，租户们很乐意成为会员。

我们想知道，为何工部局不干预或禁止在外国租界内建立此类协会，因为此类协会不利于租界的良好秩序。您能否设法将此类协会驱逐出租界？如果不能，租界很快就会遭到破坏。我们很高兴看到您关于此事的通知。

此致
敬礼，

施公桂（Sze Kung Kwei）及其他7位
开封路房东。

REPORT
Date. April 25. 1934.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. M.D. 3682/1）

Subject (in full) Rent Reduction Movement - Cases where rent has been reduced as a result of agitation by tenants and payment withheld etc.

Made W. and Forwarded by D.S.I. Duncan

Following the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1932
a number of landlords suspended collection of rent for 2
months and upwards from tenants who had suffered as a result
of the hostilities. These cases, however, although
occurring at the commencement of the Rent Reduction Movement
cannot be regarded in the same light as those covered by the
dispute as it now stands. The following is a list of cases
which have come to the knowledge of the Police this year
where payment of rent has been withheld and where reductions
have been made by the landlords as a result of agitation by
the tenants:-

1. Following an attempt on February 8 of the Judicial Police
of the 2nd Special District Court to execute Distress
Warrants on the tenants of Nos.45 and 47 Tao Teh Li, Avenue
Foch, for non-payment of rentals for 3 months, the rent
was paid into Court the same day. A similar case occurred
at No.1 Avenue Foch on February 5 with the same result.

2. The landlord of a block of houses in Shing Nyih Fang, off
Scott Road, chiefly occupied by Japanese, reduced the
rents from Tls.60 to Tls.50 in February.

3. In February the landlords of 50 new houses in the Tseu
San Li, Chusan Road, reduced the rents by 10%.

4. On March 2, the landlords of the Heng Meu Li, Rue Wagner,
agreed to reduce the rents by 10% as the result of demands
for a reduction by the tenants.

5. In consequence of a suit filed by the landlords, distress
warrants were served on March 8 on 22 houses (Lane 381,
Houses Nos.383-403 odd numbers only, and Lane 405, Houses
Nos.4-24 even numbers only) on Tientsin Road for arrears

主题（全称） 减租运动 - 因租户煽动导致减租及拒付租金等案例。

由 W. 撰写 由副督察长 (D.S.I.) Duncan 转呈

继1932年中日敌对行动之后，许多房东暂停向受敌对行动影响的租户收取2个月或更长时间的租金。然而，这些案例虽然发生在减租运动初期，但不能与目前争端所涵盖的案例同等看待。以下是警方今年得知的因租户煽动而拒付租金以及房东因此减租的案例清单：-

1. 2月8日，第二特区地方法院司法警察试图对霞飞路（Avenue Foch）道德里（Tao Teh Li）45号和47号因拖欠3个月租金的租户执行扣押令，当天租金即缴入法院。2月5日，霞飞路1号发生类似案件，结果相同。

2. 斯科特路（Scott Road）旁新怡坊（Shing Nyih Fang）一处主要由日本人居住的房屋群的房东，在2月份将租金从60两降至50两。

3. 2月份，舟山路（Chusan Road）舟山里（Tseu San Li）50栋新房的房东将租金降低了10%。

4. 3月2日，华格纳路（Rue Wagner）恒美里（Heng Meu Li）的房东因租户要求减租，同意将租金降低10%。

5. 由于房东提起诉讼，3月8日对天津路（Tientsin Road）22户房屋（381弄，仅单号383-403号；405弄，仅双号4-24号）因拖欠

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Activities in the Settlement of the Rent Reduction
Federation of all tenants in Shanghai

At 2.5 p.m. on the 16/1/36 Wong Ching An (翁吟庵) shroff and Ts Tsang Ming (朱昌明) watchman, both employed by the Shanghai Lane Investment Co. 100 Jenkee Road brought to this station one named Zung S Kwang (東日光) 32, Canton, M/canvasser residing No101 Bau Tung Road, Chapel and employed by the Rent Reduction Federation of all Tenants in Shanghai. Head Office, 181 Ying Ka Jau Road, off North Szechmen Road, Chapel.

Zung S Kwang had been observed at about 2 p.m. 16/1/36 in the Zung Woo Faung off Wushow Road by the shroff and watchman, going from door to door in the alleyway and asking tenants if they wished to become members of the Federation.

A number of the tenants were seen to pay money to Zung S Kwang after they had filled a form in (specimen attached).

Questioned at the station Zung S Kwang stated he was one of a number employed by the Federation.

Should the tenant wish to become a member and filled a form in the customary fee paid was $1.00 However, should the tenant not wish to co-operate nothing further was done and the canvasser left. No coercion or intimidation was used to induce the tenants

Shanghai, 14th Jan., 1936.

Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Shanghai

Dear Sir,

Rent Agitation

We are experiencing considerable trouble
from rent agitation societies on our Boone Road property
and our Wuchow Road property. Hand bills calling on our
tenants to refuse to pay rent have been distributed and
fees are being collected by these societies from the tenants.

We shall be greatly obliged if the police
at Kashing Road Police Station and at the Hongkew Station
may be warned, as it is possible we may have to get some of
the agitators taken to the charge rooms at these two
stations.

We are, Dear Sir,
Yours faithfully,
THE SHANGHAI LAND INVESTMENT CO., Ltd.

N.L. Sparke
Manager

Made by D. S. I. Lee Yee Tong. Forwarded by Insp. C. Phillips.

(批：Translation only attached gx)

Sir,
Re the attached letter enquiries were made by the under-
signed at the office of the 4th Branch Rent Reduction
Association 131 Ford Lane and the following has been
ascertained.
The Association was organised by over 200 residents of
the Vai San Li, Vei Sin Li and old Vei Sin Li in Thorborn
and Pingliang Roads and Ford Lane about 2 months ago with
the sole object of negotiating with house owners to reduce
the present house rent by 10% of shops and 20% of houses
in alleyways but the house owners only grant a reduction
of 10% with the former and 12.5% with the latter.
The chairman of the Association is Fan Vei Tuh (范維德)
who is the proprietor of the Sui Chong Sing (瑞昌兴) candle
and money exchange shop, 175/7 Thorborn Road and he was
elected by the standing committee of 17 members, besides
there is a secretary named Tao Tseng Wu (陶吾). The
members on the standing committee were elected by the
residents meeting and they themselves are all vitally
concerned in the present rent reduction.
Every resident is required to pay a sum of $1.00 to the
Association for initiation fees only.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

Lee Yee Tong
D. S. I.

Sir,
With reference to the above, I beg to report that at 5.05 p.m.
11-9-35, a male Chinese named Sung Tung Yee, representative of
the Sai Yih Silk Co., 463 Nanking Road, came to the station and re-
ported that representatives of the Hardoon Rent Office were at
their shop and were preventing customers from entering to make
purchases. Police were sent to the scene and the representatives
of the Hardoon Rent Co. denied interfering with either customers
or shop assistants. They stated that they had been sent there to
collect the rent due and to stay on the premises until it was
paid. Both parties were cautioned re creating a breach of the
peace and were referred to the S.S.D. Court.

From enquiries made, it was ascertained that the Silk Co.
had entered the premises on 1/4/35. The rental of the shop
being $750.00 per month, payable in advance. The rent was
paid up until 1st July and when the Hardoon Agent tried to
collect the rent for July, he was told that they were short
of money and would pay in a few days time. After the third
visit the manager of the Silk Company stated that he
was now a member of the
Rent Reduction Association and that he had been instructed not
to pay any rent until all rents in Shanghai had been reduced
by 40%. According to Mr. Yih Fah Kaung, Lawyer, representing
the Hardoon Rent Office, numerous visits were made in July,
August and September to get the Silk Company to pay the rent.
Mr. Yih was asked why they did not take the case to Court
and he stated that should they take the matter before the
S.S.D. Court, the defendants be certain to appeal and whilst the
affair was sub-judice, no rent would be paid and when there was

先生，
关于上述事项，谨报告如下：1935年9月11日下午5时05分，一名叫宋同义（Sung Tung Yee）的中国男子，南京路463号赛益丝绸公司（Sai Yih Silk Co.）的代表，来到捕房报案，称哈同洋行租赁处（Hardoon Rent Office）的代表在其店内，阻止顾客进店购物。警方被派往现场，哈同租赁公司的代表否认干扰顾客或店员。他们称是被派去收取到期租金，并在租金付清前留在该处。双方均因可能扰乱治安受到警告，并被引荐至特区法院处理。

经查询得知，该丝绸公司于1935年4月1日入驻该 premises。店铺月租金为750.00元，需预付。租金已付至7月1日，当哈同代理人试图收取7月份租金时，被告知资金短缺，将在几天内支付。在第三次上门后，丝绸公司经理表示他现在是减租协会的会员，并接到指示，在上海所有租金降低40%之前，不支付任何租金。据代表哈同租赁处的律师叶发强（Yih Fah Kaung，音译）称，7月、8月和9月多次上门要求丝绸公司支付租金。当问及为何不将此案诉诸法庭时，叶先生表示，如果他们将其提交特区法院，被告肯定会上诉，而在案件审理期间，不会支付任何租金，而当有

Rough Translation of letter addressed to
Louza Station from Shanghai Special Area
Street Union No. 1 Branch Office situated
at 602 Nanking Road on 3rd floor of
Tai-Kong Building. (Telephone No. 92051).
............
Reporting illegal exercise done by the Hardoon
Rent Office Staff when demanding the payment
of rent from the various shops who are the tenants
of the above-mentioned office, & requesting for Police
protection in case of the same being taken place.
..............
11-9-35.

Officer i/c Louza Station,
Ningpo Road.

Sir,
We beg to forward the following reports made by our members,
Doong Foh Silk Bureau et al requesting for the Police protection :-
to
" Owing/the speed depression of business, we can hardly
carry on our business also due to the fact that the
rent has grown to the maximum especially on Nanking Road.
Some of the landlords knew our difficulties and gave
their tenants a reduction on the rent but Hardoon Rent
Office insisted on his own way. Besides, Hardoon Rent
Office adopted an illegal system of collecting the rent,
which is really offensive. When collecting the rent,
the Office usually sent a party of about 8 or 10 men
to his tenant's shop where they freely caused disturbance
and hindered our business. If the tenants failed to pay
the rent on behalf of the non-business, the said Office
should take legal procedure by means of taking civil
action at Court. It is not fair to demand the payment
of the rent by force (as above mentioned). As we have
are
paid the tax to the S.M.C., of course we entitled to
receive certain previlage of protection. It is expected
that the above case will be reported to the Police.
In case, the similar disturbance committed by the
said Office, took place, we have to ask Patrol men to
bring them to the Police Station."

Hoping you will kindly consider this matter,
We are, Sir,
Yours faithfully,
(Chopped).

Translated by Clerk Shao Chen Pao.

..............
1935年9月11日。

老闸捕房主管警官，
宁波路。

先生：
谨此转呈本会会员董福丝绸局等提出的报告，请求警方保护：-
“由于商业严重萧条，我们难以维持经营，加之租金已涨至最高水平，尤其是在南京路。部分房东知晓我们的困难，给予了租户租金减免，但哈同洋行收租处坚持己见。此外，哈同洋行收租处采取了一种非法的收租方式，实在令人反感。在收租时，该处通常派遣约8至10人的一伙人前往租户店铺，肆意滋扰，阻碍我们的生意。如果租户因生意不佳而未能支付租金，该处应通过向法院提起民事诉讼的法律程序来解决。以上述方式强行要求支付租金是不公平的。既然我们要向工部局纳税，当然有权获得相应的保护特权。期望将上述案件报告给警方。若该处再次制造类似滋扰，我们将要求巡警将其带往警察局。”

希望您能体谅此事，
此致，
敬礼，
（盖章）。

由书记员邵臣宝翻译。
