First Branch Office, of the Shanghai First District Area, 3rd.
Floor of the Tsd Kong Building, 602 Nanking Road, dated 12-9-35.

Sir,

We beg to inform you that many reports have been received
during the past two days from our members, "San Yih Silk Store,
Kwun Shing Co., Tah Lai Hosiery Store, Tong Foh Silk Store and
others, at this federation that the Hardoon Rent Office had
collected the house rents from them not in accordance with
proper procedure and had sent a number of men to their stores
and
creating a disturbance, obstructing their business. They requested
us to send you a letter asking you to protect them immediately.

accordance with the above facts to you yesterday and
we are now sending you a photograph which was taken by the
San Yih Silk Sotre when the trouble occurred.

Under such circumstances, we sincerely request you to
detail some of your Police Officers to patrol especially in
the vicinity of the above mentioned shops in order to prevent
further trouble which has already occurred.

先生：

谨此告知，在过去两天内，本会收到多名会员的报告，包括“三益丝绸店”、“群胜公司”、“大利袜店”、“同福丝绸店”及其他商家，称哈同洋行收租处未按正当程序向他们收取房租，并派遣多人到其店铺制造骚乱，阻碍其生意。他们请求我们去函贵处，恳请立即予以保护。

Sir,

At 9 a.m. 25-7-35, Mr. W. Coulbourn representative of
Marcel Darge, Property and Estate Agents, No. 1 The Bund,
came to station and requested assistance to remove posters
and banners advocating a reduction of rent, which were
exhibited in Lane 991 Ward Road which property belongs to above
mentioned Firm.

S.I. Hyerscough and C.D.S.11 accompanied Mr. Coulbourn
for the purpose of preventing a breach of the peace.

Enquiries in the vicinity ascertained that the posters
were exhibited by an association formed by the tenants of the
houses in the same alleyway who are agitating for a reduction
of rent.

Mr. Coulbourn removed two of the banners but a crowd
formed and objected to the removal and demanded the return of
same.

At this juncture S.I. Hyerscough intervened as certain
members of the crowd were inclined to become boisterous.
It was then decided that both parties adjourn to House No.
156 of same alleyway to continue the discussion, however no
progress was made regarding the reduction of rent but it
was agreed that the posters were to remain until the landlords
make representatives of the disgruntled tenants to a meeting
to discuss this matter.

Hereunder is a translation of the banners etc. exhibited:-
(1) All in one heart.
(2) Uphold the General Rent Reduction Meeting.
(3) Strict movement for rent reduction.
(4) The minimum demand is for 30% reduction of rent.

先生：

1935年7月25日上午9时，外滩1号马塞尔·达吉（Marcel Darge）房地产代理行的代表 W. Coulbourn 先生来到捕房，请求协助移除张贴在华德路991弄（该物业属于上述商行）的宣传减租的海报和横幅。

警长 Hyerscough 和 C.D.S.11 陪同 Coulbourn 先生，以防止破坏和平。

经在附近调查得知，这些海报是由同一弄堂内房屋的租户组成的一个协会张贴的，该协会正在鼓动减租。

Coulbourn 先生移除了两条横幅，但人群聚集并反对移除，要求归还横幅。

此时，鉴于人群中某些成员倾向于变得喧闹，警长 Hyerscough 介入干预。随后决定双方移至同一弄堂的156号继续讨论，然而关于减租一事未取得进展，但双方同意在海报名义上的房东派代表与不满的租户开会讨论此事之前，海报予以保留。

以下是对所展示的横幅等的译文：-
(1) 万众一心。
(2) 拥护全体减租大会。
(3) 严格开展减租运动。
(4) 最低要求是减租30%。

At 11 a.m. on the 12th October, 1934, one
Yang Voong Kwei (楊鳳魁), Proprietor of Yu Shing Cheng
(裕興昌) Clothier Shop, 1202 Gordon Road, and one Chang
Tuh Shing (張德興), Assistant in the employ of the
Yee Shing Cheng (儀興昌) Clothier Shop at 1186 Gordon
Road, brought to the Footen Road Station two Chinese named
Zung Yah Ling (孫學齡), age 19, native of Shanghai, and
one Wong Vung Hsi (王文軒), age 29, native of Shanghai,
and complained that the latter two persons had called at
their respective shops for the purpose of canvassing
subscribers for a paper entitled "Special Publication for
Rent Reduction Movement in Shanghai" and of collecting a
subscription of ten cents to cover four issues of the
publication, claiming at the same time that they were
representatives of the "Rent Reduction Committee", which
has a branch office at No.3 Yeong Ching Li, Minkue Road,
Nantao.

In the case of the first complainant,
it appears that on calling at his shop they handed him
a receipt for ten cents in the name of the "Rent Reduction
Committee" and asked him to pay the subscription. This
complainant saw by the receipt that the Committee had its

南市民国路永庆里三号减租委员会代表在租界内募集捐款。

1934年10月12日上午11时，戈登路1202号裕兴昌（Yu Shing Cheng）布店店主杨凤魁（Yang Voong Kwei）一名，以及戈登路1186号仪兴昌（Yee Shing Cheng）布店店员张德兴（Chang Tuh Shing）一名，将两名华人带至福腾路巡捕房，这两名华人为孙学龄（Zung Yah Ling），19岁，上海籍，和王文轩（Wong Vung Hsi），29岁，上海籍。投诉人称，后两人曾前往他们各自的店铺，目的是为一份题为《上海减租运动特刊》的刊物招募订阅者，并收取十美分订阅费以涵盖四期刊物，同时声称他们是“减租委员会”的代表，该委员会在南市民国路永庆里三号设有分部办公室。

就第一位投诉人而言，
似乎当他们光顾其店铺时，递给他一张以“减租委员会”名义开具的十美分收据，并要求他支付订阅费。这位投诉人从收据上看到委员会的

page_data.en:
"B"
Misc. 106/34.         Footoo Road
                      October 12th;       34.

offices in Nantao and he told the representatives that
as a resident of the Settlement he could derive no benefit
by subscribing and that in his opinion they had no right
to collect subscriptions in the Settlement. They argued
with him and said that a man of his common-sense, which
was far above that of the ignorant rickshaw coolie, should
not refuse to pay the subscription and that he had only to
read the newspapers to be assured that the Committee had
been established for the public weal. This complainant,
however, insisted that he had no desire to pay the
subscription and the two men then left the shop. He
watched them to see where they were going next and he saw
them enter the shop in which the second complainant is
employed as an assistant, so he decided to go in after
them and dissuade the employees there from paying the
subscription. Meanwhile they approached the second
complainant and upon their request, in the absence of the
proprietor, he paid the subscription of ten cents and they
gave a receipt. At this moment the 1st complainant came
into the shop and drew the 2nd complainant's attention to
the fact that the Committee was a Nantao organisation, as
shown by the address on the receipt, and advised him to
take back his subscription as its representatives had no
right to collect subscriptions in the Settlement. The
2nd complainant agreed with this view and asked the
representatives to return his subscription but they

Shanghai Water Works Company.

14th September 1934.

Chief Inspector's Report of an Assault on one of
Company's Employees.
Lane 2181, L-5/137 Yangtszepoo Road.

A request having been received from the Revenue
Department to shut off water at the above for unpaid
accounts, Inspector Broadley was instructed to carry
out the work.

He shut the property off at 9.15 a.m. this morning
and in accordance with instructions proceeded to the nearest
street hydrant No.2118, in order to give the tenants an
alternative supply.

The hydrant was turned on but before he could get away
the Company's van was surrounded by the tenants of the
block and both he and his Chinese assistant were stoned
and also made the target for discharge of the contents
of night soil buckets.

The tenants had also stolen the Company's stopcock,
valve and hydrant keys from the van and the attitude
of the tenants wassuch that Broadley was compelled to turn on
the water to the block. To do this the tenants returned the
stopcock key only.

By this time a Police Van had arrived from the Glen
Road Police Station and the necessary keys were recovered
by the Police and returned to the Company's Inspector who
proceeded to the Police Station and made his report.

The Police informed Broadley that this is a dispute
between the landlord and his tenants and it is evident
that the landlord has refused to pay his water charges so
as to use this Company to bring his tenants to book.

上海自来水公司。

1934年9月14日。

总督察关于本公司一名员工遭受袭击的报告。
杨树浦路 L-5/137号，2181弄。

收税部门要求切断上述地点的供水，原因是账户欠款未付，总督察Broadley奉命执行此项工作。

他于今天上午9时15分切断了该处的供水，并按照指示前往最近的2118号街道消防栓，以便为租户提供替代水源。

消防栓被打开，但在他离开之前，公司的货车被该街区的租户包围，他和他的中国助手不仅遭到石块投掷，还成为倾倒粪桶内容的目标。

租户还从货车上偷走了公司的止水阀、阀门和消防栓钥匙，租户的态度迫使Broadley不得不重新向该街区供水。为此，租户仅归还了止水阀钥匙。

此时，一辆警车从格伦路（Glen Road，音译，疑为格林路或某具体路名）巡捕房抵达，警察找回了必要的钥匙并归还给公司督察，后者随即前往巡捕房提交报告。

警察告知Broadley，这是房东与租户之间的纠纷，显然房东拒绝支付水费，以便利用本公司来约束其租户。

先生，
关于“D”区警官的备注，卑职与副督察长刘文超（Liu Wen Chao）前往广东路420弄5号房东办事处进行了查询。
查明事实如下。
房东此前曾缴纳水费，但并未要求上海自来水公司（S.W. Works）停止供水。1934年9月13日，上海自来水公司的收费员来到上述办事处，要求支付6月、7月和8月的水费。房东告知他们，这几个月的租金尚未收讫，且因依赖租金来支付此类账目，故无钱支付水费。
收费员随即离开，在他向公司汇报后，该公司方面想必自行发出了切断供水的指令。
关于查封房屋一事，尚未收到特区法院（S.S.D. Court）的进一步消息。

先生，
1934年9月12日下午5时，华捕3227号将一名名为吴永年（Woo Yoong Hyi，音译）的男子带至巡捕房。该男子25岁，男性，出纳，宁波人，居住于南市。他于当日下午4时40分在扬州路与仁川路（Chemulpo Road）转角处被捕，系应扬州路104号主要租户郭金水（Koh Kyung Sung，音译）之请求。因其向郭金水索要上述协会捐款10分钱。

经查，该男子持有一枚编号为38的徽章及一本由上海减租协会颁发的收据簿，用于在上海居民中募集捐款（每户10分钱），以为该协会筹集资金。

经刑事侦缉股警佐104号、刑事侦缉股警员60号及卑职讯问，吴永年（Woo Koong Hyi，音译）称，上述组织由一名名为沈心鉴（Zung Sing Woo，音译）的人领导，办公地点位于南市民国路911号。

Sir,
At about 3.30 p.m. 10/9/34, F.S. Ananyin, accompanied by Chinese Judicial Police of the 1st Branch Shanghai Special District Court, visited Kashing Road Station and requested assistance to seal premise Lane 807/27 Dixwell Road, for non-payment of rent.
F.S. Jack accompanied F.S. Ananyin and party to the aforementioned premises and were obstructed by the inmates of the house in question, and other residents of the lane.
S.I. Ware subsequently arrived on the scene and, in view of the refusal of the inmates and sympathisers to quit the premises in order that they be sealed, the Municipal Police and in conjunction with Judicial Police commenced to forcible eject the occupants of the downstairs main front room. This procedure caused the ire of the occupants and other residents of the lane, which necessitated a call for police reinforcements. On arrival of the reinforcement it was discovered that the residents had to some extent been pacified, and were further addressed by Supt. Alers, D.D.O. "C", who suggested to them to visit Kashing Road Station, where they could make their complaint.
It was subsequently learned from S.I. Ware that, while the party were ejecting the occupants of the house, a male Chinese, subsequently ascertained to be one named Wo Tse Kyung (胡祖金), aged 36 years, native of Ningpo, residing at 807/28 Dixwell Road, threw an ordure bucket at the police party, causing the contents of the bucket to splash over S.I. Ware and F.S. Jack, whereupon the aforementioned person was taken into custody and was charged with interference with the lawful discharge of public functions.
On arraignment before the S.S.D. Court in the forenoon of the 11/9/34 the arrested man was remanded in custody until 15/9/34 a.m.

阁下，
1934年9月10日下午约3时30分，法医阿纳宁（Ananyin）在上海特区法院第一分院中国司法警察的陪同下，访问了嘉善路巡捕房，请求协助查封迪克威尔路807弄27号的房产，理由是未付租金。
杰克（Jack）法医陪同阿纳宁法医一行人前往上述房产，但遭到该房屋住户及弄堂其他居民的阻拦。
韦尔（Ware）巡佐随后抵达现场，鉴于住户及同情者拒绝离开房屋以便进行查封，工部局警察会同司法警察开始强行驱逐楼下正面前厅的 occupants（居住者）。此举激怒了住户及弄堂其他居民，致使警方不得不呼叫增援。增援到达后发现，居民情绪已有所平复，“C”区副总监艾尔斯（Alers）警司进一步向他们讲话，建议他们前往嘉善路巡捕房提出投诉。
随后从韦尔巡佐处获悉，在警方驱逐房屋居住者期间，一名中国男子（后查明名为胡祖金，Wo Tse Kyung，36岁，宁波人，居住于迪克威尔路807弄28号）向警方人员投掷粪桶，导致桶内污物溅到韦尔巡佐和杰克法医身上。随后该人被拘留，并被指控妨碍公务执行。
在1934年9月11日上午于上海特区法院提审时，被捕男子被还押候审，直至1934年9月15日上午。

        Acting on the advice imparted by Supt. Aiers, as previously
mentioned, about 20 women residents of the lane subsequently visited
Kashing Road Station.
        These persons were questioned and the appended particulars
ascertained.
        About nine months ago the residents of the lane, which is an
estate of 56 houses, inaugurated a rent reduction movement and
refused to make payment of rent until the landlord had reduced the
present rental of $56.80 per month. The monetary reduction required
by the tenants not being stipulated.
        At the time this rent reduction movement was inaugurated the
rentals were being collected by Wong Yoong Woo (王榮武), accountant
of the Yoong Chong Shing (永昌興) Coal Co., 805 Dixwell Road, on
behalf of the proprietor of the coal Company, one named Yih Tsung Kyiu
(葉尊九), who resides in Soochow, and who is the owner of the estate.
        Continually overtures made to tenants for the payment met with
refusal, all stating that the money was being paid into their
respective banks pending the reduction of the rent of the houses.
        In view of the inability of the landlord to collect rentals
the estate was placed in the hands of Messrs Brandt Rogers, Ltd.,
391 Kiangse Road, who are now acting as the agents of the property.
        The tenants still refuse to make payment of the rent until such
times that the landlord makes a reduction.
        In respect to the premises ordered to be sealed by the S.S.D.
Court, it was learned that the tenant took over occupancy of the
premises in May 1934, making a deposit of three months rent.
        During the ensuing three months no rent was paid by the tenant,
he being under the impression that having deposited three months rent
he had no need to pay any rent until the expiry of the three months.

        按照前述艾尔斯（Aiers）警司的建议，该弄堂约20名女性居民随后前往嘉善路巡捕房。
        对这些人员进行了讯问，并查明了附录中的详细情况。
        大约九个月前，该弄堂（一个拥有56栋房屋的地产）的居民发起了一场减租运动，并拒绝支付租金，直到房东将目前每月56.80美元的租金降低为止。租户并未明确规定要求减少的具体金额。
        在这场减租运动发起时，租金由迪克威尔路805号永昌兴（Yoong Chong Shing）煤公司的会计王榮武（Wong Yoong Woo）代为收取，他是该煤行老板叶尊九（Yih Tsung Kyiu）的代表。叶尊九居住在苏州，是该地产的所有者。
        房东方面不断向租户催缴租金，但均遭拒绝，所有人都声称在房租降低之前，钱款已存入各自的银行。
        鉴于房东无法收取租金，该地产已被移交至江西路391号的布兰特·罗杰斯有限公司（Messrs Brandt Rogers, Ltd.），该公司目前担任该物业的代理人。
        租户仍拒绝支付租金，直到房东降低租金为止。
        关于上海特区法院下令查封的房产，据悉该租户于1934年5月接管该房产，并支付了三个月的租金作为押金。
        在接下来的三个月里，该租户未支付任何租金，因为他误以为既然已经支付了三个月的租金作为押金，在这三个月期满之前无需再支付任何租金。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

At 12:45 p.m. 28-7-34 D.I. Grubb attached to Headquarters brought to Central Station a letter written in Chinese, and which was thought to contain threats and he instructed the undersigned to make enquiries into the matter.

A translation of the letter is as follows:-

Envelope addressed to Mr. Zang Yue Chee, Chinese manager, Republic Land Investment Co. 149 Yuen Ming Yuen Road.

Contents of letter.

Dear Manager Yue Chee,

We have long heard of your name but never had the opportunity to meet you but since we have moved into your company's houses in the Eastern District we begin to learn your personality. It is out of our question whether you are a good man or not as the proverb says "Mischief and fortune are brought to one, by oneself" and we wonder why you are willing to be a "running dog" of the capitalist without taking into consideration the welfare of the people. You have treated the tenants of these terraces with high handed oppression as well as continuing to seal our properties. We have suffered thereby very deeply and clearly recognize your personality and action for which we will seek means to repay. Now you are a round faced rich man and must have a lot

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

At 6.30 p.m. 1/6/34 complainant came to the
station and reported that he had received two letters,
signed "City Rent Reduction Committee Association,
Investigation Groupe.", in which he was told a bomb
would be thrown into his shop.

Enquiries by C.D.C. 289 and the undersigned
elicited that at 1 p.m. 28/5/34 he received a letter
signed, but not "chopped", by the above committee to
the effect that he had already paid his rent which
was breach of the association's regulations, and
that a parcel of excrement would be sent to him. It
also said that if he defaulted again a bomb would be
thrown into his shop. It finished up by telling him
to organize a branch of the Rent Reduction Associa-
tion.

During the night of 30/5/34 his door was smeared
with excrement and at 1 p.m. 1/6/34 he received another
letter. This time he was warned that if he did not
have a branch of the organization running by 3/6/34
they would throw the bomb on that day.

The envelopes were taken to the Carter Road sub-
post office and an official there stated that though
the post mark was very indistinct, he thought that the
letters had been posted on Soochow Road (South side)
between Thibet Road and the Garden Bridge.

The necessary precautions will be taken on 3/6/34
meanwhile enquiries are being continued.

经刑事侦缉队警员289号及本人查询得知，34年5月28日下午1时，他收到一封由上述委员会署名但未盖印的信函，大意是他已支付租金，违反了协会规定，并将寄给他一包粪便。信中还称，如果他再次违约，将向他的店铺投掷炸弹。最后要求他组织一个减租协会分会。

Translation.

1st letter. Received 1 p.m. 28.5.34

The "Rent reduction" movement is now progressing in the
whole city. It was ordered that from January the rent payment be
stopped. Now we hear that you have already paid the February rent,
it is an obvious breach of our regulations. Last night we sent you
a parcel of spicy yellow gold powder (excrement) as a present. If
you pay rent again, before rent reduction is effective we will send
you a bomb. After receiving this letter, make haste to organize a
rent reduction branch, and be responsible to manage it.
.. .. b. .. .. ..

2nd letter. Received 1 p.m. 1.6.34.

We hope you received our first letter, but the branch
organization is not yet arranged. Last night we sent somebody to
your shop and smeared the yellow powder (excrement) on your window.
We should have put it in your mouth, but as you are a 'good merchant
we gave you some "face". We now give you three days limit in which
to organize the rent reduction branch committee. If you have still
failed we will do the fiercer action mentioned in our first letter,
and fear it will then be too late to regret.

(Signed)
City Rent Reduction Committee Associa-
tion, Investigation Groups.

希望你已收到我方第一封信，但分会组织尚未安排妥当。昨晚我们派人到你的店铺，将黄粉（粪便）涂在你的窗户上。本应塞进你嘴里，但鉴于你是位‘好商人’，给你留了些‘面子’。现限你三天内组织减租分会委员会。若仍未能办成，我们将执行第一封信中提到的更激烈行动，届时恐悔之晚矣。

Subject (in full) The Judicial Police obstructed in the execution of their duty.

Made by D.S.Goloe Ukoff, Forwarded by W M Burton

Sir,

I beg to report that at 11.20 a.m. 5/6/34, T.P.S. Braikovsky attached to the Judicial Police reported to this station that he together with C.P.C's.1011 and 995 also attached to the Judicial Police were accompanying S.S.D.Court clerk Yang Yoo Ming (楊育民) and Process server Ts Z Tsing (朱士珍) who had been ordered by Court to have the property of 61 tenants occupying the buildings of the Republic Land Investment Co., attached, and that the said tenants were obstructing them in the execution of their duty.

(Note and view to file. Jy)
(noted HG 6/6 34)

F.S.104, Allen was detailed to proceed with the above officers to the scene of occurrence and on arrival at Lee Zung Founz alleyway off East Broadway they saw one Yih Wei Foh (葉惠富) 37, Ningpo, tailor of house No.19, in the same alleyway, who was acting in a disorderly manner, talking excitedly to his neighbours and thus preventing the officers from carrying on their work.

F.S.Allen removed the above named and brought him to the station. At 11.55 a.m. the same date the officers of the Judicial Police, brought to the station two others named Zung Yeong Taung (程雲堂), 26, Ningpo, cook and Taung Ching Taung (程錦棠) 52, Ningpo, cook, both of 23 Lee Zung Faung alleyway of Broadway East.

F.S. 104号 Allen 奉命随同上述警官前往事发地点，到达百老汇路（East Broadway）旁的李忠坊（Lee Zung Founz）弄堂时，看见同弄堂19号的住户叶惠富（Yih Wei Foh），37岁，宁波人，裁缝，行为紊乱，激动地与邻居交谈，从而阻碍警官开展工作。

Shanghai, May 28th 1934.

To the Superintendent,
West Hongkew Police Station.

Dear Sir:-

We, the tenants of Ning Kong Lee off North Chekiang Road, beg to respectively inform you that on account of demand of an increase of 40 per cent monthly house rent, a legal proceeding has been taken place by the landowner Lee Dah-fu against the tenants at the end of 1930 and after having been made with a counter appeal to the Higher District Court, an order was issued by the said court on the 26th. January 1931 ordering to make an increase of 15 % instead of 40 %. Owing to the War broke out at Shanghai on the 28th January 1931, it was impossible for the tenants to deal with this matter within the fixed period of 20 days and most of them living at Ning Kong Lee have removed away. Both the landowner as well as Woo Tse-ping, his lawyer, have never mentioned anything again in regard to this matter until on the 20th. April 1934 while a Court Order was suddenly received ordering 32 tenants at Ning Kong Lee to make repayment of over 3 years' increase with the amount of $179.40 up to $750.00. The reason why we can't fulfil the order is that firstly the situation at present has greatly changed since the 28th. Jan. 1931, as we really have suffered so heavily during the War when both the iron gates at the corner have been closed for about 4 months; secondly most of the tenants are now NOT the original ones living at Ning Kong Lee before the War and are absolutely without any knowledge of the court case; thirdly it is rather unreasonable for the landowner to demand for such an increase of house rent just at the time when the local market is badly so bad at everywhere and yet some reduction of house rent have already begun at different places such as at Nantao, Chapel and also in the Settlements. Besides that the house rent of Ning Kong Lee is comparatively higher than that in the neighbourhood as this has already been ascertained in a reply received from the Major of Greater Shanghai who has sent the Chairman of the Commission of House Rent Affairs to make a thorough investigation into this matter. Under these circumstances we have been lodging a strong protest against the Land-owner's demand at the Court for execution of the Order and in the meantime we must ask you to kindly send a warning to the said landowner, who is represented by his lawyer Woo Tse-ping at No. 3 Thibet Road, Lane 340, not to press the tenants too hard and say "in case any trouble or disturbance will be arisen upon the landowner's so doing, he will take the entire responsibility."

Yours faithfully,
(Chop) The Union of the tenants of
Ning Kong Lee.

Information will be furnished:
Address:- Care of
412 Lane No. 7 Ning Kong Lee
372 " " 7 " " "
402 " " 3 " " "

上海，1934年5月28日。

致：
虹口西区警署巡官。

尊敬的先生：-

我们，浙江北路宁康里的租户，谨此分别告知阁下，因房东李达夫（音译）要求每月房租增加40%，其于1930年底对租户提起诉讼；经向高等分区法院提出反诉后，该院于1931年1月26日发布命令，裁定房租增幅为15%而非40%。由于1931年1月28日上海爆发战争，租户无法在规定的20天内处理此事，且居住在宁康里的大多数租户已搬离。房东及其律师吴子平（音译）此后从未再提及此事，直到1934年4月20日，突然收到法院命令，要求宁康里的32名租户补交三年多的增租款，金额从179.40美元至750.00美元不等。我们无法履行该命令的原因如下：首先，自1931年1月28日以来，目前局势已发生重大变化，我们在战争期间遭受了沉重打击，当时街角的铁门关闭了约4个月；其次，大多数租户并非战前居住在宁康里的原住户，对该诉讼案完全不知情；第三，在当地市场普遍低迷之际，房东要求如此大幅度的涨租极不合理，且南市、闸北及租界等地已开始减租。此外，宁康里的房租相对高于周边地区，这一点已由大上海市长派出的房租事务委员会主席在进行彻底调查后的回复中得到证实。鉴于上述情况，我们已在法院对房东要求执行命令的行为提出强烈抗议，同时恳请阁下向该房东发出警告，其代理律师为西藏路340弄3号吴子平，要求其不要过度逼迫租户，并声明“若因房东此举引发任何麻烦或骚乱，由其承担全部责任。”

此致，
敬礼，
（盖章）宁康里租户联合会。

China Times (Editorial):

THE COMMENCEMENT OF ANGLO-JAPANESE TRADE WAR

By the use of force, Japan has destroyed
the peace in the Far East, and China as a consequence
has suffered. By enforcing a policy of dumping, Japan
has disturbed the world market, and Britain has been
deprived of all her former exclusive markets. Japan is
realizing her ambition by political and financial means.
No wonder she is held in contempt by the countries of
the world. However, no country is bold enough to punish
her for her political encroachment. Her encroachment
by financial means has caused reactions. India is the
first Dominion of Britain to react to the Japanese
financial invasion. Agitation for measures to deal with
the Japanese competition is particularly manifest among
textile traders of Lancashire. As a last resort, Mr.
Runciman, President of the British Board of Trade, made
an announcement of a protective policy.
Some one says that although Japan could
not be punished with political sanction., she would be
dealt with financially by Britain in cooperation with
America and that we can rejoice in the possibility of
Japan being thus endangered and our country being relieved.
From the announcement made by Mr. Runciman,
we deduce the following three conclusions:-
In the first place, the announcement was
made to pacify his country men, because if it is intended
as the beginning of a conflict, why has not the British
Government abrogated the Anglo-Japanese Treaty of Commerce?
In the second place, the deadlock in the
negotiations between Britain and Japan occurred when
Britain insisted upon the negotiations covering the whole
world while Japan maintained that the parley should be
confined only to the British colonies and Dominions. Should
the announcement be intended to break up the relations
between Britain and Japan, the latter can dump all her
surplus goods on the markets outside the British colonies
and and Dominions.

《时事新报》（社论）：

英日贸易战之开端

日本以武力破坏远东和平，中国因此受害。日本推行倾销政策，扰乱世界市场，英国丧失其以往所有的独占市场。日本正通过政治和金融手段实现其野心。难怪其为世界各国所蔑视。然而，尚无国家敢于因其政治侵略而惩罚之。其金融侵略已引起反响。印度是第一个对日本金融入侵作出反应的英国自治领。兰开夏郡的纺织商中，要求采取措施应对日本竞争的运动尤为明显。作为最后手段，英国贸易委员会主席朗西曼先生（Mr. Runciman）宣布了一项保护性政策。
有人说，虽然日本未受政治制裁之惩罚，但英国将联合美国对其采取金融手段加以对付，我们可以为日本由此陷入困境、我国得以解脱的可能性而感到欣慰。
从朗西曼先生的声明中，我们得出以下三个结论：——
首先，该声明旨在安抚其国民，因为如果意在开启冲突，英国政府为何不废除《英日通商条约》？
其次，英日谈判陷入僵局，是因为英国坚持谈判应涵盖全球，而日本则主张会谈应仅限于英国殖民地和自治领。如果该声明意在破裂英日关系，后者可将其所有剩余商品倾销到英国殖民地和自治领以外的市场。

May 10, 1934. Morning Translation.

China Times and other local newspapers:

CHANGE OF NAMES IN THE PUBLIC SAFETY BUREAU

In pursuance of a resolution passed at the meeting of police officers of various cities convened by the Ministry of Interior last year, General Wen Hung En, Commissioner of Public Safety, has submitted an application to the Shanghai City Government for permission to call the eight Police Divisions the eight Branch Public Safety Bureaux.
In an interview, General Wen stated that alterations have been completed in the Public Safety Bureaux in Peiping, Tientsin, Tsingtao and Cantan, and that the new names will be used as soon as Mayor Wu Te-chen has authorized the alteration.

China Times and other local newspapers:

THE RENT REDUCTION MOVEMENT

A meeting of the Executive Committee of the Shanghai Rent Reduction Movement Committee took place at 2 p.m. yesterday. 15 persons including Wong Hong Hwei (王鸿辉), Chang I Zung (张一麐) and others were present.
The following resolutions were discussed and passed:-
1) That a letter be sent to the editor of the Sin Ya Pao (新夜报), an evening newspaper, demanding the name of the person who wrote an article in the paper stating that the rent reduction movement was unsuccessful.
2) That a reward of $500 be offered to anyone who can prove that the above allegation is true.
3) That a planning committee be authorized to assist the main committee and that Chien Lung Chang (钱龙章) and 14 others be elected to serve on the committee.

China Times and other local newspapers:

MINISTRIES OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INTERIOR TO DISCUSS THE DREDGING OF SOOCHOW CREEK

A joint meeting of the Ministries of Communications and Interior will be held next week at Nanking to discuss measures for the dredging of the Soochow Creek. The meeting will last four days. The Ministry of Communication has appointed Kuo Ting San (郭廷三), Chief of the Navigation Department and Taao Tse Yu (陶志虞), Chairman of the Yangtsze River Conservancy Board, representatives at the conference. All the steamship companies in this city have been notified to submit proposals.

Ta Mei Wan Pao dated May 7:

MEETING OF THE RENT REDUCTION MOVEMENT ACCELERATION
ASSOCIATION.

At a meeting held on May 6 by the Executive
Committee of the Rent Reduction Movement Acceleration
Association which was formed by various local shop-owners
associations, the following resolutions were passed:-
1. That a petition be submitted to the local Tangpu
and other political organs.
2. That another petition be submitted to the Shanghai
Chinese Chamber of Commerce and the latter be also requested
to launch a rent reduction movement.
3. That a letter be despatched to the Shanghai Rent
Reduction Movement Committee emphasizing our support to
the Movement.
4. That various shop-owners associations be informed
to notify their members to pay their house rentals in
accordance with the measures drawn up by the Shanghai Rent
Reduction Movement Committee and that in the event of the
landlords refusing to receive the reduced rate of rentals,
the money be kept in a certain bank.
5. That various shop-owners associations be notified
to form branches of the Rent Reduction Movement Acceleration
Association.
6. That King Chu-hsiang (金楚相), Chow Liang-ngoh
(丘良玉) and 3 others be elected members of the Standing
Committee.
7. That slogans be printed and distributed to various
shop-owners associations.
8. That this Association be disbanded as soon as the
reduction in house rentals has been affected.

Meeting of Nantao District Rent Reduction Movement
Committee

A meeting of the Nantao District Rent Reduction
Movement Committee took place yesterday. Sun Ching Tao
(沈錦濤) was in the chair. After discussion, the
following resolutions were passed:-
1) That permission be granted for the formation of a
rent reduction unit by the representatives of the street
union of the Western City.
2) That propaganda on the rent reduction movement be
broadcast from various radio stations.
3) That the Chinese Boyscout Headquarters be requested
to detail boyscouts over 15 years of age to lecture on the
rent reduction movement.
4) That tenants and sub-tenants who have not yet
organized rent reduction units be permitted to appeal for
assistance from the District Committee.
5) That permission be granted for the formation of a
unit of the District Committee by the tenants of the Yuan
Lung Li Alleyway (元龍里).

in rentals.

a meeting at which it was decided to hold a mass meeting
of citizens in the district.

THE PUBLIC HYGIENE MOVEMENT

With a view to drawing the attention of the public
to public hygiene during the summer, Dr. Lee Ding An,
Commissioner of Public Health of the Shanghai City
Government decided to hold a public hygiene movement
in June next.
At 2 p.m. yesterday, a meeting of the Preparatory
Committee for the movement took place at the Chinese
Y.M.C.A. Building on Szechuen Road. More than ten
persons representing the Bureau of Public Health, the
National Child Welfare Association, the Chinese Y.M.C.A.
and Y.W.C.A. attended.
The following resolutions were discussed and
passed:-
1) That the movement be held on the 11th and 12th,
the 18th and 19th, and the 25th and 26th of June.

On behalf of the tenants of the houses on Chang Ka Zah(張家宅), Dah Chi Road(大吉路), the local Rent Reduction Committee yesterday sent the following two letters to the Special District Court and the Nantao District Court:-

China Times and other local newspapers :

DISCONNECTION OF WATER SUPPLY

Following the disconnection of water supply to
the Bei Teh Li Alleyway (北德里) off Tatung Road,
negotiations were conducted by the tenants with the land-
lord and the Shanghai Waterworks Company, but proved
unsuccessful.
Yesterday Lawyer Wong Yee Koh (王義舸),
representing the tenants received a reply from the
Shanghai Waterworks Company. In addition to despatching
a letter refuting the statements made by the Shanghai
Waterworks Company the lawyer accompanied by several
representatives of the tenants called at the company.
They were received by the sub-manager, Mr. Walter. The
lawyer told him that the tenants would pay the water
charges and requested the company to connect the water
supply. The sub-manager, however, refused to accept
the payment unless the tenants agreed to the installation
of water meters.
The conference lasted several hours, but no
agreement was reached and both sides remained obdurate.
Before the delegates of the tenants left the
Company, they warned the latter that unless the Company
complied with the request for the re-connection of the
water supply, in accordance with the agreement concluded
with the Shanghai Municipal Council, the Company should
be held responsible for any incident resulting from the
disconnection.
The following is the gist of the reply from
the Shanghai Waterworks Company to Lawyer Wong Yee Koh:-
"In reply to your letter of the 27th regarding
the water supply to the houses in Sinza and Tatung Roads,
we have to inform you that the owner of the houses has
already signed a contract with us for the installation of
water meters.
"The articles quoted by you have nothing to do
with the case, because after the landlord has accepted
the terms and conditions of the Company, the payment
of water charges is no concern of his.
"Under the circumstances, we had to disconnect
the water supply. Please ask your clients to call on us
to discuss the matter."
Yesterday the Chief of the Press Information
Office of the S.M.C. sent a letter to newspaper offices
stating that the report published in yesterday's issue
concerning an interview between Lawyer Wong Yee Koh and
Mr. Jones, Secretary of the S.M.C., was inaccurate. Mr. Jones
did not side with the Waterworks Company neither did he
refuse to consider the request of the representative.
The letter added that Lawyer Wong did not interview
Mr. Jones.

停止供水

继大通路（Tatung Road）北德里（Bei Teh Li Alleyway）停止供水后，租户与房东及上海自来水公司进行了交涉，但证明 unsuccessful（未成功）。
昨日，代表租户的律师王义舸（Wong Yee Koh）收到上海自来水公司的回复。除发函驳斥上海自来水公司的说法外，该律师还在几名租户代表的陪同下拜访了该公司。
他们由副经理沃尔特（Walter）先生接待。律师告知他，租户愿意支付水费，并要求公司恢复供水。然而，副经理拒绝接受付款，除非租户同意安装水表。
会议持续数小时，但未达成协议，双方均坚持己见。
在租户代表离开公司前，他们警告后者，除非公司按照与上海工部局达成的协议满足恢复供水的请求，否则公司应对因断水引发的任何事件负责。
以下是上海自来水公司给律师王义舸的回复要点：
“就你方27日关于新闸路和大通路房屋供水的来信，我方须告知，房屋业主已与我方签署安装水表的合同。
‘你方引用的条款与本案无关，因为房东在接受我方的条款和条件后，水费的支付已与其无关。
‘在此情况下，我方不得不切断供水。请让你的客户来我司商讨此事。’”
昨日，工部局新闻处处长致函各报社，称昨日刊登的关于律师王义舸与工部局秘书琼斯（Jones）先生会谈的报道不实。琼斯先生既未偏袒自来水公司，也未拒绝考虑代表的请求。
信函补充说，王律师并未会见琼斯先生。

DISCONNECTION OF WATER SUPPLY TO BEI TEH LI ALLEYWAY.

With reference to the disconnection of water
supply to the Bei Teh Li ( 培德里 ) alleyway, off Sinza
Road, by the Shanghai Waterworks Company at the request
of the Catholic Mission, the owners, the tenants of the
alleyway called a meeting at which it was resolved to

Near the Bei Teh Li alleyway stands the Bei
Teh Girls School and owing to the inconveniences incurred

suspended studies for two days.
At a meeting held at 8 p.m. yesterday at the

Lawyer Wong Yien-kwoh ( 王咸穀 ), representing
the tenants of the Bei Teh Li alleyway, yesterday
despatched the following letter to the Chinese Ratepayers
Association and various other public bodies:-
"According to tenants of the Bei Teh Li alleyway,
off Sinza Road, the water supply has been provided for
many years by the Catholic Mission, the owners of the
property. Owing to high water rates in 1930, the tenants
agreed to an increase of $1. The owners have attempted
to increase the water charges by $5, but the tenants object.
"Without warning the tenants, the owners at
9 a.m. April 24 requested the Shanghai Waterworks Company
to disconnect the water supply to the Bei Teh Li alleyway.
"Upon enquiries at Sinza Station, the tenants
were informed that the disconnection was due to the non-
payment of house rentals, while at the Shanghai Waterworks
Company, they were told that this action was carried out
on the instructions of the owners.

and the Shanghai Waterworks Company on March 17, 1928,
either the landlord or the Shanghai Waterworks Company
is allowed to disconnect the water supply to houses.
"The water supply concerns the life of the people
and we hereby ask your Association to despatch a letter
to the S.M.C. requesting that the Shanghai Waterworks
Company be instructed to connect the water supply at once."

April 30, 1934. Afternoon Translation.

Chen Pao publishes the following comment:

RENT REDUCTION MOVEMENT.

Due to trade depression, local residents have requested landlords to reduce the rentals. The movement to reduce the rentals has not met with much success, but cases wherein landlords have forced the tenants to vacate their premises or increased the rentals have frequently occurred. We are surprised that the municipal authorities have not assisted the public.

The landlords of Bei Teh Li (培德里), Tatung Road, reported to be Catholics, have increased the water charges. The tenants oppose the increase and the water supply is now disconnected. This action has been sponsored by the Catholics who preach "righteousness" and "love." The lives of the tenants will be in danger if fire breaks out on the premises.

The landlords should at once restore the water supply to the tenants.

《申报》刊登如下评论：

减租运动。

由于商业萧条，本地居民已请求房东降低租金。减租运动并未取得多大成功，但房东强迫租户搬离或增加租金的情况却频繁发生。令我们惊讶的是，市政当局并未协助公众。

据报，大同路培德里（Bei Teh Li）的房东为天主教徒，他们提高了水费。租户反对涨价，目前供水已被切断。这一行动是由宣扬“正义”与“博爱”的天主教徒发起的。如果该处发生火灾，租户的生命将面临危险。

房东应立即恢复对租户的供水。

A ROUGH TRANSLATION OF THE PETITION MADE BY THE
HONG ZEU FUNG SUB-COMMITTEE OF THE RENT R.M.A.

The petitioners beg to bring to your notice the following
oppression adopted by the landlord, Phen Nyi Tai, of the Hong Zeu
alleyway off Ferry Road & Robison Road:-

The houses situated at the above address and the property
of Phen Nyi Tai, a well-known rice merchant, and are under the
management of the Probst, Hanbury (China) Ltd., Jinkee Road. Owing
to the comparatively high rate of rent imposed upon the tenants,
the latter therefore organized a "Rent-Reduction Sub-committee"
in order to request the land-lord to make a reduction of the
house rent. As a result of the financial embarrassment faced
by all the tenants, naturally some of them had to owe some three
months' rent to the land-lord, and as a consequence of which, the
latter, despite of the public opinion, had through the Court
detained the and sealed the properties, which is a very cruel
act. When the tenants rent the house, they furnished a guarantee
paper which guaranteed the tenants' financial possibilities. Now
the land-lord instead of acting through the proper channel, that
is to ask for the rent from the respective guarantor, had adopted
such a bitter measure. The land-lord was undoubtedly naturalized
by those imperialists and had therefore adopted the imperialist-
istic action. We hereby respectfully beg to request you, for the
spirit of the late Dr. Sun's "Three People's" doctrine, to
prevent the landlord from pressing the tenants any further." The
petition is herewith presented to you by our representatives
Yih Yuen Foong, Sze Sou Ying, Koo Kou Hsian & etc.
page_data.zh:
减租运动协会鸿寿坊小组委员会所提请愿书的粗略译文

请愿人谨提请阁下注意渡船路（Ferry Road）与罗宾森路（Robison Road）旁鸿寿坊（Hong Zeu alleyway）房东潘义泰（Phen Nyi Tai，音译）所采取的下列压迫行为：-

位于上述地址的房屋系著名米商潘义泰之财产，并由金基路（Jinkee Road）的Probst, Hanbury (China) Ltd.（普罗布斯特、汉伯里（中国）有限公司）管理。由于向租户征收的租金相对较高，租户因此组织了“减租小组委员会”，请求房东降低房租。由于所有租户均面临经济困难，自然有些人拖欠了房东约三个月的租金，因此，尽管舆论反对，房东仍通过法院扣押并查封了房产，此举极为残酷。租户在租房时提供了担保书，以保证其财务能力。如今，房东未通过正当渠道（即向各自担保人收取租金），反而采取了如此严厉的措施。该房东无疑已归化于那些帝国主义者，因而采取了帝国主义式的行动。我们谨此恳请阁下本着已故孙博士“三民主义”的精神，阻止房东进一步逼迫租户。”本请愿书由我们的代表叶云峰（Yih Yuen Foong）、施瘦影（Sze Sou Ying）、顾古香（Koo Kou Hsian）等人呈交阁下。

REPORT

Subject (in full) Rent Trouble at Se Wo Li, East Seward Road.

Made by and Forwarded by Detective Inspector Wardrop.

Sir,
At 11.30a.m. 20-3-34, a party of Judicial Police and 1st.
S.S.D. Court officials visited the Se Wo Li, East Seward Road,
and proceeded to seal up the furniture and household effects
of the tenants. Police were informed and attended to prevent
any disturbance.
It appears that the tenants of forty houses about seven months
ago commenced to agitate for a reduction of rent, and since then
have deposited the rent in the bank instead of paying the landlords
who are the Republic Land Investment Company, No. 21 Yuen Ling
Yuen Road. The landlords took action in the 1st. S.S.D. Court
for recovery of the rent, and recently obtained judgment for
three months rental.
In consequence of above judgment, an order was issued by the
Court attaching the household effects of the defaulting tenants
and restraining them from moving same until the rent was paid.
As a result of the Judicial Police carrying out the above order
in house Nos. 4, 6, 10, 13, 25, 40, 42 and 46, the tenants of
3, 7, 9 12, 14, 17, 22, 24, 32 and 44 paid up the rent outstanding
by them to the landlords representative who was present.
Judicial Police and Court representatives will again visit
the above alleyway on the morning of 21-3-34, to execute the order
on the remaining houses. The tenants representative and leading
actor in the agitation is a Chinese lawyer named Wong Chih S (王吉士)
who has an office at No. 3 Se Wo Li, East Seward Road.
I am, Sir,
R Wardrop,
D. I.

报告

主题（全称）：东熙华德路（East Seward Road）世和里（Se Wo Li）的租金纠纷。

撰写及呈报人：沃德罗普（Wardrop）侦探督察。

先生，
1934年3月20日上午11时30分，一队司法警察和第一特区地方法院官员前往东熙华德路世和里，着手查封租户的家具和家庭用品。警方接到通知后到场以防止任何骚乱。
据悉，约四十户房屋的租户在七个月前开始煽动减租，此后他们将租金存入银行，而非支付给房东，即源林园路21号的共和置业公司（Republic Land Investment Company）。房东在第一特区地方法院提起诉讼追讨租金，并于最近获得了三个月租金的判决。
鉴于上述判决，法院发布命令，扣押违约租户的家庭用品，并禁止其在付清租金前移动这些物品。由于司法警察在第4、6、10、13、25、40、42和46号房屋执行上述命令，第3、7、9、12、14、17、22、24、32和44号房屋的租户向在场的房东代表支付了拖欠的租金。
司法警察和法院代表将于1934年3月21日上午再次访问上述弄堂，对其余房屋执行命令。此次抗争活动的租户代表和主要发起者是一名名叫王吉士（Wong Chih S）的中国律师，他在东熙华德路世和里3号设有办事处。
此致，
R·沃德罗普，
侦探督察。

撰写人：莫伊尔（Moir）高级警司 呈报人：[签名]

先生，

减租运动委员会的一个分支办事处已由一名叫马思其（Moh Kyi S）的人在希常小学（Shee Zaung Primary School）开设，该校位于康纳脱路519弄9号（福源里弄堂）。该办事处于1934年3月6日正式开业，并在每户门外张贴了通常措辞的标语以及《减租指南》海报，译文如下：

“减租指南”。“减租期限：从中华民国二十三年（1934年）一月至中华民国二十六年（1937年）十二月”

“房屋租金减免幅度：
1. 1922年至1924年间建造的房屋，租金减免百分之十。
2. 1925年至1927年间建造的房屋，租金减免百分之二十。
3. 1928年至1930年间建造的房屋，租金减免百分之三十。
4. 1931年至1933年间建造的房屋，租金减免百分之四十。

1922年或之后出租的房屋，如果租户已经支付过增加的租金，也必须按照上述折扣比例对已支付的增加部分进行减免。

[签名]

REPORT
Subject (in full) Further Report Re organization of a new Branch Office of the Rent Reduction Movement Committee at Markham Li, Markham Road.
Made by D.S.I. O.I.F. Forwarded by Joseph J. Sharman
Sir,
An inauguration meeting of the Markham Li alleyway Rent Reduction Movement Committee was held at the Zee Yuen Garden, 168 Connaught Road between 2.30 p.m. and 3.30 p.m. on the 4/3/34, when a representative named Zung Kiu Foong(陳九峯) from the Shanghai Rent Reduction Movement Committee's Headquarters attended and presided over the meeting, at which the following resolutions were passed:-
1. That the rent in this alleyway be paid with a 20 per cent discount in accordance with general rules decided by the Headquarters.
2. That the unreasonable oppression by the landlord ordering the tenants of this alleyway to remove be opposed and ignored.
3. That no rent or water rate be paid before dissolution of these problems, all the rent and water rate due should be deposited in a reliable bank instead of paying them to the landlord, unless ordered by this committee.
120 persons attended this meeting, 9 men were then elected from amongst them as executive committees, their names follows-
1. Tsang Tuh Ling(鐘德林). 2. Ching Fuh Yeong(金德榮)
3. Wong Kai Shui (黃瑞書). 4. Tsang Tung Zai(張棟材)
5. Tsang Sau Zee (張少泉) 6. Lieu Sau Ching(刘少卿)
7. Chui Ts Bei(邱子培). 8. Lieu Hung Shuen(刘鴻勳)
9. Woo Chai Ziung(吳蔡祥).

报告
主题（全称）：关于在马格汉路马格汉里（Markham Road, Markham Li）组织减租运动委员会新分支办事处的进一步报告。
撰写人：O.I.F. 高级警司 呈报人：约瑟夫·J·沙曼（Joseph J. Sharman）
先生，
马格汉里弄堂减租运动委员会的成立大会于1934年3月4日下午2时30分至3时30分在康纳脱路168号芝园（Zee Yuen Garden）举行，上海减租运动委员会总部的代表陈九峯（Zung Kiu Foong）出席并主持会议，会上通过了以下决议：
1. 根据总部决定的一般规则，本弄堂的租金按八折支付。
2. 反对并无视房东命令本弄堂租户搬离的不合理压迫。
3. 在这些问题解决之前，不支付任何租金或水费，所有应付的租金和水费应存入可靠的银行，而不是支付给房东，除非本委员会另有命令。
120人出席了此次会议，从中选出9人组成执行委员会，名单如下：
1. 鐘德林 (Tsang Tuh Ling). 2. 金德榮 (Ching Fuh Yeong)
3. 黃瑞書 (Wong Kai Shui). 4. 張棟材 (Tsang Tung Zai)
5. 張少泉 (Tsang Sau Zee) 6. 刘少卿 (Lieu Sau Ching)
7. 邱子培 (Chui Ts Bei). 8. 刘鴻勳 (Lieu Hung Shuen)
9. 吳蔡祥 (Woo Chai Ziung).
（批注：奥洛夫补充 4月2日）
（签名：约瑟夫·J·沙曼） （签名：高级警司。）

REPORT
Date February 14, 1934.
Subject (in full) Arrest of two coolies posting bills on electric light poles.
Made by D.S.I. Crawford, Forwarded by Det. Inspr. Telfer,
Sir,
At 10.30 a.m. the 14/2/34, C.P.C.1136 found Zung Ping Tseu
(陳品舟) 35, native of Tsungming, residing 229 Woochang Road
and Koo Yoen Chang (顧遠章) 25, Tsungming of the same address,
both employed as tea-boys in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North
Honan Road, posting bills on electric light poles on the Minghong
Road and brought them to the Hongkew Station.
The bills referred to are of two kinds relating to the reduction
of rents and the oppression of the tenants (copies attached).
On being interrogated the two men were found to be tea boys
employed in the branch office of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce,
229 Woochang Road and they had been instructed by a clerk in the
head office of the Chamber in North Honan Road to paste the bills
on poles on the following roads; Tiendong, Minghong, Woochang and
Woosung Roads. The bills were given to them by the clerk at the
Chamber of Commerce, North Honan Road and for this work they
received no extra pay. The two coolies live on the premises of the
branch office at 229 Woochang Road and pay no rent.
The bills and paste were detained at the station and the two
coolies allowed to go at 11.30 a.m. after receiving a caution that
no bills should be pasted on electric light poles. They were also
instructed to inform a responsible person of the Chamber of Commerce
that the bills and paste would be returned provided he called at
Hongkew Station.
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
C. Crawford
D. S. I.
Senior Detective i/c.

报告
日期：1934年2月14日。
事由（全称）：逮捕两名在电灯杆上张贴标语的苦力。
呈报人：侦探副督察克劳福德（Crawford），经由侦探督察特尔弗（Telfer）转呈，
敬启者：
1934年2月14日上午10时30分，华籍警员编号1136发现陈品舟（Zung Ping Tseu），35岁，崇明籍，住吴昌路229号；以及顾远章（Koo Yoen Chang），25岁，崇明籍，住址同上。二人均受雇于北河南路中国总商会，担任茶役，当时正在明宏路（Minghong Road）的电灯杆上张贴标语，遂将其带至虹口巡捕房。
所述标语有两种，内容涉及减租及反对压迫租户（附副本）。
经讯问，查明该二人系吴昌路229号中国总商会分会的茶役，他们受北河南路商会总办事处一名职员的指示，将标语张贴于下列各路的电线杆上：天潼路、明宏路、吴昌路及吴淞路。标语由北河南路商会的职员交给他们，此项工作并未获得额外报酬。这两名苦力居住在吴昌路229号分会的 premises（处所/房产）内，免付租金。

Subject (in full) Agitation for Rent Reduction

Made by D.S. Moore Forwarded by （签名）

During the afternoon of February 14th, 1934, posters
purporting to emanate from the Shanghai Municipal Rent Reduction
Movement Committee were found pasted on shutters and doors of
closed business premises on Boundary Road. The following is a
translation of the contents of the posters.
1. To rehabilitate local business and to restore prosperity to
Shanghai, rentals must be reduced.
2. Measures Governing the Rent Reduction Period. From January
1934 to December 1937
a) Rent on houses constructed between 1922 and 1924 be paid at
90% of the present rate.
b) Rent on houses constructed between 1925 and 1927 be paid at
80% of the present rate.
c) Rent on houses constructed between 1928 and 1930 be paid at
70% of the present rate.
d) Rent on houses constructed between 1931 and 1933 be paid at
60% of the present rate.
e) In a case where a house was rented after 1922 and the rental
has been increased thereafter, the rate of reduction in rent to
be calculated according to the year when rent was increased.
3. To reduce rent in order to relieve the distress of the people.
4. In order to enforce the doctrine of livelihood, the rent should
first of all be reduced.

（签名） W. Moore

Political (3) June 27, 1932.

Shanghai Citizens Rent Reduction and Remission Movement
Committee - General Meeting

One hundred and thirty two Chinese claiming to represent
various local bodies attended a meeting convened by the
Shanghai Citizens Rent Reduction and Remission Movement Com-
mittee in the Zang Kung Primary School, 186 Burkill Road
at 3 p.m. June 26 and passed the following resolutions:
1. That the Shanghai Municipality be requested to promulgate
before the end of June measures for dealing with rent
reduction and remission.
2. That the Shanghai Municipality be requested to request
the Judicial Authorities not to hear any case regarding
the current rent dispute until these measures have been
promulgated.
3. That seven representatives be appointed to submit an appeal
to the Shanghai Municipality regarding the rent question.
4. That local various bodies be instructed to submit similar
appeals to the Municipality.
5. That a manifesto be issued advocating the necessity for
rent reduction and exemption.
6. That those tenants who have entered into agreement with
the landlords regarding rent reduction be entitled to the
same reduction and exemption as those who so far have not
done so.
7. That the local water companies be requested to continue the
supply of water to tenants irrespective of the application
of the landlords for discontinuance of supply as a counter
measure against the non-payment of rent.
8. That pending the promulgation of measures by the Municipality
the rentals be deposited in the banks.

During the meeting, copies of a handbill containing the
following resolutions passed at the 2nd Representative Meeting
held in the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association on April
29, 1932, and submitted to the Shanghai Municipality for
approval and promulgation were distributed among the attendance:
1. That the rent of houses in areas north of the Soochow Creek
be remitted for February, March and April, while the rent
question for May and subsequent months be decided in
accordance with the circumstances obtaining.
2. That the rents of houses in Nantao, Pootung and Western
District Extra-Settlement road areas be remitted for February
and March and that only 40% of the rent be paid for April
and until such time as normal conditions are restored.

政治类 (3) 1932年6月27日。

上海市民减租免租运动委员会 - 全体大会

一百三十二名声称代表各地方团体的华人，于6月26日下午3时，参加了由上海市民减租免租运动委员会在伯基路（Burkill Road）186号藏公小学召开的会议，并通过了以下决议：
1. 请上海市政府在六月底前颁布处理减租和免租的措施。
2. 请上海市政府要求司法当局在这些措施颁布之前，不予受理任何有关当前租金纠纷的案件。
3. 指派七名代表就租金问题向上海市政府提交请愿书。
4. 指示各地方团体向市政府提交类似的请愿书。
5. 发布宣言，倡导减租和免税的必要性。
6. 凡已与房东就减租达成协议的租户，应享有与迄今未达成协议者相同的减租和免租待遇。
7. 请本地自来水公司继续向租户供水，不论房东是否以停水作为对抗拒付租金的对策而申请停止供水。
8. 在市政府颁布相关措施之前，租金应存入银行。

会议期间，向与会者分发了一份传单副本，其中包含1932年4月29日在宁波同乡会举行的第二次代表会议上通过并提交上海市政府批准和颁布的以下决议：
1. 苏州河以北地区的房屋租金免除二月、三月和四月的租金，五月及以后月份的租金问题视具体情况而定。
2. 南市、浦东和西区越界筑路地区的房屋租金免除二月和三月的租金，四月直至恢复正常状况期间，仅支付40%的租金。

3. That the rents of houses in that part of the Settlement
south of the Soochow Creek and in French Concession be
exempted from payment for February and March and that
only 50% of the rent be paid for April and until such
time as normal conditions are restored.

4. That the rents of houses in Chanci, Chanju, Kiangwan,
Wusung and the areas north of the Boundary Gates of the
Settlement be totally remitted until such time as normal
conditions are restored.

5. That with the exception of the districts mentioned in
(1) and (4), charges for electricity and water etc.
for the period during which rent is remitted be paid
by the tenants and that the sub-tenants should also pay
the rates to the 1st tenants proportionately.

6. That the 1st tenants and the sub-tenants be entitled to
equal remission and/or reduction in rent.

7. That during the period of rent remission and reduction,
neither the estate owner nor the 1st tenants should ask
their sub-tenants to remove or increase the rental.

Zuan Foong Li, Kashing Road - tenants inaugurate a Union

A new body under the style of the "Zuan Foong Li
Tenants' Union" was inaugurated at a meeting held by some
50 persons at Lane 304, No.3 Kashing Road, between 3 and 5 p.m.
June 6. Besides the election of committee members to take
charge of the Union, the meeting was marked by the passing of
a resolution that the owners of the estate, the Shanghai
Investment Company, be asked to remit rent for three months
and to reduce the present rentals until normal conditions
are restored.

Federation of Kung Yue Li, Pah Tai Deu and Nyieh Sz Ka
(off Thorburn Road) Tenents - inaugurated

Some 20 members of the above mentioned federation held
a meeting in their office, No.33 Pah Tai Deu off Thorburn
Road, between 2 and 4 p.m. June 26, when the federation was
formally inaugurated. During the proceedings copies of a letter
addressed to the landlord of the houses in the above mentioned
three alleyways soliciting sympathy from and urging the land-
lord to remit rentals for three months, February, March and
April were distributed.

政治类 (4) 1932年6月27日。

3. 公共租界苏州河以南部分及法租界的房屋租金免除二月和三月的租金，四月直至恢复正常状况期间，仅支付50%的租金。

4. 闸北、真如、江湾、吴淞及公共租界边界门以北地区的房屋租金全部免除，直至恢复正常状况为止。

5. 除第(1)和第(4)项所述地区外，免租期间的电费和水费等费用由租户支付，二房东也应按比例向大房东支付费用。

6. 大房东和二房东有权获得同等的租金免除和/或减免。

7. 在免租和减租期间，业主和大房东均不得要求二房东搬离或增加租金。

嘉善路钻凤里 - 租户发起成立工会

6月6日下午3时至5时，约50人在嘉善路3号304弄举行会议，成立了名为“钻凤里租户联合会”的新团体。除了选举负责管理该联合会的委员外，会议还通过了一项决议，要求该物业业主上海置业公司（Shanghai Investment Company）免除三个月的租金，并在恢复正常状况之前降低现有租金。

孔悦里、白太德和聂家（托尔本路附近）租户联合会 - 成立

上述联合会的约20名成员于6月26日下午2时至4时，在托尔本路（Thorburn Road）附近白太德33号的办公室举行会议，正式成立了该联合会。会议期间，分发了致上述三个里弄房屋房东的信函副本，恳请房东同情并免除二月、三月和四月共三个月的租金。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

At 9.30.a.m. on the 3-7-32 the Complt accompanied by his shroff Yang Kai Shou of 5-44 Kyung Poh Lee, Avenue Road, came to the Station with reference to this case.

Yang Kai Shou was interrogated by the undersigned and C.I.D.35 and he corroborated the Complt's version of the affair, and in addition stated that a slight altercation occurred between the Complt and Liu Ng Tsan at the time the latter was acting as interpreter. The cause being a difference of opinion over the payment of rent for the months during which the Sino-Japanese hostilities were in progress.

However, since the shroff can speak fluent English, there appears no reason for the services of Liu Ng Tsan, being required.

The Complt still expressed his desire to charge the two accused persons inasmuch that he intends to take Court proceedings for an ejection order, and a conviction for assault against the two defendants would be favourable for his case.

C.P.C.181 who resides at Pah La Dou has been instructed to endeavour to effect the arrest of the two accused.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, February 20, 1936

Nanking Acts On
Rental Disputes

Investment Returns To
Be 12 Per Cent And
Mediation Provided

Seeking to minimize friction between landlords and tenants, the Executive Yuan in Nanking has promulgated a set of regulations requiring local governments to set up a standard for rentals, restricting the returns from realty investments to 12 per cent annually, and ordering that all rent disputes be heard by a mediation committee before the cases are sent to law courts.

The regulations, to be effective as soon as rules for enforcement are approved by the Government, are expected to bring far-reaching effects to both landlords and tenants. They contain 17 articles. Highlights of the regulations are:

Courts Not First Recourse:
No rental dispute should be sent to law courts until efforts of the mediation committee according to these regulations fail.

The local governments, considering the local conditions, shall fix a standard for rents and submit the same to the superior for approval. Any revision of the standard because of change in social economical conditions should also be submitted for approval. The standard should be so fixed that returns should not be more than 12 per cent annually from the investments on the land and construction cost.

In the event of disputes over rents, the mediation committee should be called within seven days after the filing of application.

Make-Up Of Committee
The mediation committee is to be formed by a representative from the local government, a representative from the local Kuomintang, a representative from local court and a representative from each of the parties.

In the event that mediation results in an agreement, the agreement should be written down and filed with the local government. When the mediation fails, the case is to be referred to the law court. The mediation committee is to forward the records of the case and to be informed of the decision given by the court.

Fine Provided
In the event one of the parties fails to carry out terms of the agreement, he will be fined a sum double the monthly rent. If the conflicting parties fail to ask mediation and directly file their cases before the law courts, the latter may proceed with the case after fining the parties a sum representing one month of rent.

The mediation committee is to collect no charges for its service.

All rent cases, still pending in court or outside the court, are to be dealt with under these regulations.

（批：File / 22 FEB. 1936）

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年2月20日，星期四

南京就租金纠纷采取行动

投资回报率定为12%并提供调解机制

为尽量减少房东与租户之间的摩擦，南京行政院颁布了一套法规，要求地方政府制定租金标准，将房地产投资的年回报率限制在12%，并命令所有租金纠纷在诉诸法院之前须由调解委员会审理。

这些法规一旦政府批准实施细则即刻生效，预计将对房东和租户产生深远影响。法规共包含17条。法规要点如下：

法院并非首选途径：
除非根据这些法规进行的调解努力失败，否则任何租金纠纷不得提交法院。

地方政府应考虑当地情况，确定租金标准，并报上级批准。因社会经济条件变化而对标准进行的任何修订，也应报请批准。标准的确定应使土地和建筑成本的投资年回报率不超过12%。

如发生租金纠纷，应在提出申请后七天内召集调解委员会。

委员会组成
调解委员会由地方政府代表、当地国民党代表、地方法院代表以及各方代表各一人组成。

如果调解达成协议，应将协议书面化并向当地政府备案。如果调解失败，案件将移交法院。调解委员会需移送案件记录，并获知法院作出的判决。

罚款规定
如果一方未能履行协议条款，将被处以相当于两个月租金的罚款。如果冲突双方未申请调解而直接向法院提起诉讼，法院可在对双方处以相当于一个月租金的罚款后受理案件。

调解委员会不收取服务费用。

所有仍在法院内或法院外待决的租金案件，均须依照这些法规处理。

（批注：归档 / 1936年2月22日）

MEDIATION BEFORE CASE
GOES TO COURT

A series of important regulations for the settlement of house rent disputes without bringing the matter to law courts were adopted by the Executive Yuan at a meeting on February 18. The main articles of the regulations are:

That, unless mediation fails after applying the following regulations, the matter shall not be brought to a law court.

That a standard house rent shall be fixed by the local government authorities according to local conditions. The highest standard house rent shall not be more than twelve per cent. of the yearly premium derived from the total value of land and buildings thereon.

That, when a dispute arises, at the request of either party, the local government authorities shall convene meetings of the mediation committee to bring about a settlement of the dispute within one week.

That the mediation committee shall be composed of representatives from the local government office, local Kuomintang office, local district court, and parties to the dispute.

That parties to the dispute shall nominate their delegates within one week after receiving a notice.

That during the period of mediation, the landlords shall not force their tenants to vacate the premises occupied by them.

That, when mediation is brought to a successful conclusion, a written statement shall be made out, signed by the parties to the dispute, and reported to the government office.

That this written statement shall be regarded as a contract between the parties to the dispute.

That, when mediation fails, due to the disagreement of either one party or both parties, and the dispute has been referred to a law court, all documents connected with the unsuccessful mediation shall be sent to the court concerned.

That, after a dispute has been settled through mediation, either party which has failed to observe, or carry out, the agreement entered into in this regard, is liable to a fine amounting to twice as much as the monthly rent for which dispute they have come for mediation. Landlords who force tenants to vacate premises during the period of mediation are liable to a similar fine. The local government office will ask the law court to execute the decision.

That no charges shall be made for the mediation of house rent disputes.

That house rent disputes, which have not been settled when the regulations are promulgated, shall be settled according to the provisions of the regulations.

房屋租金纠纷
法规

行政院通过一系列重要条款

案件诉诸法院前先行调解

行政院在2月18日的会议上通过了一系列旨在不经法院解决房屋租金纠纷的重要法规。法规主要条款如下：

除非适用以下法规后调解失败，否则事项不得提交法院。

地方政府当局应根据当地情况确定标准房屋租金。最高标准房屋租金不得超过土地及其上建筑物总价值所衍生的年度溢价的百分之十二。

发生纠纷时，应任何一方请求，地方政府当局应在一周内召开调解委员会会议，以促成纠纷解决。

调解委员会应由地方政府办事处、当地国民党办事处、当地地方法院以及纠纷各方的代表组成。

纠纷各方应在收到通知后一周内提名其代表。

在调解期间，房东不得强迫租户搬离其所占用的房屋。

调解成功达成结论时，应出具书面陈述，由纠纷各方签署，并向政府办事处报告。

该书面陈述应视为纠纷各方之间的合同。

如因一方或双方不同意导致调解失败，且纠纷已提交法院，所有与不成功调解相关的文件应送交有关法院。

纠纷经调解解决后，任何一方如未能遵守或履行就此达成的协议，须缴纳相当于其为调解而来之争议月租金两倍的罚款。在调解期间强迫租户搬离房屋的房东须缴纳类似罚款。地方政府办事处将请求法院执行该决定。

房屋租金纠纷调解不收取任何费用。

法规颁布时尚未解决的房屋租金纠纷，应按照法规规定予以解决。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 15, 1936

REDUCING RENTS

The general tendency of rents in Shanghai to fall has been apparent for some time. Advertisements in this journal have been eloquent on the subject. Landlords have sensed the difficulty of the situation and, in consequence, have voluntarily offered rent reductions. No landlord claims to be possessed of an extra white pair of wings on that account; still the fact deserves record, if only because some landlords have not followed suit. There are, however, people, who consider the moment opportune to apply what might be called a method of artificial perspiration to the brows of the landlords—generous and stingy alike. In a certain property in Shanghai the rents were reduced not long ago to the extent of about 21 per cent. by the spontaneous action of the landlords. The tenants seemed to be pleased. This contentment was disturbed by receipt of a circular from an outside philanthropist who expressed a fervent belief in the value of what he called "a united protest" as a means of securing further favours from the landlords. His calculations were not based on sound reasoning for they included the statement that "house-owners are not inclined to allow any reduction, as long as they are not requested or forced by their tenants". The particular tenants whom he thus addressed had had practical proof of the falsity of that statement, but some of them, on the principle of trying everything once, lent an ear to his suggestions. In the desperate search for unity the public-spirited "organizer" offered to draw up a petition for signature by all tenants. He ingeniously proceeded:

As it is rather difficult to unite all the tenants of these flats. I undertake to make out such a petition, signed by all the tenants, to hand this petition over to the houseowners, and in general to do everything to obtain the desired reduction.

For this arduous labour a small sum was demanded in advance for "expenses", and the balance—ten times that sum—was to come when "a successful reply" had been received. It is to be feared that this attempt to create another flourishing industry will not prove remunerative. Most tenants realize the benefit of keeping in direct touch with their landlords without the interference of outsiders. The incident shows the necessity for detecting the spurious from the real in handling the rent problem. Landowners and houseowners comprise gentry who may be slow to respond to the economic requirements of the moment, in a time of changing values, but taken as a whole they cannot afford to be neglectful of those considerations. In any event, for the sake of encouraging a quasi-benevolent third party to exercise his talent for the manufacture of "round robins", no tenant in his senses is going to antagonize a landlord who has voluntarily reduced rents by 21 per cent.

《字林西报》，1936年2月15日，星期六

降低租金

上海租金普遍下跌的趋势已显现一段时间。本报刊登的广告对此已有充分反映。房东们已察觉到局势的困难，因此主动提出减租。并无房东以此自诩拥有额外的洁白羽翼（意指自夸高尚）；尽管如此，这一事实仍值得记录，毕竟有些房东并未效仿。然而，有些人认为时机已到，可以对房东们——无论慷慨还是吝啬——采取一种可称为“人工催汗”的手段。在上海某处房产中，房东自发行动，将租金降低了约21%。租户们似乎感到满意。但这种满足感被一封来自外部“慈善家”的通告所打破，此人热烈信奉他所谓的“联合抗议”的价值，视其为从房东那里获取更多优惠的手段。他的计算并非基于合理的推理，因为其中声称：“只要租户不要求或强迫，房主就不倾向于允许任何减租。”他所针对的特定租户已有实际证据证明该说法的虚假性，但其中一些人本着“凡事试一次”的原则，听取了他的建议。在这位具有公共精神的“组织者”绝望地寻求团结的过程中，他提出起草一份请愿书，供所有租户签名。他巧妙地写道：

由于很难将这些公寓的所有租户联合起来，我承诺制作这样一份由所有租户签名的请愿书，将其交给房主，并总体上采取一切措施以获得预期的减租。

为此项艰巨劳动，他预先索取一小笔款项作为“费用”，余款——即该金额的十倍——将在收到“成功的答复”后支付。恐怕这种试图创造另一个繁荣行业的尝试并不会带来收益。大多数租户意识到，在没有外人干涉的情况下与房东保持直接接触的好处。这一事件表明，在处理租金问题时，有必要辨别真伪。地主和房主包括士绅阶层，在价值观变化的时期，他们可能对当前的经济需求反应迟缓，但总体而言，他们不能忽视这些考量。无论如何，为了鼓励一个 quasi-benevolent（准仁慈的）第三方施展其制造“联名信”的才能，任何神志正常的租户都不会去敌对一位已自愿减租21%的房东。

HARDOON SUES FOO
LOO ZOO
Nanking Road Shop Owes
Ten Months' Rent
The Foo Loo Zoo Restaurant, popular Chinese restaurant at 691 Nanking Road, was sued by its landlord, Messrs. S. A. Hardoon Co., in the First Special Court yesterday afternoon for the recovery of over $9,000, the total amount of ten months' house rent due to the plaintiffs.
The defendant shop asked for a rent reduction for one-third, namely, that its monthly rent be reduced from over $900 to a little over $600, the reasons given by them being that business was bad and other landlords had given similar reductions to their tenants.
The plaintiff declared that the fact that other landlords had given rent reductions to their tenants could not prove that the value of land had depreciated and that the fact that the defendant had paid several months' rent at the original rate after their lease contract had expired showed that they were willing to occupy their premises at the original rent rate.
Judgment was reserved till Saturday.

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, DECEMBER 1, 1935
Sensational Rent Reduction
Ruling In Shanghai
Will Highest Tribunal Sustain Judgment Of Court?
—Creation Of A Board Urged For Settling
Landlord-Tenant Disputes

By ARTHUR AND T
Recently, the Special District Court handed down a ruling that granted to the tenant-plaintiffs a 20 per cent. reduction in their rentals, retroactive to January 1 of this year. Irrespective as to whether this judgment will be sustained by the highest tribunal, the considerations involved are of immense interest. No doubt, the legal aspect will be the subject of much professional wrangling, but what of socio-economic guidance in this matter?
From the point of view of the owner, holder, or investor the Court's judgment is alarming and appears inequitable. How is it in the competency of the judiciary to interfere with price-fixing, which is automatically governed by supply and demand, is queried. Why should lessors submit to arbitrary ruling? And did the Court in issuing this judgment, reckon:
1.—That tenants may be taking unfair advantage of their landlords by organizing collective demands for reduced rentals when the rates charged may be moderate and not at all productive of a good return to investors;
2.—That the Court is unduly interfering with private rights;
3.—By its authoritative action, it weakens the lessor's fiscal position, which sets up a chain of effects leading to disastrous issue;
4.—That the decision is rather of an unprecedented nature, which, even if unstained finally, could cause, in the interim, serious consequences to the general body of land-holders dependent upon banks and financiers who would be disconcerted by the administrative intrusion and its implications;
5.—That the landlords suffer the risk of vacancy and are unable to obtain relief from the State;
6.—That owing to adverse conditions in obtaining in real estate, landlords are not in an advantageous position—it is a tenant's market—and the latter could seek premises suitable to their ideas of rental, the Court action thus adding momentum to an already descending movement, which, apart from appearing inequitable, is aggravating.
7.—That as no two pieces of property can be identical, the measure of warranted rental differs and the question whether a certain landlord is over-rating his premises or not depends on his individual case; a general ruling is not suitable, as its application would be more than fair in some cases and improper in others.
The above points are sufficient for practical purposes but are not exhaustive of the owner's case.

The Tenant's Angle
Taking up the tenant's angle, we have:
1.—That there is a great disproportion in his budget of rent to earnings—he feels that the product of his work goes mainly to landlords;
2.—During times of prosperity he pays increased rentals and why should this sixty outlive general declining conditions:
3.—Whilst there has been widespread fall in rentals, shifting his locale to lower-priced premises would not compensate for the loss he would incur by the transfer—it is not only a matter of initial removal expenditure to him but, as in the case of a professional or retail business, there would be a setback in the clientele built up and accustomed to frequent a certain locality; illustrative of this angle, we have the Wing On and Sincere Companies' emporium developments that not only served the existing large population in the neighbourhood but by reason of this presence drew to themselves a large customer trade, which, in turn, added considerably to the density of the district—their industry built up the neighbourhood almost as much as the environment developed them;
4.—That the tenant in the majority has small means which puts him at a disadvantage towards the landlord;
5.—The occupant, in the course of his tenancy, quite often prevents dilapidation of the property leased by him, even enhances its value through improvements put in at his own expense, and as fixtures revert to the owners if not otherwise stipulated, a removal to other quarters may entail considerable loss;
6.—Premises constitute a first necessity, and therefore, if exploited, would exert inordinate hardship—it should, he thinks, be regulated by the authorities;
7.—Landlords in general, it is averred, are taking advantage of the enhanced value of Settlement and Concession areas which, but for special protection and extrality privileges, would level down to that of the enveloping districts.
There are several other points which may be brought up but let us be content with an equal number for either party.

Socio-Economic Principles
It is not difficult for legal wits to advance arguments ad lib on contending sides, but what we are here concerned with is the reception and treatment to be given by the authorities to this matter. It is true that whilst another case in court met with a decision which was against tenants who pleaded rent reduction on the ground of the prevailing depression, yet the ferment on the question of rent reduction will not subside and the subject would have to be very seriously taken in hand by the State. The problem has hardly any precedent and, therefore, the authorities, in finally shaping out a "deal," would be greatly assisted by creating a "reference frame" or seeking guidance from fundamental socio-economic principles.
A cursory inspection of "backgrounds" shows that, in equity, the primary consideration is the axiomatic dictum of the greatest good of the greatest number. As a corollary, individual life must be subordinated, or rather made to harmonize with, collective existence. The civilized governments of the word have recognized that first necessities have to be made subject to regulation by the State. In the field of utilities, for instance, a municipal franchise contains restrictions upon profits and rates —profiteering tendencies are suppressed through articles and by-laws.

Monopolistic Factor
Applying these broad consideration to real estate—especially urban—it cannot be denied that land, being limited, tends to become monopolistic, as, at any one time, all the existing terrain is being owned by a group, and it is irrespective whether such group is made up of a few powerful magnates or by a great number of small holders. The point is that the condition for a monopoly exists. These ideas are not new and as far back as two centuries ago "the single tax" on the rent of land was debated by the famous group of French economists, known as the Physiocrats. The arguments of this school of thought were popularized, a hundred years later, first in America and then abroad, by the eminent American writer on economics, Henry Georges, whose unselfish devotion to economic and social questions attracted enormous popular feeling and respect. The basis of his doctrine was that the private ownership of land, like that of air and sunlight, is inequitable. Whilst the tax proposition which emerged was rejected by economists, a consensus of opinion recognizes that there should be measures aiming at the gradual state appropriation of future unearned increment of land, that is to say, the benefit in rising values created by the existence of a community should redound to the commonweal. In 1913 Lloyd George, then British Chancellor of the Exchequer, put forward a Land Reform Scheme that harmonized with modern aims, which tend to reduce the power of land monopoly. He proposed bringing the subject of its control and use under a Ministry of Lands. The incidence of the Great War prevented the development.
This should serve to indicate the modern world trend and attitude, especially towards land in cities, where continuous appreciation of values is due to communal usages and not to any merits of the possessors, who are responsible only for improvement which, of course, will be exempt from taxation.

A Nucleus For Reform
As far as Shanghai is concerned, these views are rather extreme, and it is not suggested that any attempt be made to introduce the application of reforms as conceived by the most advanced minds, which reforms have not yet been universally adopted. However, they would serve as a basis for the adoption of an attitude which would look with favour on the introduction of measures that could alleviate the genuine hardship experienced by the vast body of renters in general who find that in Shanghai the item of rental is out of all proportion to their total overhead.
The Chinese Government should take particular care to investigate the creation of a Board to whom all disputes between landlords and tenants, as regards rentals, can be referred. The Board should be constituted of duty-appointed representatives of land-owners, tenants, and delegates of the Government. Such personnel would be in a much better position to handle individual cases than a Court of Law.
As the Government is about to create a Mortgage Bank and relieve the situation by amending the auction law, it would be appropriate, concomitantly, to form a body or chamber to agree reasonableness and fairness in matters of rates of rental.
Without effecting a radical reform, the Chinese Government could thus enact measures in keeping with the inevitable future trend.

《上海星期时报》，1935年12月1日
轰动性的减租
上海之裁决
最高法庭会维持法院判决吗？
——敦促设立委员会以解决房东与租客纠纷

作者：ARTHUR AND T

近期，特区法院作出一项裁决，给予作为原告的租客百分之二十的租金减免，并追溯至今年1月1日生效。无论该判决是否会得到最高法庭的维持，其所涉及的考量因素均极具关注价值。毫无疑问，法律层面将成为专业人士激烈争辩的主题，但此事在社会经济指导方面又有何意义呢？

从业主、持有人或投资者的角度来看，法院的判决令人震惊，且似乎有失公平。有人质疑，司法机构何以有权干涉由供需关系自动调节的价格制定？房东为何要服从武断的裁决？法院在作出此判决时，是否考虑到：

1. 当收取的租金适中且完全不能为投资者带来良好回报时，租客可能会通过组织集体要求减租来不公平地利用其房东；
2. 法院过度干涉了私人权利；
3. 凭借其权威行动，削弱了出租人的财政状况，从而引发一系列导致灾难性后果的连锁反应；
4. 该判决性质颇为前所未有，即使最终未被推翻，在此期间也可能对依赖银行和金融家的广大土地持有者群体造成严重后果，因为这些金融界人士会对行政干预及其隐含意义感到不安；
5. 房东面临房屋空置的风险，且无法从国家获得救济；
6. 由于房地产处境不利，房东处于非优势地位——这是一个租客市场——后者可以寻求符合其租金预期的处所，法院的行动 thus（因此）为已经下行的趋势增添了动力，这不仅显得不公，更加剧了局势恶化。
7. 由于没有两处房产是完全相同的，合理租金的标准各不相同，某位房东是否对其房产估价过高取决于其个案；一般性的裁决并不适宜，因为其应用在某些情况下可能过于宽泛，而在其他情况下则不当。

以上几点足以满足实际目的，但并未穷尽业主方的所有理由。

租客的角度

从租客的角度来看，我们有：
1. 其预算中租金与收入的比例严重失调——他感觉自己的劳动成果主要流向了房东；
2. 在繁荣时期他支付了增加的租金，为何在普遍衰退的情况下这六十（注：原文如此，疑指某种比例或特定群体，此处照实译出）仍应存续：
3. 虽然租金普遍下降，但搬迁到低价处所并不能弥补因转移而遭受的损失——这不仅涉及初期的搬迁费用，而且对于专业人士或零售业务而言，还会导致已建立并习惯光顾某一特定地点的客户群受挫；说明这一角度的例子是永安公司和先施公司的商场发展，它们不仅服务于附近现有的大量人口，而且由于这种存在吸引了大量的顾客交易，这反过来又大大增加了该地区的人口密度——它们的产业几乎与环境发展它们一样多地构建了该社区；
4. 大多数租客财力微薄，这使他们在面对房东时处于劣势；
5.  occupant（居住者/租客）在租赁期间，往往防止了其租赁财产的破败，甚至通过自费进行的改良提升了其价值，并且除非另有规定，固定装置将归业主所有，因此搬迁到其他住处可能导致重大损失；
6. 住房构成第一必需品，因此，如果被剥削，将造成过度的困难——他认为，这应由当局进行监管；
7. 据称，总体而言，房东正在利用租界和公界区域价值的提升，若非受到特殊保护和治外法权特权的影响，这些区域的价值本应与周边地区持平。

还有其他几点可以提出，但让我们满足于双方各列同等数量的论点即可。

社会经济原则

法律界的聪明人不难在争论双方随意提出论点，但我们这里关心的是当局对此事的接受和处理方式。诚然，虽然另一起法庭案件作出了不利于以普遍萧条为由请求减租的租客的判决，但关于减租问题的动荡不会平息，国家必须非常严肃地着手处理这一主题。这个问题几乎没有先例，因此，当局在最终制定“交易方案”时，如果能创建一个“参考框架”或寻求基本社会经济原则的指导，将获得极大帮助。

粗略审视“背景”可知，在公平原则上，首要考虑的是“最大多数人的最大幸福”这一公理格言。作为推论，个人生活必须服从于，或者更确切地说，与集体存在相协调。世界上的文明政府已经认识到，第一必需品必须受制于国家的监管。例如，在公用事业领域，市政特许经营权包含对利润和费率的限制——通过章程和附则抑制牟取暴利的倾向。

垄断因素

将这些广泛的考量应用于房地产——尤其是城市房地产——不可否认的是，由于土地有限，倾向于形成垄断，因为在任何给定时间，所有现有土地均由一个群体拥有，无论该群体是由少数强大的巨头组成还是由众多小持有人组成，都无关紧要。关键在于垄断的条件是存在的。这些观点并不新鲜，早在两百年前，著名的法国经济学家群体，即重农学派，就辩论过对土地租金征收“单一税”。这一思想流派的论点在一百年后首先在美国，然后在国外，由杰出的美国经济学作家亨利·乔治（Henry Georges）普及开来，他对经济和社会问题的无私奉献吸引了巨大的公众情感和支持。他的学说基础是，土地的私人所有权，如同空气和阳光一样，是不公平的。虽然由此产生的税收提议被经济学家们拒绝，但舆论共识认为，应当采取措施旨在逐步由国家占有土地未来的非劳获增值，也就是说，由社区存在所创造的价值上升收益应归于公共利益。1913年，时任英国财政大臣的劳合·乔治（Lloyd George）提出了一项与现代目标相一致的土地改革方案，这些目标倾向于减少土地垄断的力量。他提议将土地的控制和使用事项置于土地部之下。第一次世界大战的爆发阻碍了这一发展。

这足以表明现代世界的趋势和态度，特别是针对城市土地，其价值的持续升值是由于公共使用所致，而非占有者的任何功绩，占有者仅对改良负责，而改良当然将免税。

改革的核心

就上海而言，这些观点相当极端，并非建议尝试引入由最先进思想家构思的改革应用，这些改革尚未被普遍采纳。然而，它们可以作为采取一种态度的基础，这种态度将有利于引入能够缓解广大租客群体所经历的真实困难的措施，这些租客发现上海的租金项目与其总开销完全不成比例。

中国政府应特别小心调查设立一个委员会，将所有关于租金的房东与租客之间的纠纷提交给该委员会。该委员会应由官方任命的业主代表、租客代表和政府代表组成。此类人员在处理个案方面比法院处于更有利的地位。

鉴于政府即将创建抵押银行并通过修订拍卖法来缓解局势，同时成立一个机构或商会以就租金费率的合理性和公平性达成一致将是适宜的。

在不进行激进改革的情况下，中国政府 thus（因此）可以颁布符合不可避免的未来趋势的措施。

REDUCTION

No Evidence to Show Estate Has Depreciated:
Area Not Affected by Order

The full text of the judgment in
e rent reduction action brought by
x Canton Road shop proprietors
gainst Tsung Teh Rental Agencv.
eir landlords, is now available. The
tion was recently dismissed by the
rst Special District Court's Civil
vision and a report has appeared in
e "North-China Daily News." Mr.
ao Wen-chi, attorney-at-law, re-
esented the tenants. while Dr. L.
Yang was the lawyer for the
ndlords. A translation of the judg-
ent follows.

Judgment

"The plaintiffs by their attorney
ked for judgment that (1) the
aintiffs be exempted from paying
vo months' rent on account of the
ostilities of January, 1932, amounting
$2,756.64 (2) the plaintiffs be per-
itted to reduce the rent to an
nount equal to 60 per cent of the
resent rate of rent from July 1. this

uced each month by the amount of

sts.

"The plaintiffs allege that Wu
hia-chu is now occupying the pre-
ises at 448 Canton Road and operat-

ong at the monthly rental of $262.24
he plaintiff Chang Chi-san is occupy-
ig the premises at 452 Canton Road
nd operating the Shun Cheng piece
oods hong at the monthly rental of
209.79; the plaintiff Chiu Hung-
ing is occupying the premises
434 Canton Road and operating the
Ho Tung Shoe Store at the month-
rental of $188.81; the plaintiff Ni
uan Yao is occupying the premises
435 Canton Road and operating the
Chong Kuan at the monthly rental
$188.81; the plaintiff Wang Ying
se is occupying the premises at 430
anton Road and operating the Hung
ah Shoe Store at the monthly rental
$188.81. That the plaintiffs have
een occupying the said premises for
ore than ten years; that during the
id period the rentals have been on
veral occasions increased on the
ound of prosperity of the market;
at the present rate of rental is
most twice as much as the original
ntal; that the plaintiffs have been
ffering from the oppression from
e capitalists; that in recent years
ere has been a general and serious
pression; that as rental could be
creased at prosperous times, it
ould be reduced at hard times.
at the value of real property in
anghai has depreciated which is a
ell known fact; that according to
w either party may apply to Court
r increase or reduction of rent as
e value of the real property should
crease or increase; that on these
ounds the plaintiffs ask for a re-
ction of rent.

Reductions Near By

"The plaintiffs also allege that the
her landlords of the neighbouring
operty have reduced the rent by
per cent. which are substantiated
the rent receipts; that the plain-
ts' demands are not without pre-
dent; that although the defendants
ntend that the plaintiffs may vacate
e premises if they should find the
ht too high, the plaintiffs have all
tablished business in the said pre-
ises and that so it is almost impos-
ole for them to vacate these pres-
ses. The plaintiffs also contend
at as the result of the hostilities in
anuary, 1932, they closed their busi-
ss; that according to custom and
e order by the Municipal Govern-
ent, the plaintiffs should be ex-
pted from paying two months' rent:
at the defendants have refused all
e demands of the plaintiffs and so
ey brought this action. The plain-
s produced four rent receipts, chit
oks and newspapers to substantiate
eir claims.

"Counsel for the defendants ask
d dismissal of the action with costs
d allege that the plaintiffs have
en their tenants of the said pro-
rty; that they have been paying
air rental at the present rate since
nuary 1. 1931 at which time re-
justment of the said rental was
reed upon; that there might have
en increases prior to the said time
if there were any, such increases
re made by the former owner in
ich the defendants took no part;
at at the time when the tenants
reed to continue the tenancy at
increased rate. there was a con-
ct from which neither party
uld withdraw without the consent
the other, that as the plaintiffs did
t and could not agree to the re-
ction requested, the plaintiffs can-
alter the terms of such tenancy
thout the consent of the defendants;
at as the plaintiffs are tenants on
nthly tenancy, they are always at
erty to terminate such by notice
d vacating the premises if they

t and unreasonable, that the de-
