THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JULY 1, 1932
4036
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. & S. B. REGISTER
D 3482
21/7/32

13 Tenants Sued By Algar
Company For Back Rent On
Shops Closed During War

Present Trial Likely
To Be Considered
"Test Case"

With the eyes of all landowners
and tenants in the city turned to
a "test" case pending in the First
District Court for a decision on the
dispute of war rentals which tenants
declare they should be exempted
from paying for the months of
February and March, the hearing
of the suit brought by Algar and
Company, agents for the Cathay
Land Company, against 13 of their
tenants opened yesterday morning.
After an eventful hearing during
which attorneys for both sides based
their contentions on different arti-
cles of the Chinese Civil Code,
Judge Yang Fang announced that
he would reserve judgment.

The case which involves 15 to 20
million dollars is considered by
landowners and house-agents as
well as tenants one of the most im-
portant legal battles of the year
as many minor differences between
landlords and tenants prevalent in
normal times can also be decided by
a decision of the court.

Rentals Retained

Practically every Chinese trader
in the city has retained the rentals
for February and March, asserting
that during the period of the Sino-
Japanese hostilities they have done
no business and their stores and
shops were closed following a gen-
eral strike proclaimed by the Chin-
ese Chamber of Commerce.

Algar and Company, represented
by A. M. Preston, vice-chairman of
the Shanghai Property Owners' As-
sociation, took the lead in bringing
civil action against the tenants
having named 13 traders doing
business at Chekiang and Peking
Roads behind Wing On and Com-
pany on Nanking Road as de-
fendants in this "test" case.

When the case opened yesterday
morning Mr. Preston for plaintiffs
handed the judge a map of the city
stating that it might be of interest
to the court to see where the
tenants' premises were located. The
houses were situated in the Central
District, he said, and was in the
most safest place in the entire city
during the local hostilities.

A Question Of Usage

"We have done our part and
proved the contract," attorney stat-
ed, "and the onus of proof is on
the defendants to show why they
should not pay their rent."

Replying for the tenants Mr.
Andrew C. Y. Law, well-known
local solicitor, said he based his case
on Article 441 of the Civil Code
which reads "A lessee cannot be
exempted from paying rent if the
lessee cannot make whole or full
use of the premises through his own
cause." Mr. Law argued that the
general strike proclaimed and clos-
ing of the tenants' premises doors
were not effected through their own
cause and the case should succeed
on this point.

It was possible that one or two of
the defendants' stores were opened
during the strike period, he said,
but only to serve those who were
in strict need. An hotel was open-
ed to accommodate refugees, he said,
and a drugstore also provided me-
dicines to the wounded, but in these
two cases the court should con-
sider them to have been legally
closed as they did not do business
with the general public.

Considered "Test Case"

In commencing his address Mr.
Preston, associated with Mr. Chen,
stated that the present proceedings
was a "test" case which was being
watched with the greatest of inter-
est by all landlords and tenants in
Shanghai. A legal decision would
decide the general dispute in all
areas and would be considered ex-
tremely important, he added.

Three articles in the Civil Code
provided his case, Mr. Preston de-
clared. Article 439 read, "The lessee
must pay the rent at the
agreed time or in the absence of
such agreed time according to cus-
tom; or in the absence of such
agreement or custom, the rent must
be paid at the termination of the
lease." Article 435, he said, reads,
"If in consequence of circumstances
that a lessee is not responsible
a thing leased is partially destroyed
during the continuance of the lease,
the lessee may ask for a reduction
of rent proportionate to the part
destroyed."

Closing Said Private Matter

The third article reads, "A lessee
of an agricultural land is entitled
to a reduction or exemption of the
rent if by reason of force majeure
the fruits of the thing leased de-
creased or totally failed."

The arguments for the defense.

Attorney Preston continued after
citing the above articles, "is that
because the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce had issued a proclama-
tion they were in fact prevented
from using their houses. Their
consent to close their premises
guided by the Chamber of Com-
merce was a private matter and in
no way concerns the legal issue.

"I would like to emphasise that
the tenants have not brought their
arguments within the four walls
of the Civil Code or have shown
any valid grounds why they should
be exempted from paying rent."

（批：Miles
1.7.32）

《大美晚报》，1932年7月1日，星期五

上海公共租界
C. & S. B. 登记簿
D 3482
32年7月21日

阿尔加公司起诉13名租户
追讨战争期间关闭店铺的
欠租

当前审判可能
被视为
“测试案例”

全市所有房东和租户的目光都聚焦于第一特区地方法院 pending 的一起“测试”案件，等待就租户声称应免除支付二月和三月租金的战时租金纠纷作出裁决。昨日早晨，汇业地产公司代理人阿尔加公司起诉其13名租户的案件开庭审理。经过一场充满波折的听证会，双方律师依据《中华民国民法典》的不同条款提出主张，杨芳法官宣布保留判决。

这起涉及1,500万至2,000万美元的案件被房东、房屋代理人以及租户视为今年最重要的法律战役之一，因为平时普遍存在的房东与租户之间的许多细微分歧，也可由法院的判决来决定。

**扣留租金**

本市几乎每家中国商人都扣留了二月和三月的租金，声称在中日敌对行动期间，他们未做生意，且在中国商会宣布总罢工后，他们的店铺关门停业。

由上海业主协会副主席A. M. Preston先生代表的阿尔加公司率先对租户提起民事诉讼，将13家在南京路永安公司背后、浙江路和北京路经商的商人列为本“测试案例”的被告。

案件昨日早晨开庭时，原告方Preston先生向法官递交了一份城市地图，称法院可能有兴趣了解租户 premises 的位置。他说，这些房屋位于中央区，在当地敌对行动期间是全市最安全的地方。

**使用问题**

“我们已经履行了义务并证明了合同，”律师陈述道，“举证责任在于被告，需说明为何不应支付租金。”

代表租户答辩的是当地著名律师罗安德先生（Mr. Andrew C. Y. Law），他说他的案件依据是《民法典》第441条，该条规定：“如果承租人因自身原因无法完全或充分使用房屋，不得免除租金支付义务。”罗先生辩称，宣布总罢工和租户关闭店门并非出于他们自身的原因，案件应在此点上胜诉。

他说，被告中可能有一两家商店在罢工期间开业，但仅是为了服务那些有迫切需求的人。他说，一家酒店开放以安置难民，一家药店也为伤者提供药品，但在这两种情况下，法院应视其为合法关闭，因为它们并未向公众开展业务。

**被视为“测试案例”**

Preston先生在开始发言时，与陈律师联合陈述，目前的诉讼是一起“测试案例”，受到上海所有房东和租户的最大关注。他补充说，一项法律判决将决定所有地区的普遍纠纷，并将被认为极其重要。

Preston先生宣称，有三条民法典条款支持他的案件。第439条规定：“承租人必须在约定的时间支付租金，若无约定时间，则依习惯支付；若无此约定或习惯，则须在租约终止时支付租金。”他说，第435条规定：“如果在租赁存续期间，因承租人不承担责任的情况导致租赁物部分毁损，承租人可以要求按毁损部分的比例减少租金。”

**停业属私人事务**

第三条规定：“如果因不可抗力导致租赁物的收益减少或完全丧失，农业用地的承租人有权减少或免除租金。”

辩方的论点。

Preston律师在引用上述条款后继续说道：“是因为中国商会发布了公告，他们实际上被阻止使用房屋。他们在商会指导下同意关闭场所属于私人事务，与法律问题毫无关系。

“我想强调，租户并未将其论点限定在《民法典》的范围内，也未出示任何有效理由说明为何应免除租金支付义务。”

（批注：Miles
1932年7月1日）

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 29, 1932

Judgment For
Tenant-Landlord
Battle Delayed

Fight To Get Rentals For
War Period Will Open
Next Week

The rent "test" case brought by Algar and Company, for the Cathay Land Company in the First District Court on May 21 against 13 of their tenants to decide whether the court would uphold or reject their declaration that no rents for the months of February and March should be paid to the landlords on account of the Sino-Japanese hostilities during that period when their businesses remained closed was brought under the spotlight again when hearing was set yesterday.

It is recalled that judgment was reserved at the last hearing by Judge Lur but an interlocutory judgment was sent to the attorneys in the case which held that there was insufficient evidence for the court to render a judgment either way and the case would have to be reopened and re-argued.

Asks Judgment

Yesterday morning the tenants were not represented before a new judge who presided and asked the court to adjourn the case until their counsel was prepared to defend them. Mr. A. M. Preston, representing the landlords, promptly asked for judgment in default and the judge read a petition he received from Mr. Andrew C. Y. Law, counsel for the tenants. The petition laid out the reasons why the case would have to be adjourned and the impossibility for judgment to be rendered on default.

According to the new laws promulgated which came into force on June 8, he held, the judge on hearing a litigation for the first time could not give judgment on default if no answer was filed to the petition. He further pointed out that he had not been served with a summons announcing the date for the hearing and had learned that a date had been fixed from his client. Judge Yang Pang subsequently adjourned the case one week.

The civil suit is an aftermath of a long dispute with foreign landlords and Chinese tenants regarding the payment of rental during the Sino-Japanese conflict. The tenants contend that they had done no business at all for two months as they had closed their shops following an order from the Chinese Chamber of Commerce that all Chinese shops and traders should cease doing business as a general protest to the unwarranted invasion of Japanese on Chinese soil and their subsequent destruction of homes and human lives.

Matter Of Grace

The landlords, on the other hand, hold that the tenants' premises were located at Chekiang and Pakhoi Roads behind the Wing On departmental store in the Central district and had been in no manner affected by the trouble in outlying districts. Mr. Preston said they refused to be intimidated by threatening letters they received and that it would be a matter of grace if the landlords would allow reduction of rental in certain individual cases.

The case is occupying the attention of all landowners in the city as a ruling on the issue will not only conclude the dispute but will be accepted as a precedent to be used in settling future disputes of the same nature.

It is understood that the Municipality of Greater Shanghai have asked Chinese tenants and landowners to submit petitions as to their contentions in the rent issue and that they will make an order after carefully studying the petitions with a view to effecting a compromise as arbitrators.

《字林西报》，1932年6月29日，星期三

房东与租客之争
判决延期

关于战时租金的诉讼
将于下周开庭

由阿尔加公司（Algar and Company）代表凯泰地产公司（Cathay Land Company）于5月21日在第一特区地方法院提起的租金“测试”案件再次成为焦点。该案起诉了13名租户，旨在裁定法院是支持还是驳回其声明，即鉴于中日敌对行动期间商铺停业，二月和三月的租金不应支付给房东。昨日已确定听证日期。

据悉，在上一轮听证中，卢尔法官（Judge Lur）保留了判决权，但向本案律师发出了一项中间判决，认为法院缺乏足够证据作出任何一方的判决，因此必须重新开庭并重新辩论。

要求判决

昨日上午，租户方未出庭，新任主审法官要求将案件休庭，直至其辩护律师准备好为他们辩护。代表房东的A. M. 普雷斯顿先生（Mr. A. M. Preston）随即要求作出缺席判决，法官宣读了他收到的租户代理律师安德鲁·C·Y·罗先生（Mr. Andrew C. Y. Law）提交的请愿书。请愿书阐述了案件必须休庭的理由，以及无法作出缺席判决的原因。

他指出，根据6月8日生效的新颁布法律，法官在首次审理诉讼时，如果未针对诉状提交答辩状，则不能作出缺席判决。他进一步指出，他本人并未收到宣布听证日期的传票，而是从他的当事人处得知已确定了日期。随后，杨邦法官（Judge Yang Pang）将案件休庭一周。

这起民事诉讼是外国房东与中国租户之间就中日冲突期间支付租金问题长期纠纷的后续。租户方主张，由于中国商会下令所有中国商店和商人停止营业，以普遍抗议日本对中国领土的无理入侵及其随后对家园和生命的破坏，他们在两个月内完全没有做生意，因此关闭了店铺。

出于恩惠之举

另一方面，房东方认为，租户的房屋位于中区永安百货公司背后的浙江路和北海路，丝毫未受到外围地区骚乱的影响。普雷斯顿先生表示，他们拒绝被收到的恐吓信所吓倒，并称如果房东在某些个别情况下允许减租，那将是出于恩惠。

此案正引起全市所有业主的关注，因为对此问题的裁决不仅将终结这一纠纷，还将作为先例被接受，用于解决未来同类性质的纠纷。

据悉，大上海市政府已要求中国租户和业主就其在租金问题上的主张提交请愿书，并将仔细研究这些请愿书，以便作为仲裁人达成妥协后发布命令。

（批：登记。请附卷宗。M.S. 1932年6月29日）
（批：长官，已附。R 1932年6月29日。）

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, JUNE 4, 1932

“Test” Case Over
Unpaid Rentals
To Be Reopened

Tenants Refused To Pay
Rents For March
And February

The “test” case brought by Algar
and Company against 13 of their
tenants occupying and trading in
premises at the corner of Chekiang
and Pakhoi roads in the First
District Court recently when the
latter refused to pay the rent for
the months of February and March
on account of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities during that period, will
be reopened in the civil division
and argued again.

Counsels for the landlord and
tenants, Mr. A. M. Preston and
Andrew C.Y. Law, respectively, have
been both informed of the decision
of the judge who at the last hear-
ing had reserved judgment to re-
try the case. No date has yet been
set.

The decision of the judge has an
important bearing, according to the
attorneys of both sides, as it will
not only definitely set a ruling re-
garding the payment of rental by
tenants who are withholding pay-
ment until judgment in the case
is handed down but also involves
the movement of 10 to 20 million
taels.

The argument of the landlord in
the case is that the tenants must
live up to the terms of the lease
and pay their monthly rental. The
plaintiffs hold that during the
troublous period the 13 tenants who
have been residing in houses in the
Central District have not been
affected in any way. The shops,
they say, were opened and the
defendants resided in the houses.

The defense set out by Mr. Law
was that the tenants had in accor-
dance with a request from the
Chamber of Commerce in protest
against the Japanese invasion closed
their shops for two months. It was
not a case where they themselves
agreed to discontinue their trade
but had followed a patriotic move-
ment arising from a public order.

《字林西报》，1932年6月4日，星期六

欠付租金的
“测试”案件
将重新开庭

租户拒绝支付
三月和
二月的租金

阿尔加公司（Algar and Company）近期在第一特区地方法院对其13名租户提起的“测试”案件将重新在民事庭开庭并进行辩论。这些租户占据并经营着浙江路与北海路拐角处的房产，因中日敌对行动期间的原因，拒绝支付二月和三月的租金。

房东和租户的代理律师分别为A. M. 普雷斯顿先生（Mr. A. M. Preston）和安德鲁·C·Y·罗先生（Andrew C.Y. Law），双方均已获知法官的决定。该法官在上一轮听证中保留了判决权，决定重审此案。目前尚未确定日期。

据双方律师称，法官的决定具有重要影响，因为它不仅将对那些在案件判决下达前扣留租金支付的租户之租金支付问题作出明确裁决，还涉及一千万至两千万两白银的资金流动。

本案中房东方的论点是，租户必须遵守租赁条款并支付每月租金。原告方认为，在动荡时期，居住在中区房屋内的13名租户未受到任何影响。他们说，店铺照常开业，被告也居住在房屋内。

罗先生提出的辩护理由是，租户应商会的要求，为抗议日本入侵而关闭店铺两个月。这并非他们自行同意停止贸易的情况，而是遵循源于公共命令的爱国运动。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, MAY 30, 1932

SHANGHAI RENTALS
REDUCTION
Mr. Wang Ching-Wei
Is Sympathetic
To Delegates

NANKING, May 29.—Mr.
Wang Ching-wei, president of the
Executive Yuan, expressed lively
sympathy for the reduction of
rentals in Shanghai in order to
mitigate the plight of the people
as a result of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities.
In a verbal reply to a deputa-
tion representing these organiza-
tions whom he received yesterday,
President Wang pointed out that
while at Nanking and Hangchow
rentals have been reduced as a
result of the war, it is only fair
that a similar procedure should be
observed at Shanghai, the scene
of most of the fighting.
Regarding the request that the
date of the general settlement of
yearly accounts for the 20th year
(which was postponed to the end
of the current month from last
December) be further delayed,
President Wang was also sympa-
thetic. However, in both matters
he counselled mutual forbearance
between those concerned and
advised that the questions be re-
ferred direct to Mayor Wu Teh-
chen so that a speedier solution
may be reached.—Kuo Min.

SI,
Passed by you & be attached to
appropriate file.

《上海泰晤士报》，1932年5月30日，星期一

上海租金
减免
汪精卫先生
对代表表示
同情

南京，5月29日电。——行政院院长汪精卫先生对上海减免租金以缓解因中日敌对行动导致的民众困境表示了热烈的同情。

在昨日接见代表这些组织的代表团时，汪院长口头答复指出，虽然南京和杭州因战争原因已减免租金，但在作为主要战场的上海，采取类似程序也是公平的。

关于将民国二十年年度账目总结算日期（去年12月已推迟至本月底）进一步延期的请求，汪院长也表示同情。然而，在这两件事上，他劝告有关各方相互克制，并建议将问题直接提交给吴铁城市长，以便更快达成解决方案。——《国民新闻》

Fifty members of the above association held a meeting
on May 14 at No.96 Peking Road between 3.30 and 6.30 p.m.
Mr. Kwei Yen Fong, Chariman of this association and also
a committee member of the Shanghai Property Owners
Association presided and the following resolutions were
passed :-

1. That the S.M.C. give an explanation as to why it has
approved without first consulting the consumers the
decision of the Shanghai Waterworks to collect the
water rate according to the meter reading, and the
S.M.C. be appraised of the disregard of the Waterworks
for the position of the estate owners and the welfare
of the people, in view of the Company's resolve to cut
off the water supply for non-payment.

2. That the rentals of houses north of the Soochow Creek
be reduced and remitted in proportion to the scale
determined by the S.M.C. for reduction and remission
of the Municipal rates, and the Waterworks, the Power
Company and the Council be asked to remit the water, and
electricity charges and land tax for those periods.

3. That all members refuse to sign contracts for water supply
according to the meter system.

4. That Estate owners be advised to construct artesian wells.

5. That the Waterworks be advised to adopt the following
measures in the event of the meter system being adopted.

A) The meter installation fees and deposits not to be the
responsibility of the estate owners.

B) The water rate at 6.25% of the rentals to be collected
from the tenants direct by the Waterworks.

The estate owners are rigorously pressing their
tenants for arrears of rents, and are attaining some results,
although the Eastern District remains a serious problem in
view of the continued refusal of tenants in this area to
pay any rents, which attitude is mainly attributable to the
activities of the various rent reduction and remission
Associations.

The case of Algar & Co. Estate agents versus 17
tenants of a block of buildings at the rear of the Wing
On Co. Nanking Road for non-payment of rents was heard at

中国地产业主协会关于租金问题的会议

上述协会的五十名成员于5月14日下午3点30分至6点30分在北京路96号举行会议。该协会主席兼上海业主协会委员桂燕芳先生（Mr. Kwei Yen Fong）主持会议，并通过以下决议：-

1. 工部局应解释为何在未事先咨询消费者的情况下，批准上海自来水公司按水表读数收取水费的决定；鉴于该公司决定对欠费者切断供水，应告知工部局自来水公司无视业主立场和人民福祉的情况。

2. 苏州河以北的房屋租金应按工部局确定的市政捐税减免比例进行减免，并要求自来水公司、电力公司和公董局免除相应期间的水费、电费和地税。

3. 所有会员拒绝签署按水表系统供水的合同。

4. 建议业主开凿自流井。

5. 建议自来水公司在采用水表系统的情况下采取以下措施。

A) 水表安装费和押金不由业主承担。

B) 按租金6.25%计算的水费由自来水公司直接向租户收取。

业主们正在严厉催促租户缴纳拖欠的租金，并取得了一些成果，尽管东区仍然是一个严重的问题，因为该地区的租户继续拒绝支付任何租金，这种态度主要归因于各种减租免租协会的活动。

阿尔加公司（Algar & Co.）房地产代理商诉南京路永安公司后方一栋建筑的17名租户欠付租金案，于

page_data.en:
- 2 -
2 p.m. May 19, 1932 at the Shanghai Special District Court
when the case was remanded for judgement on May 26 at
2 p.m. This case is regarded by the estate owners in the
nature of a test case, likely to reveal the attitude of
the Court in the matter of rent payments and the outcome
will undoubtedly be accepted by the majority of tenants.
Further action will be immediately commenced by the estate
owners in other cases should a favourable decision be
rendered by the Court.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
1932年5月19日下午2点在上海特区地方法院审理，案件被发回，定于5月26日下午2点宣判。此案被业主们视为一种测试性案件，可能会揭示法院在租金支付问题上的态度，其结果无疑将被大多数租户所接受。如果法院作出有利判决，业主们将立即在其他案件中采取进一步行动。

Shanghai Citizens' Rent Reduction and Remission Movement

of Commerce

At 11 a.m. May 18, three representatives of the

Committee, 251 Chefoo Road, called at the Chamber of

Tenants' Association of Ward Faung, Ward Road - Meeting

alley between 4 and 5.15 p.m. May 18 and decided that as

for April, the matter be reported to the Citizens'
Federation.

a union

A new tenants' union under the style of the "Hardoon
Tenants' Federation" was inaugurated at a meeting of some

18. The meeting was presided over by Long Ching-chi

80 Kiukiang Road, who is one of promoters of the new
organization in question. During the proceedings, an
executive committee of 11 persons was elected to take charge

上海市民减租免租运动委员会——向上海总商会提出诉求

5月18日上午11时，上海市民减租免租运动委员会（地址：芝罘路251号）的三名代表前往北河南路的上海总商会，就上海减租免租运动一事寻求协助。他们被告知，其请求将转交商会执行委员会审议。

华德路华德坊租户协会——会议

5月18日下午4时至5时15分，华德路华德坊租户协会的十二名成员在同弄堂51号的办事处举行会议，决定鉴于房东拒绝免除四月份租金，将此事项上报市民联合会。

已故哈同先生名下房产的租户发起成立工会

5月18日下午3时至4时20分，在西藏路80号的宁波同乡会举行了一次会议，约70名声称代表哈同先生名下房产租户的华人参加了会议，会上宣布成立名为“哈同租户联合会”的新租户组织。会议由九江路80号天宝斋药店老板郎經濟（Long Ching-chi）主持，他是该新组织的发起人之一。会议期间，选举产生了由11人组成的执行委员会负责

page_data.en:
- 2 -
of the new body and the following resolutions were passed:-
1. That the landlord be asked to adopt the solar calendar in collecting rents.
2. That the landlord be asked to remit the rents for February and March, and that at the same time the tenants be notified to pay their rents in arrears for months other than the above.
3. That a manifesto bearing on the inauguration of the organization be issued.
This new organization has established a temporary office in 323 East Kung Woo Li, Foochow Road.

Eastern District Rent Reduction & Remission Movement Committee
- Meeting
Some 40 Chinese claiming to represent various tenants in the Eastern District held a meeting under the auspices of the above-mentioned committee in its office, 20 Museum Road, between 3 and 6 p.m. May 18 when the following resolutions were passed :-
1. That in compliance with a request of the Kwang Ling Li (Rangoon Road) Tenants' Union, Mr. Liu Hung-shuin (劉洪勳), the Committee's legal advisor (20 Museum Road), be requested to write to the landlord of Kwang Ling Li, Rangoon Road, expressing opposition to his decision to increase the rentals and demanding the remission of 3 months' rent.
2. That every possible assistance be rendered to the newly inaugurated Soong Mur Li and Poo Ai Fang (Yangtszepoo Road) Tenants' Unions in connection with the rent reduction and remission movement.
3. That in connection with the dispute between the sub-tenants and the 1st tenants of the Poo Ai Fang, (Yangtszepoo Road) and Nankwei Road, the former persisting in the demand for rent reduction and remission, a letter be addressed to the parties concerned exhorting them to shelve their dispute pending the settlement of the question between the 1st tenants and the landlords.
4. That in connection with the notice of the Provisional Joint Office of Branch Associations of the Citizens' Federation in Hongkew District warning the Hongkew residents not to take heed of organizations other than the Joint Office interested in rent problems (Vide I.R. 16/5/32), investigations be made to whether the Joint Office considers this committee as being one of the other or outside organizations of whom no notice should be taken.
5. That posters bearing the Committee's resolutions that "Rents for February, March and April be remitted and 50% of the rents be paid from May and until such time as normal conditions are restored" be prepared for distribution and exhibition in the Eastern District.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
管理该新机构，并通过了以下决议：-
1. 要求房东在收取租金时采用阳历。
2. 要求房东免除二月和三月的租金，同时通知租户缴清除上述月份外的欠租。
3. 发布一份关于该组织成立的宣言。
该新组织已在福州路东公和里323号设立临时办事处。

东区减租免租运动委员会——会议

5月18日下午3时至6时，约40名声称代表东区各租户的华人在上述委员会位于博物馆路20号的办事处举行了会议，会上通过了以下决议：-
1. 应广陵里（仰高路）租户协会的要求，请该委员会法律顾问刘洪勳（Liu Hung-shuin，地址：博物馆路20号）致函仰高路广陵里的房东，对其加租决定表示反对，并要求免除三个月租金。
2. 就减租免租运动而言，向新成立的宋慕里和普爱坊（杨树浦路）租户协会提供一切可能的协助。
3. 鉴于普爱坊（杨树浦路）及南桂路次承租人与第一承租人之间的纠纷，前者坚持要求减租免租，特致函有关各方，劝告他们在第一承租人与房东之间的问题解决之前，搁置争议。
4. 鉴于市民联合会虹口区分会联合办事处发布通告，警告虹口居民不要理会除联合办事处以外其他关注租金问题的组织（见1932年5月16日情报报告），现调查联合办事处是否认为本委员会属于不应理会的其他或外部组织之一。
5. 制作印有本委员会决议的海报，即在“免除二、三、四月租金，从五月起直至恢复正常状况为止仅缴纳50%租金”的决议，并在东区进行分发和张贴。

25th District Branch (North Szechuen Road) of the Citizens'
Federation - Meeting

Twenty six members of the 25th District Branch of the
Citizens' Federation held a tiffin party in the Dah Chung
Hwa Restaurant, 453/4 Fokien Road between 12 noon and
2.30 p.m. May 16. Chang Yih-zung (張一宗), owner of
the Yung An Lee Confectionery Shop, 513 Nanking Road,
presided. The following resolutions were discussed
and passed :-

1. That the rents of houses in the district for February,
March, April and May be remitted and that only 50% of
the rents be paid from June until such time as normal
conditions are restored.

2. That this resolution be passed to the local Kuomintang
and Government Authorities for reference.

3. That in connection with the removal on April 27 of
about ten thousand dollars worth of furniture and
property from the Woo Kai-vung (胡開文) Chinese Pen
& Ink Shop, 457 North Szechuen Road (North of Boundary
Gate) by the landlord Chen Chung-zu (陳仲慈) through
the Land & Estate Office represented by A. Du Pac de
Marsoulies, due to non-payment of rent for the period
after January 18, and the leasing of the premises to
other interests, every possible assistance be given to
the manager of the Woo Kai-vung Shop in filing a lawsuit
against the alleged oppressors.

Meeting of Tenants Association of the Zai Kong Li, Zai
Ching Li and Zai Yue Li Alleyways, off East Kashing Road

At 9 a.m. May 15, about 100 Chinese who claim to be
tenants of the above mentioned alleyways held a meeting
in the Yangchow Theatre, in the Zai Yue Li alleyway of
Urga Road, O.O.L. to inaugurate the above association.
After some discussion the following resolutions were
passed :-

1. That the landlords be requested not to collect rent
for the past three months.

市民联合会第二十五区支部（北四川路）——会议

5月16日中午12时至下午2时30分，市民联合会第二十五区支部的二十六名成员在福建路453/4号的大中华酒楼举行午餐会。南京路513号永安利糖果店老板张一宗（Chang Yih-zung）主持会议。讨论并通过了以下决议：-

1. 免除该区房屋二、三、四、五月的租金，从六月起直至恢复正常状况为止，仅缴纳50%的租金。

2. 将此决议送交当地国民党及政府当局参考。

3. 鉴于房东陈仲慈（Chen Chung-zu）通过由A. Du Pac de Marsoulies代表的地产处，以未支付1月18日之后期间的租金为由，于4月27日将北四川路457号（界门以北）胡开文笔庄价值约一万美元的家具和财产搬走，并将房屋出租给其他方，现向胡开文笔庄经理提供一切可能的协助，以对所谓的压迫者提起诉讼。

东嘉善路载恭里、载庆里和载悦里弄堂租户协会会议

5月15日上午9时，约100名声称是上述弄堂租户的华人在欧尔路（Urga Road，原文如此）载悦里弄堂的扬州剧场举行会议，以成立上述协会。经过讨论，通过了以下决议：-

1. 要求房东不收取过去三个月的租金。

2. That the landlords be requested to charge the same rent
for red brick houses as charged for blue brick dwellings.
(Note: the rent for red brick houses is $35 and $32 per
month and that for blue brick houses is $34 per month).

3. That the payment of rent be shelved pending a reply to
the above two resolutions from the landlords.

The meeting terminated at 11 a.m.

2. 要求房东对红砖房收取与青砖住宅相同的租金。（注：红砖房月租金为35元和32元，青砖房月租金为34元）。

3. 在房东对上述两项决议作出答复之前，暂缓支付租金。

17th & 28th District Branches of the Citizens' Federation -
Meeting

Some 20 committee members of the 17th (North Szechuen
Road) and the 28th (Boone Road) District Branches of the
Citizens' Federation at a meeting held in 101 Chihli
Road, between 7 and 8 p.m. May 14 decided that they were
not satisfied with the Council's concession in the matter
of Rate remission and would ask the Chinese members of
the Council to fight for better concessions.

The meeting was presided over by Wang Chien-ngoeh
(王劍諤), committee member of the 17th District Branch
of the Citizens' Federation.

6th District Branch (East Seward Road) of the Citizens'
Federation - issues posters

On May 14, copies of a poster purporting to emanate
from the 6th District Branch of the Citizens' Federation
were found posted on East Seward Road. The poster
states that a unanimous resolution has been passed exempting
the payment of the February, March and April rents in the
district, and warns the residents not to take heed of other
organizations purporting to be interested in the rent
problem.

Copies of a handbill of a similar nature purporting
to emanate from the "Provisional Joint Office of Branch
Associations of the Citizens' Federation in Hongkew District"
were distributed to residents in Hongkew District on May 14.

5月14日晚7时至8时，市民联合会第十七区（北四川路）和第二十八区（百老汇路）支部的约20名委员在直隶路101号举行会议，决定他们对工部局在减免捐税问题上的让步不满意，并将要求工部局华董争取更好的让步条件。

市民联合会第六区支部（东熙华德路）——张贴海报

齐齐哈尔路太和里租户——反对支付四月租金

Shanghai Citizens' Rent Reduction and Remission Movement
Committee - Appeal to Chinese Authorities

Three representatives of the above mentioned
organization called at the local Kuomintang Headquarters,
West Gate, at 10.30 a.m. May 6 and submitted an appeal for

as resolved by the organization on April 28 (Vide I.R.29/4/32).

Provisional Joint Office of the Hongkew Citizens'
District Branch Associations - Meeting

Some 16 members of the above office at a meeting
held in their office, 207 Teh An Li, North Shansi Road,
between 3.10 and 5 p.m. May 6 decided that the rate in
the district be withheld till a reply is received
from the S.M.C. in settlement of the dispute, and the

MISCELLANEOUS.

Shun Pao:

HOUSE REMISSION CONFERENCE.

The Shanghai Citizens House Rent Remission Movement Committee held a meeting at 3 p.m. yesterday at which the following resolutions were passed:-
1. That representatives be detailed to submit appeals to the Kuomintang and the political organs.
2. That Wang Han Liang, Chen Yia Fu, Chen Pei Tuk and three others be elected to the Schemes Committees.
3. That the controversy between the landlord and the tenants of Hwa Tuk Terrace, Tsen Foong Le, Dong Ching Terrace, Yun Hwa Le, Si Hou Li, Dong Yu Li, and others, be settled by the Mediation Committee.
4. That assistance be rendered to the tenants of the Fu Hai and Loh Sian Terraces who are being oppressed by the landlords. three
5. That, with regard to the/measures for remission of house rents submitted by the Fu An Terrace tenants, the first be not discussed, the second be transmitted to the landlord and the third be held over.
With reference to the Yun Hwa Photo Studio case, the committee has sent a warning to the landlord.
The Rue du Marche and Broadway Road Tenants Federation held a meeting at 7 p.m. yesterday, at which a resolution was passed that the landlord be requested to remit the house rents for February, March and April; the remission after May will depend on developments in the local situation.
A responsible person of the Shanghai Real Estate Owners Association yesterday informed a reporter of the Kuo Min News Agency as follows that the Association has devised measures for a remission of house rent. The matter will depend on the action of the Municipal authorities in regard to the remission of the Municipal rate. If the S.M.C. remit the Municipal rate in the Hongkew district for spring quarter, then the house rent will also be remitted for that quarter.

Shanghai District Rent Reduction & Remission Movement
Committee - Meeting

Some 160 Chinese claiming to represent various
street unions, branches of the Citizens' Federation and
tenants' unions, held a meeting under the auspices of the
Shanghai District Rent Reduction & Remission Movement
Committee in the Ningpo Fellow Countrymen's Association,
80 Thibet Road, between 3 and 5.45 p.m. April 28. Yu
Hwa-loong (余華龍), a lawyer with an office at 2 Burkill
Road, presided. The following resolutions were discussed
and passed :-

1. That the rents of houses in areas north of the
Soochow Creek be remitted for February, March and
April, while the rent question for May and subsequent
months be decided in accordance with the circumstances
obtaining.

2. That the rents of houses in Nantao, Pootung and Western
District Extra-Settlement road areas be remitted for
February and March and that only 40% of the rent be
paid from April until such time as normal conditions are
restored.

3. That the rents of houses in that part of the Settlement
south of the Soochow Creek and in French Concession
be exempted from payment for February and March and
that only 50% of the rent be paid from April until
such time as normal conditions are restored.

4. That the rents of houses in Chapei, Chenju, Kiangwan,
Woosung and the areas north of the Boundary Gates of
the Settlement be totally remitted until such time
as normal conditions are restored.

5. That the 1st tenants and the sub-tenants be entitled
to equal remission and/or reduction in rent; but the
latter should pay the electricity and water rates to
the former proportionately.

6. That during the period of rent remission and reduction,
neither the estate owner nor the 1st tenant should ask
their sub-tenants to remove or increase the rent rate.

7. That in view of the fact that many estate owners are
inserting advertisements in the local press notifying
the tenants to register with them at a certain fixed
date under the pain of being ejected, various public
bodies be asked to chop and endorse a petition to be
submitted to the local Kuomintang and Government
Authorities for assistance.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, APRIL 21
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 3484
27. 4. 32

RATES AND RENTS
The attitude of many Chinese in the International Settlement in objecting to paying rates and rents is causing much concern, in the former case to the Municipal Council and in the latter to the property owners. Although there are a number of hard cases, which might be dealt with on their merits, the movement, as a whole, appears to be dominated by an obstructionist spirit and a desire to profit by unusual circumstances, fostered by various street unions and other organizations. The Municipal Council has now the matter of the rates and similar demands under its consideration and it is expected that within a few days some definite policy will be enunciated. With regard to the rent question, Mr. T. C. Britton, presiding at the annual meeting of the Shanghai Property Owners' Association on Monday evening, pointed out that it was a very difficult question on which to lay down any hard and fast rule, for each and every case put forward necessitated individual consideration. The Committee of the Association, he said, had given a great deal of thought to the matter and felt that consideration should be given to those tenants who were, to all intents and purposes, forced to evacuate for safety's sake the premises occupied by them. It was mentioned by Mr. Britton that it had been reported to the Committee that property owners were experiencing some difficulty in the collection of their rents in areas that were certainly not affected by the recent hostilities in so far as the safety of the inhabitants was concerned. The areas in question included the Central District, the Western and certain parts of the Eastern District of the International Settlement, also the French Concession, and the Committees certainly had no intention of advocating that any allowance be made to tenants in these parts of the town. In commenting upon the need for great care in dealing with applications for remittance of rent, Mr. Britton remarked that it had come to the Association's knowledge that many Chinese tenants who were not forced to evacuate for safety nor were in any immediate danger, arranged to let portions of their premises to refugees at lucrative rates. He was putting the matter mildly, for as a matter of fact, there have been outrageous profiteering on the part of many Chinese who, in spite of the losses of their fellow-countrymen, although some have shown kindness and charity to the poor refugees, have taken advantage of the situation to make money out of the distress of others. There have been a great many instances in which refugees have been charged exorbitant rents for the poorest accommodation and, when their money has gone, pushed into the street. It is to be emphatically hoped that persons who have been acting in such a manner towards refugees will not obtain a remission of rates from the Municipal Council or of rent from their superior landlords. As an example of what has been going on, we may say that in conversation with a well-known real estate compradore the other day, we were informed by this gentleman that many of the cheap "hotels," which formerly supplied "bed space" to the poor at ten cents and twenty cents a night, during the recent troubles put up their prices for this "accommodation" to as much as forty and fifty cents per night. In one case, of which we have knowledge, a shopkeeper who is the tenant of a shop and workshop on a ground floor and several floors of flats above (all sub-let) still rents every available space, however, diminutive, nightly to refugees. Business in his shop, he complains, is bad owing to the recent hostilities, but he makes light of the other "little profits."
There is no doubt that the majority of people in Shanghai are considerably the worse off for the happenings of the past few months and many have lost all their possessions and practically all their business, but we shall all have to take it in the best possible spirit and pull together so that recovery may be as rapid as possible. People who have suffered out of all proportion to others deserve our sympathy and should be given what practical assistance is possible. But this is a very different thing to giving a wholesale remission of rates and rents as some appear to expect. We sincerely hope that Chinese house-holders will turn deaf ears to foolish agitation and realize that if rates and rents are not paid promptly, the longer will be the time which Shanghai will take to recover from the recent disaster which has overtaken her and that it is to everybody's advantage to do his or her level best to meet their obligations as quickly and completely as possible. This is an essentially individual matter and there is no better form of co-operation than meeting one's dues without delay, even if it means sacrifice, for then all will be the gainer and the man or woman who is free from debt at this time of crisis is in a far better position to take advantage of the opportunities that will arise when the commercial life of the city returns to normal.

《字林西报》，4月21日，星期四
上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与特别股登记处。
编号 D 3484
1932年4月27日

捐税与租金

国际租界内许多华人拒缴捐税和租金的态度，引起了各方的高度关注：前者令工部局担忧，后者令业主担忧。尽管有一些困难个案可以视具体情况酌情处理，但总体而言，这场运动似乎受到一种阻挠精神和利用非常局势牟利欲望的支配，并得到了各类街道联合会及其他组织的煽动。工部局目前正在审议捐税及类似要求事宜，预计数日内将公布明确政策。关于租金问题，布里顿（T. C. Britton）先生周一晚在上海业主协会（Shanghai Property Owners' Association）年会上主持时指出，这是一个很难制定任何硬性规定的问题，因为提出的每一个案例都需要单独考量。他说，协会委员会已对此事给予了充分思考，认为应当体谅那些出于安全考虑而被迫撤离其所占房屋的租户。布里顿先生提到，据向委员会报告，业主们在某些区域的租金收取方面遇到了一些困难，而就居民安全而言，这些区域肯定未受近期战事影响。相关区域包括国际租界的中区、西区以及东区的部分地区，还包括法租界，委员会当然无意主张给予这些市区部分的租户任何减免。在评论处理租金减免申请需格外谨慎的必要性时，布里顿先生 remarked 称，协会获悉，许多并未因安全原因被迫撤离、也未面临任何直接危险的华人租户，安排将其房屋的部分空间以有利可图的价格出租给难民。他这还是说得含蓄了，事实上，许多华人进行了令人愤慨的投机倒把，尽管有些人对贫困难民表现出善意和慈善，但他们却利用局势从他人的苦难中牟利。有很多实例显示，难民为最简陋的住所被索取高昂租金，而当他们的钱花光后，便被赶至街头。我们要强烈希望，以这种方式对待难民的人，不会从工部局获得捐税减免，也不会从其上级房东那里获得租金减免。作为正在发生之事的例证，我们可以说，日前在与一位知名的房地产买办交谈时，这位先生告诉我们，许多以前每晚以一角和两角的价格向穷人提供“床位”的廉价“旅馆”，在近期的动荡中将这种“住宿”的价格提高到了每晚四角甚至五角。在我们所知的一个案例中，一名店主租下了一间位于底层的店铺和作坊，以及楼上的几层公寓（均转租），但他仍然每晚将每一个可用的空间，无论多么狭小，都出租给难民。他抱怨说，由于近期的战事，他店里的生意很差，但他对其他的“小利”却轻描淡写。

毫无疑问，上海的大多数人都因过去几个月的事件而境况大不如前，许多人失去了所有财产，实际上也失去了全部生意，但我们大家都必须以最好的精神面貌面对，团结一致，以便尽可能迅速地恢复。遭受不成比例痛苦的人值得我们的同情，应给予他们力所能及的实际援助。但这与一些人似乎期望的那样全面免除捐税和租金截然不同。我们真诚希望中国住户对愚蠢的煽动充耳不闻，并认识到，如果不及时缴纳捐税和租金，上海从近期遭遇的灾难中恢复所需的时间就越长，而尽快且尽可能地履行各自义务符合每个人的利益。这本质上是个人的事情，没有比毫不拖延地履行债务更好的合作形式了，即使这意味着牺牲，因为这样所有人都将受益，而在危机时刻无债一身轻的人，在城市商业生活恢复正常时，将处于更有利的地位来把握出现的机会。

on its own merits.

Mr. Britton, vice-president of the
association, took the chair yester-
day in the absence of Mr. N. L.
Sparke who is now on home leave.

The General Committee for the
ensuing year is composed of Messrs.
A. M. Preston, H. G. Robinson, H.
Sandor, K. Sasaki, R. E. Sargson,
E. Sigault, R. D. K. Silby, N. L.
Sparke, E. A. Sykes, F. M. Vanze-
burgh, W. R. Walter, G. J. Wilson,
A. W. Burkill, H. M. Cumine, M. O.
Dayles, K. Inouye, N. E. Kent, G. F.
King, Y. P. Kwei, A. Loonis, S. C.
McDonald, Y. Meyer, Cohn, Mor-
ris, and Baron Guillaume.

Mr. H. M. Spence proposed the
resolution favoring the adoption of
the committee named and Mr. J. C.
Petit seconded.

Following is the report as given
by Mr. Britton:

"Before dealing with the cash statement
I wish to express on behalf of the com-
mittee their very real appreciation of the
work done by your chairman, Mr. N. L.
Sparke during the past year. Mr. Sparke
left just recently on home leave and I can
assure you that his advice and assistance
have been of the utmost value and it is
sincerely hoped that on his return he will
continue to give his valued advice and ser-
vices to the association.

Balance of The Account

In dealing with the accounts you will
notice that at the close of the year there
was a credit balance with the Hongkong
& Shanghai Banking Corporation of Tls.
4,533.92 as compared with a credit balance
of Tls. 4,284.30 for the year ending De-
cember 31st, 1930. I think we may consider
this satisfactory as current subscriptions
collected are generally less than those of
1930 owing to the fact that during 1931
we were able to collect some outstanding
subscriptions. Our membership remains
practically the same. The expenses for
last year are unavoidably in excess of those
for the year 1930, but for income from all
sources amounting to Tls. 7,172.62 expendi-
ture.

During the past year several matters of
importance came before your committee and
I propose to give you a brief summary of
them. At last year's annual meeting, Mr.
Britton mentioned that the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council building rules were being
revised and suggested that a small com-
mittee of the association be elected to liaise
the sub-committee of the Engineering
Society in order that the joint committee
could confer with the Commissioner of
Public Works, thus obviating many difficul-
ties later. This committee has since been
appointed and a sub-committee was
appointed.

owners would be served best by resuming
the chopping of the official plans under
protest. I think I can say without fear
of contradiction that your committee's
views had a useful and beneficial effect
on the discussions and actions which fol-
lowed.

Your committee also had conferences
with representatives of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council regarding road surrender
endorsements on consular title deeds and
I am happy to say these conferences ter-
minated in a complete understanding
between both parties. You will readily see
that these questions needed very careful
study and necessitated our calling in legal
advice and I wish to thank our advisors
for the generous amount of time given to
our association.

Correct Phone Service

A member of the association requested
your committee to ascertain information on
the telephone service outside Settlement
and Concession limits, for there appeared
to be a great deal of difficulty in supplying
the demand of subscribers. Your committee,
after discussion this matter decided to
approach Mr. Gill of the Shanghai Tele-
phone Company, who very kindly consented
to attend a committee meeting in order to
answer to the best of his ability and ques-
tions that members might ask.

Mr. Gill in addition to answering ques-
tions very kindly gave your committee a
complete lay-out of the situation from the
time the Shanghai Telephone Company took
over from the previous company and made
thoroughly clear the whole position. I do
not propose to go into any detail but should
any member desire information on this
question will be please communicate or call
on the secretary who will post him as to
the position now obtaining.

Water Meters Discussed

The Shanghai Waterworks Company's
metering system has been discussed by
your committee during the year. The
introduction of this system of general metering
for water will involve radical changes in
water charges. High rent properties may
be expected to save on their rent and low rent
properties may be expected to have to pay
more. Difficulties there will be but this
Waterworks Company assures us of its
close co-operation and is confident that
these difficulties will be overcome.

Your committee has received communica-
tions from some members interested par-
ticularly in the difficulties caused by the
Shanghai situation, this change to the
water-rate system should be postponed. As
I have pointed out, however, if this is
expected to benefit only one class and not
others so late, I think the matter might
well be left to the incoming committee to
deal with.

Rent Changes Discussed

Before concluding I wish to refer briefly
to the changes we have experienced this
year. Although this does not concern the
body under review it is of very great im-
portance to property owners. Your
committee have had several requests for
information and advice on the question of
dealing with tenants in the areas affected
by the disturbances. You will realize that
this is a very difficult question to solve
as it involves hard and fast rules for
each and every case put forward meets
with particular circumstances.

Your committee has given a great deal
of thought to this matter should be
brought up so that you may have
their opinion in the press that this
matter should be dealt with by the
tenants themselves. It should not be
dealt with by the association as a whole.
It is a matter for each individual owner
to deal with his own tenants. The
association can only give advice and
assistance where possible.

《大美晚报》，1932年4月19日，星期二
协会反对除虹口以外任何地方的减租
上海业主团体在华懋饭店举行年会

布里顿（T. C. Britton）先生在昨日下午于华懋饭店举行的上海业主协会年会上发表的年度报告中，提请注意因中日敌对行动给业主带来的困难，他表示，关于给予租户任何减免的问题，应根据每个具体案例的是非曲直单独考量。

协会副主席布里顿先生昨日主持会议，主席斯帕克（N. L. Sparke）先生目前回国休假缺席。

下一年度的总委员会由以下先生组成：普雷斯顿（A. M. Preston）、罗宾逊（H. G. Robinson）、桑多尔（H. Sandor）、佐佐木（K. Sasaki）、萨格森（R. E. Sargson）、西戈特（E. Sigault）、西尔比（R. D. K. Silby）、斯帕克（N. L. Sparke）、赛克斯（E. A. Sykes）、范泽堡（F. M. Vanzeburgh）、沃尔特（W. R. Walter）、威尔逊（G. J. Wilson）、伯基尔（A. W. Burkill）、卡明（H. M. Cumine）、戴尔斯（M. O. Dayles）、井上（K. Inouye）、肯特（N. E. Kent）、金（G. F. King）、桂永清（Y. P. Kwei）、卢尼斯（A. Loonis）、麦克唐纳（S. C. McDonald）、迈耶（Y. Meyer）、科恩（Cohn）、莫里斯（Morris）以及纪尧姆男爵（Baron Guillaume）。

斯彭斯（H. M. Spence）先生提议通过上述委员会名单的决议，佩蒂（J. C. Petit）先生附议。

以下是布里顿先生所作的报告：

“在处理现金报表之前，我谨代表委员会对你们的主席斯帕克（N. L. Sparke）先生在过去一年中所做的工作表示由衷的感谢。斯帕克先生最近刚回国休假，我可以向各位保证，他的建议和帮助具有极高的价值，并真诚希望他回来后能继续为协会提供宝贵的建议和服务。

账户余额

在处理账目时，你们会注意到，年底时在汇丰银行（Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation）的贷方余额为规元4,533.92两，而截至1930年12月31日的年度贷方余额为规元4,284.30两。我认为我们可以对此感到满意，因为收集的当期会费通常少于1930年，这是由于我们在1931年能够收回一些拖欠的会费。我们的会员人数基本保持不变。去年的支出不可避免地超过了1930年的支出，但来自所有来源的收入总额为规元7,172.62两。

在过去的一年里，有几件重要事项提交给了你们的委员会，我打算对此作简要总结。在去年的年会上，布里顿先生提到工部局的建筑规则正在修订，并建议选举协会的一个小型委员会与工程学会的小组委员会联络，以便联合委员会能与工务局局长会晤，从而避免日后出现许多困难。该委员会此后已获任命，并设立了一个小组委员会。

通过抗议性地恢复官方图纸的盖章程序，业主们的利益将得到最好的维护。我想我可以毫无异议地说，你们委员会的观点对随后的讨论和行动产生了有益且积极的影响。

你们的委员会还与工部局代表就领事契据上的道路退让背书问题进行了会谈，我很高兴地说，这些会谈以双方达成完全谅解而告终。你们很容易看出，这些问题需要非常仔细的研究，并需要我们寻求法律建议，我要感谢我们的顾问为协会慷慨投入的大量时间。

电话服务更正

协会的一名成员请求你们的委员会查明租界和法租界范围以外的电话服务信息，因为在满足用户需求方面似乎存在很大困难。你们的委员会在讨论此事后，决定接触上海电话公司的吉尔（Gill）先生，他非常 kindly 同意出席委员会会议，尽其所能回答成员们可能提出的问题。

吉尔先生除了回答问题外，还非常 kindly 地向你们的委员会全面介绍了自上海电话公司从前一家公司接手以来的情况，并彻底澄清了整个局面。我不打算详述细节，但如果有任何成员希望了解此问题的信息，请与秘书联系或拜访秘书，秘书将告知目前的状况。

讨论水表

上海自来水公司的计量系统在今年已由你们的委员会进行了讨论。引入这种普遍的水表计量系统将涉及水费的根本性变化。高租金房产有望节省租金，而低租金房产则可能需要支付更多费用。虽然会有困难，但自来水公司向我们要保证其密切合作，并有信心克服这些困难。

你们的委员会收到了一些特别关注因上海局势造成困难的成员的来信，他们认为推迟这一水费制度的变更。然而，正如我所指出的，如果这仅预期使某一类人受益而非其他人，且为时已晚，我认为此事不妨留给新一届委员会处理。

讨论租金变动

在结束之前，我想简要提及我们今年经历的变动。虽然这与正在审议的机构无关，但对业主来说非常重要。你们的委员会收到了几份关于如何处理受动荡影响地区租户问题的信息和咨询请求。你们会意识到，这是一个很难解决的问题，因为它涉及硬性规定，而提出的每个案例都遇到特殊情况。

你们的委员会已对此事给予了充分思考，应在媒体上提出你们的意见，即此事应由租户自行处理。不应由整个协会来处理。这是每位业主与其各自租户之间的事务。协会只能在可能的情况下提供建议和协助。

上海公共租界工部局警务处

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, APRIL 24, 1932
REDUCTION OF RENTS
AND RATES
Views To Be Supported
By Collection Of
Evidence
HONGKEW MERCHANTS'
RESOLUTION
To enable representatives of the
Provincial Joint Office of the
Hongkew Branch Citizens' Asso-
ciation to negotiate with the
Shanghai Municipal Council, mem-
bers of the joint office have re-
solved to collect evidence to
support the view, that it is impos-
sible for Chinese merchants to
resume business in their district.
On Friday, 16 members of
the joint office conferred and in
addition to agreeing that evidence
be collected on the question of
business resumption, it was re-
solved that the matter of the reduc-
tion and remission in rates be
shelved, pending a reply from the
Chinese Ratepayers' Association.
In Hongkew recently there has
been a wave of resentment against
the payment of rates, taxes, and
licence fees of all descriptions. The
Shanghai Municipal Council has
already allowed some relief to
shopkeepers and others, who were
obviously affected by the war con-
ditions which prevailed in their
areas recently, but many of the
Chinese are dissatisfied with the
Council's proposals. An extensive
campaign is under way and the
shopkeepers are making a strong
effort to gain further concessions.
On Friday the several resolutions
were passed by the various Hong-
kew Branches of the Shanghai
Special District Citizens' Federa-
tion, and the street unions of
Yingziang, Ward, Soochow, Broad-
way, Seward, Yangtzepoo, Dixwell,
Urga, Kashing, Hanbury, East
Yuhang, Kaifeng, North Thibet,
Elgin, Cunningham, North Fukien,
North Shansi, North Kiangsi,
Tsepoo, Tiendong, Funteh, Woo-
sung, and Minghong Roads, at a
meeting in the afternoon.
This meeting also decided to
collect evidence to prove that busi-
ness cannot be resumed in the
Hongkew districts. When the
evidence has been compiled, a
protest will be lodged with the
Shanghai Municipal Council.
Another resolution was that the
question of house rent reduction
be postponed for the next four
months.
That the matter of the remis-
sion of municipal rates in the
Hongkew district be settled after
a reply has been received from the
Chinese Ratepayers' Association;
and that a protest be lodged
against the reduction of only two
months' rates made by Mr. Wu Sh
Tieh, acting head of the Nye
Ward Company, was also decided
by the meeting.

减免租金
及捐税
拟收集证据
以支持相关主张
虹口商人的决议
为使虹口支会市民协会联合办事处的代表能够与上海工部局进行谈判，该联合办事处的成员已决议收集证据，以支持“中国商人无法在其所在区域恢复营业”这一观点。
周五，联合办事处的16名成员举行会议，除同意就恢复营业问题收集证据外，还决议将减免及豁免捐税一事暂时搁置，待华人纳税会回复后再议。
近期，虹口地区掀起了一股反对缴纳各类捐税、税款及执照费的愤怒浪潮。上海工部局已对受近期该地区战事影响明显的店主及其他人士给予了一定程度的救济，但许多华人对工部局的提议并不满意。一场大规模的运动正在进行中，店主们正大力争取进一步的让步。
周五下午，在上海特别区市民联合会虹口各支会，以及引翔、华德、苏州、百老汇、西华德、杨树浦、狄思威、乌尔嘎、嘉兴、汉璧礼、东余杭、开封、北西藏、爱尔近、康脑脱、北福建、北山西、北江西、乍浦、天潼、福德、吴淞和明洪路等马路商界联合会的会议上，通过了多项决议。
此次会议还决定收集证据，以证明虹口地区无法恢复营业。证据汇编完成后，将向上海工部局提出抗议。
另一项决议是将房屋减租问题推迟四个月再议。
会议还决定，虹口地区市政捐税的豁免问题，须在收到华人纳税会的回复后再行解决；并决定对业广地产公司代理经理吴铁（Wu Sh Tieh，音译）先生仅减免两个月捐税的做法提出抗议。

pasted on every house to be visited on the doors. In addition,
pawn-shop proprietors have sent a letter to the Council
asking for exemption from payment of one quarter's licence
fees on the ground that business is bad. Other demands for

1932年4月23日，星期六

虹口商人
要求减免三个月租金

呈请房东免除二、三、四月租金

典当商亦大声疾呼豁免执照费

反对支付租金的抗议浪潮正在虹口及周边地区蔓延。继上海工部局决定在近期战事直接受影响地区普遍豁免捐税后，华人现在要求在这些地区减免三个月的租金。一份请求豁免的请愿书已在房东中传阅。印有相同内容的海报被张贴在每一户要拜访的人家的门上。此外，当铺业主已向工部局致函，以生意萧条为由，请求豁免一个季度的执照费。其他豁免要求也已送达工部局。

那些要求减免捐税、租金及执照费的人士提出的理由是，北区近期的骚乱导致商业萧条及既得损失。针对目前最严重受影响地区的租金豁免抗议活动，工部局面临着各区纳税人要求减免捐税的压力。减租抗议并不局限于受中日冲突直接影响的地区，在未直接遭受损失的地区也提出了此类要求。法租界及远离战场的其他地区也加入了这一运动。在未直接受骚乱影响的外围地区，抗议的重点更多在于减捐而非减租。但在北区，运动的目标明确为完全豁免。一些房地产公司和房东已宣布打算给予一定的减免，但发起当前抗议活动的……

District Branch Citizens' Associations, located at 207 Te An

existence as a result of a resolution passed at a joint meeting

Canton Road, on April 7 (Vide I.R. of April 8). While

APRIL 10, 1932
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
3482.
20/4/32.

Increasing Agitation
For Rental Reductions
And Rate Exemption

Council And Landlords Faced With Heavy Losses
As Tenants And Chinese Ratepayers
Refuse To Pay Amounts Owing

STREET UNIONS AND FEDERATIONS ARE
CHIEFLY CAUSE OF TROUBLE

Landlords in the Settlement and the Shanghai Municipal Council are faced with a difficult problem in the increasing agitation against the payment of rents and taxes by a large proportion of the Chinese community. Fostered by the various street unions and citizens federations in this city, tenants and Chinese ratepayers are refusing to pay the amounts owing prior to the outbreak of hostilities and insist upon big reductions in rentals. Claiming that they have suffered severe losses owing to the Sino-Japanese hostilities in this area, Chinese ratepayers in many instances have refused point-blank to pay rates for the current quarter and declare that they will not do so until the Japanese have withdrawn. The agitation is extending to other sections of the Chinese community and at a recent meeting of various Chinese bodies resolutions were carried calling upon tenants to seek exemption from the payment of certain items.

The agitation which is developing in such proportions that property owners are now busily devising ways and means for combatting it. Many large property owners have announced their willingness to forego rentals for the months of February and March, on condition that the arrears up to February 1 are paid. Some have even promised a slight reduction in rent, but those behind the agitation are exerting every effort to precipitate a crisis between landlords and tenants.

The opposition is definitely organized and is supported by the various street unions in different parts of the city. These bodies virtually act as dictators to residents in their own particular districts and their decisions are usually obeyed without question.

The agitation is particularly strong in the West Hongkew, North Hongkew and Hongkew Districts, where as a result of the recent fighting in the West Hongkew area certain residents are making the payment of the full rental impossible before the end of the present year. In the French Concession also there has been a considerable increase in rentals and consequently a withholding payment of the same.

Organized Opposition
Investigations made by the authorities show that the agitation is not confined to one section but has spread to all organizations and sections of the community. Various methods are being used to bring about a cessation of payment of rents and rates.

In some cases wholesale evictions have been attempted it appears, but the tenants may do as they please. The Municipal Council is faced with a similar problem. The refusal of Chinese ratepayers to pay

要求减租及
免税的抗议活动日益加剧

因租户及华人纳税人拒绝支付欠款
工部局与房东面临巨大损失

马路商界联合会及各团体是主要肇事者

随着大部分华人社群反对支付租金和税款的活动日益加剧，租界内的房东和上海工部局面临着一个棘手的问题。在各马路商界联合会及本市各市民团体的煽动下，租户和华人纳税人拒绝支付敌对行动爆发前的欠款，并坚持大幅降低租金。许多华人纳税人声称因该地区的中日敌对行动遭受了严重损失，断然拒绝支付本季度的捐税，并宣称在日本人撤走之前绝不付款。抗议活动正蔓延至华人社群的其他阶层，在最近一次各华人团体的会议上，通过了呼吁租户寻求豁免某些项目支付的决议。

抗议活动发展之势如此之大，以至于业主们正忙于 devising（策划）应对之策。许多大业主已宣布愿意免除二月和三月的租金，条件是付清截至2月1日的欠款。有些人甚至承诺略微减租，但抗议活动背后的推手正竭尽全力促使房东与租户之间爆发危机。

反对派是有组织的，并得到全市各地各马路商界联合会的支持。这些团体实际上在其各自辖区内对居民行使独裁权，其决定通常被无条件服从。

抗议活动在虹口西区、虹口北区和虹口区尤为强烈，由于近期虹口西区的战斗，某些居民使得在今年年底前全额支付租金成为不可能。在法租界，拒付租金的情况也有显著增加，从而导致租金被扣留。

有组织的反对
当局调查显示，抗议活动并不局限于某一区域，而是已蔓延至社会各界的各组织。人们正采用各种手段来停止支付租金和捐税。

在某些情况下，似乎曾尝试大规模驱逐租户，但租户们我行我素。工部局面临着类似的问题。华人纳税人拒绝支付

the amounts owing would appear
to be more serious than was form-
erly believed. Officials of the
Council admit that large numbers
of Chinese have definitely refused
to pay rates for the current quar-
ter, despite the fact that the
Council agreed to relieve them of
the burden of taxation for the
period of February and March.
This was especially applicable to
the Hongkew District where many
Chinese were forced to evacuate
and the majority of whom have
not since returned. But the Chin-
ese are demanding more. They in-
sist, in many instances, that they
will not pay until the Japanese
troops have withdrawn. Their at-
titude is tantamount to defiance.
In this respect they have the sup-
port of various Chinese public
bodies all of which declare that
rates should not be paid while the
Japanese forces remain in this
area. They claim that they were
paying for protection from the
Council which has not been given.
The contention is made that resid-
ents of the Hongkew District have
suffered enormous losses as the
result of the Japanese occupation
of that area.

All Over Shanghai
The agitation is spreading. Ap-
plications for exemption from the
payment of certain licence fees
have already been made by a num-
ber of organizations claiming to
represent groups of licensed prem-
ises. Even the handcart owners
have joined the movement and
there is no telling, at the present
moment, where it will end. The
Municipality of Greater Shanghai
is also affected. Applications for
exemption of tax payments have
been made to the civic body and
have been turned down. Proclam-

ations insisting upon payment
have been posted in various dis-
tricts in Nantao and other sur-
rounding areas. But this has not
brought much money into the
municipal coffers.

A similar agitation has been
started in the French Concession
which was the district of Shanghai
to suffer least in the recent up-
heaval. The House Rent Reduc-
tion and Exemption Committee in
the French Concession has sent a
letter to the French Consul-General
asking him to enforce the order
issued in 1930 restricting rentals.
It also demands that landlords be
prevented from evicting tenants
for non-payment of rents. It pro-
mises, however, that municipal
taxes and water and electricity
charges will be paid.

Committee Formed
The Municipality of Greater
Shanghai, in view of the increas-
ing agitation, for rent reductions
has decided to form a special com-
mittee to deal with the question.
Representatives are to be appoint-
ed to co-operate with various
Chinese bodies for the purpose of
examining individual applications
for reductions and exemptions.
These will be considered and
judged according to the extent of
the losses suffered by tenants dur-
ing the recent hostilities.

In the Settlement, landlords have
held conferences on the matter and
are at present devising means to
cope with the situation.

The position of the Shanghai
Municipal Council, however, is
occasioning considerable thought in
official quarters and it is believed
likely that definite steps may have
to be taken to cope with the con-
tinued refusal of large numbers
of Chinese to pay their rates.

欠款的情况似乎比原先认为的更为严重。工部局官员承认，大量华人已明确拒绝支付本季度的捐税，尽管工部局已同意免除他们二月和三月期间的税务负担。这种情况在虹口区尤为突出，许多华人被迫撤离，且大多数人至今未回。但华人要求更多。在许多情况下，他们坚持在日本军队撤走之前不付款。他们的态度无异于挑衅。在这方面，他们得到了各华人公共团体的支持，这些团体均宣称只要日军留驻该地区，就不应缴纳捐税。他们声称，向工部局缴税是为了获得保护，但这种保护并未提供。有人辩称，由于日军占领该地区，虹口区居民遭受了巨大损失。

遍及上海
抗议活动正在蔓延。一些声称代表持照场所群体的组织已提出豁免某些执照费的申请。甚至连黄包车夫也加入了这场运动，目前尚不知其结局如何。大上海市政府也受到影响。已向该市政机构提出免税申请，但被驳回。南市及周边各区域已张贴坚持要求缴款的告示。但这并未给市政金库带来多少收入。

法租界也发起了类似的抗议活动，该地区是上海在近期动荡中受损最小的区域。法租界减租免税委员会已向法国总领事致函，要求其执行1930年发布的限制租金的命令。该委员会还要求禁止房东因欠租而驱逐租户。不过，该委员会承诺将缴纳市政税及水电费。

成立委员会
鉴于减租抗议活动日益加剧，大上海市政府决定成立一个特别委员会来处理此事。将任命代表与各华人团体合作，审查个别减租及豁免申请。这些申请将根据租户在近期敌对行动中遭受损失的程度进行审议和裁定。

在租界内，房东们已就此举行会议，目前正在策划应对局势的手段。

然而，上海工部局的处境令官方部门深感忧虑，人们认为可能必须采取明确措施，以应对大量华人持续拒绝缴纳捐税的局面。

Shanghai Citizens' Rent Reduction & Exemption Movement
Committee - Meeting

Fourteen members of the abovementioned committee
held a meeting in their office, 101 Chihli Road, between
6.20 and 7.50>p.m. April 8, and passed the following
resolutions :-

1. That five representatives be sent to the Social Bureau
to submit views in writing on rent reduction and
exemption.

2. That a circular be issued to local bodies requesting
them to submit before April 14 the names of their
two representatives who will attend a general meeting
to be-convened by the Committee in the near future.

上海市民减租免租运动委员会——会议

上述委员会的十四名成员于4月8日下午6时20分至7时50分，在直隶路101号该会办事处举行会议，并通过以下决议：

1. 派遣五名代表前往社会局，就减租及免租事宜提交书面意见。

2. 向各地方团体发出通函，要求其于4月14日前报送两名代表的姓名，以便参加本委员会近期召开的全体大会。

Shanghai Citizens' Rent Reduction and Exemption Movement
Committee - Meeting

Some eight members of the above-mentioned committee
held a meeting in their office, 1st floor, 101 Chihli Road,
between 6.30 and 7.20 p.m. April 5 and passed the
following resolutions :-

1. That a formal letter be delivered to estate owners,
requesting them to grant reduction or exemption of rent.

2. That a letter be sent to the "Rent Reduction & Exemption
Committee of Various Organizations in the French Concession",
welcoming the three representatives appointed by the former
to join the committee in the Settlement.

上海市民减租免租运动委员会——会议

上述委员会约八名成员于4月5日下午6时30分至7时20分，在直隶路101号一楼该会办事处举行会议，并通过以下决议：

1. 向房产业主递交正式信函，请求其给予减租或免租。

2. 致函“法租界各团体减租免租委员会”，欢迎该委员会指派的三名代表加入公共租界内的本委员会。

The people of the favoured classes are always 
cunning, and can deal effectively with any movement 
which affects their interests. For instance, the 
recent rent reduction movement has spread throughout 
Shanghai; those who possess estates feel that their 
interests are at stake, and immediately, they begin 

to pretect their interests, uspending the construction 
of new houses, thereby endangering the livelihood of 
300,000 workers. These workers Will naturally be 
utilized to opnose the rent reduction movement, and 
the Rent Reduction Movement Committee is faced with 

a difficult problem. A&A dispute has now arisen between 
the workers whose employment is threatened and the 
Rent Reduction Committee, and the real estate owners 
have withdrawn from the "battle-field". 

Hoping to settle this dispute for the welfare 
of the citizens, we, the spectators, express the 
following opinions- & ‘ 

It is common knowledge that the house rent in 
Shenghai is higher than in other parts of. the country; 
and it is also a fact that the livelihood ef Local 
citizens has been seriously affected by the world 
economic depression and the Shanghai Sino-Japanese 
hostilities. Hence, the rent reduction movement 
receives general approval. For the sake of the 
future of our three million local citizens, the 
movement must coytinue. But, ignoring the general 
situation, the local house owners have dexterously 
ised the masons and carpenters to oppose the movement. 

At present, the most suitable measure to solve 
this problem is to petition the City Government to 
prevent the house owners from suspending construction 
work, and the masons labour unions should be urged 
and assisted by society to fight against the 
suspension of work instead of against the rent reduction 
movement. . :

ia at Owing to trade depresston, high house

increased. In Shanghai, house rents have been increased

tenants pay for the price of the land by increasing the 
house rents.

construction of houses. It is also hoped that the 
various public organizations will “support the house 
rent reduction movements.

ai RENT REDUCTION MOVEMENT 


P Owing to trade depression, various public 
organizetions have combined to launch a tent reduction 


“movement. For this purpose, a rent reduction movement 


committee has been formed and a series of principles drawn 
up to guide the negotiations for the reduction. In this 
connection, the writer has something to say about the 


movemente 


Natural calamities and civil warfare have 
brought about bankruptcy in rural China, 411 the money 
from the interior has been transported to large commercial 
centres and many unemployed people have flocked to these 
centres to seek a living. These migrations have accounted 
for the increase in the population of Shanghai and the 
development in the banking enterprise. 

In countries where industries and commercial 
undertakings have been developed, the money would be employed 
for improvements, but in-China, a country financially back- 
ward, the situation is different, for most of the surplus 
funds are speculated in land investments. The only thing 
that has resulted from these investments is the erection of 
large buildings in the commercial centres, while the people 
of rural China are being oppressed. 

So much for the people of the rural country. 
But what about the life_of city dwellers? In Shanghai, in 
contrast to the development in land investment, prices are 
on the decline and the purchasing power of the people has 
decreased. The rents should be reduced, but on the contrary 
they are increased. The greater the increase in rents, the 
less will be the purchasing power of the people. If this 
state of affairs continues, the situation will become more 
serious. Therefore, the rent reduction movement is necessary 
from the standpoint of the living of the people and the 
development of industry and commerce. 

Se oe Ms According to the statements made-by Mr.Kwei Ye 

Bong (-$ 32. ), member of the Standing Committee of the 
Shanghai Héuse Owners Association, 90, of the houses in ; 
Shanghai are owned by land investment companies and most of 
the property has been mortgaged to banks. He said that if 
the tenants wished _to reduce the rents, the investment 
companies would demand from the banks a reduction in interest 
to compensate for their loss. Thus we know that all these 
land investments are under the control of the banks. It is 
unreasonable for the banks to oppose the demand of the people 
for a reduction in rents as being prejudicial to their 
interests. 

We would advise the banking circles to show 
sympathy with the people in the rent reduction movement and to ' 
sacrifice some of their profits for the benefit of the people.

Shanghai is the centre of industry and commerce 
of China and the city is densely populated. Increases in

accordance with the prosperity of the residents. The . 
movement recently promited by various local public podies

depression and to maintain business merchants have reduced 
the prices of all purducts. The house rents, however, 
still remain high. A reduction in house rents is 
essential. 

House rents here are extremely high and even a 
very small room in the International Settlement or the 
French Concession costs at least $5 or $6 per month. 
People whose income is small suffer great hardships and 
the interests of these poor people must be carefully 
considered. The rent reduction movement will become 
more powerful and success will be attained if the poor 
residents join in the struggle. 

Residents throughout Shanghai should be urged 
to participate in the recent rent reduction movement and 
district representatives should be appointed to carry out 
the work. An appeal should first be made to the Chinese 
and the Settlement authorities and then definite steps 
should be taken to ensure the success of the movement.
